titre: TypeORM based Database Migration
description:
Regarding SQL schema database migrations, it was first suggested to run the migration on application startup, however this can be problematic if application is running on several replicas since several migrations can run concurrently.

Suggestion:

  1. Roll migrations as a container app job
  2. In the service's container app, setup an init container so that app is launched only when migrations are completed
  3. the container image for the migration job is the same as for the app but will be executed with a command override
  4. Migration Job Is triggered by mesx-infra pipeline in prod and by services pipeline in dev/ppr
Job based migration example:
https://andrewlock.net/deploying-asp-net-core-applications-to-kubernetes-part-8-running-database-migrations-using-jobs-and-init-containers/

description:
The app proxy based on traefik used in MES X.0 is configured to expose all http api endpoint outside of the container app environment.

MES X.0 is composed of external apis, ui projects and internal apis:
  • External
    • Use Case Backends (picking backend, wk integration backend...)
    • User Interfaces (picking ui, leveling board ui...)
  • Internal
    • Domain apis
    • Data Ingestion Services apis
As per security best practices, internal APIs should not be available for calls outside of the container app environment, however, for dev/test and troubleshooting reasons, these apis can be exposed in the dev environment, maybe also in ppr.

The objective of this user story is to configure the app proxy to implement the following:
API Type dev ppr pro
Internal API exposed not exposed not exposed
External API exposed exposed exposed

Code Review for mesx-app-order
description:
Code Review for mesx-app-order

pickingOrder.controller.ts:
  • Utilizes query param DTO from this Resource https://tkssharma.com/nestjs-playing-with-query-param-dto/?mwg_rnd=4205775.
  • ResponseDTO and Swagger annotations are implemented.
  • Unused `getHello` route.
  • Evaluate the necessity of `/* eslint object-curly-newline: 0 */`. It's generally advised to fix ESLint issues rather than disabling rules.

productionOrder.controller.ts:
  • Similar structure as pickingOrder.controller.ts.
  • Error handling is well-implemented but should be moved to the service layer. NestJS best practices recommend keeping controllers lean and delegating business logic to services.
  • Consider removing the body in a GET request, especially when it's typed as a string. GET requests typically don't have a request body.

pickingOrder.service.ts and productionOrder.service.ts:
  • Missing try-catch blocks in methods interacting with the database. Including error handling with try-catch blocks is crucial for handling potential errors during database operations.
  • Consider typing the response of functions for better code clarity and robustness.

Explore the use of class-validator and class-transformer to validate incoming data, as recommended in the NestJS documentation. This ensures robust data validation and transformation capabilities https://docs.nestjs.com/techniques/validation

Project Structure:
  • The approach of structuring by Layer is commendable but may become cluttered, especially in larger projects with numerous features/modules.
  • Suggest evaluating the use of Project Structure by Feature, especially for microservices containing many features. Refer to the provided articles for guidance on structuring NestJS projects.: https://medium.com/@ankit_64419/nestjs-based-product-project-architecture-and-folder-structure-f8fb3791e82
          https://medium.com/the-crowdlinker-chronicle/best-way-to-structure-your-directory-code-nestjs-a06c7a641401#Config%20%E2%9A%99%EF%B8%8F

titre: Code Review for mesx-materialized-view-picking
description:
subscribe.controller.ts
​
  • assign payloadDTO for data: Consider implementing a PayloadDTO to define the structure of the data being handled by the controller. This can improve code clarity and maintainability by clearly specifying the expected shape of the incoming data.
  • Explore the use of class-validator and class-transformer: NestJS recommends using class-validator and class-transformer for robust data validation and transformation. Integrating these libraries can ensure that incoming data is validated against defined rules and transformed into the desired format, enhancing the reliability and integrity of the application. Refer to the NestJS documentation for guidance on how to implement validation: NestJS Validation Techniques.
  • Try using the variable environment of pubsub name and topic.
subscribe.service.ts
  • Consider moving interfaces PickingOrderItem and MinSeqNumResponse to a global interface folder: To improve organization and reusability, it's advisable to move interfaces such as PickingOrderItem and MinSeqNumResponse to a global interface folder. This ensures that interfaces are easily accessible and can be reused across different parts of the application.
  • Create DTO for both API calls: Utilizing DTOs (Data Transfer Objects) for data structures passed between services can enhance code readability and maintainability. By defining DTOs for each API call, you can explicitly specify the structure of the data being exchanged, making it easier to understand and manage data flow within the application.
  • Make the API call functions separate from the logic: Consider separating the logic for making API calls into distinct functions. Dividing the code into smaller, focused functions can improve readability, maintainability, and testability. Each function should have a clear and specific purpose, making the code easier to understand and modify. This approach also facilitates unit testing of individual components, enhancing overall code quality.

description:
-Component Composition:
Break down the component into smaller, reusable components if it becomes too large or complex. This enhances code reusability and simplifies maintenance.
Example: "PickingScreenLayout.vue" component can be devided in more components.

-Linting Rules:
Ensure eslint rules are enabled and consistently followed across the codebase. Removing temporary disablements (/* eslint-disable */) helps maintain code quality and consistency.

-Type Annotations:
Utilize explicit type annotations for variables like resetSelect, options, and optionsHour to enhance code clarity and ensure better type safety, especially in TypeScript environments.
Avoid using the "any" type whenever possible, as it undermines type safety and clarity in the codebase.

-Comments and Documentation:
Incorporate comments and documentation to elucidate intricate logic, algorithms, or business rules. Comments should provide context and rationale, particularly for sections that may not be immediately clear to other developers.

-Logical Order:
Organize code logically, grouping related functionality together. Ensure variables, functions, and components that are closely related are placed near each other, improving code readability and maintainability.

-WK-details:

WK-details is designed as a separate module but is part of the picking-screen module.

-Pinia for State Management:
Consider leveraging Pinia in the application, as it simplifies state management tasks and enhances scalability.

  1. Retrieving Selected Items:

    • For each selected item, validate if it can be closed (determined by the CLOSEABLE boolean value, indicating if the destination location is pool stock).

  3. Creating Shop Order List:
    • Compile a list of shop orders from the selected items.
  4. Closure Confirmation:
    • Present a confirmation dialog to inquire if the user confirms the closure of selected WKs with Pool Stock Destination Location.
  5. Response Handling:
    • Process the response of the closure request.
    • Upon successful closure, display a success message and clear the selections in the table.

Options

Advantages

Drawbacks

Separate repos for DI and API

  • Decoupling
  • Duplicate Definitions of Entities

Single repo for DI and API

  • Less Decoupling (But same domain boundary anyway)
  • Unified Entities Definitions

Package entities and migration as library (Separate Library Repo)

  • Conserve initial repo organization
  • Complex to Setup
  • Work over 3 repositories and 3 pipelines

Package entities and migration as library (Library Built From Api Repo)

  • Conserve initial repo organization
  • Complex to Setup
  • Work over 2 repositories and 3 pipelines


Note that:
  • With a single repository, we can still have seperate pipelines for di and api and seperate container app instances

Analysis
description:
Analysis for events History

 

Aim: The aim of this task is to measure the reliability of voice-to-act classification.

Table Creation: A table named events_history will be created with the following structure:

Table Structure: eventsHistory

  • id: string; auto-generated
  • plantId: number: the plant ID
  • objectId: string; the ticket ID
  • classificationMode: string; modification done by voice or manual
  • lastModifiedTimestamp: Date; date of the modification (current date)
  • details: string; details of the classification which includes:
    • cause1
    • cause2
    • cause3
    • remark

Backend Processing:

  • In the downtime backend, if the classification is done by voice, log the event.
  • If the classification is done manually:
    • Check the last modification.
    • If the last modification was done by voice, log it.

Next Steps for the Future


API Creation: Create an API with one mandatory input (plant) and two optional inputs (ticketId and numberOfEvents). This API will retrieve the history of events based on the provided inputs.

API Details:

Inputs:

  • plant: The ID of the plant (mandatory)
  • ticketId: The ID of the ticket (optional)
  • numberOfEvents: The number of events to retrieve (optional)

Functionality:

  • If plant is provided:
    • If neither ticketId nor numberOfEvents are provided, return the top 100 events logged for this plant.
    • If only numberOfEvents is provided, return the top numberOfEvents events logged for this plant.
    • If only ticketId is provided, return all events logged for that ticket on this plant.

description:
@GHAZOUANI Mohamed Neji As per your feedback: '

As we discussed, these are the comments that I noticed about SonarQube:

  • "Import name ResourceFamilyAssignModule must match one of the following formats: camelCase (external_eslint_repo:@typescript-eslint/naming-convention). In NestJS naming convention, the class representing the service should follow the PascalCase convention.

  • Prefer named exports. (external_eslint_repo:import/no-default-export) does not correspond to our rules.

  • Type property name CAUSE must match one of the following formats: camelCase (external_eslint_repo:@typescript-eslint/naming-convention). I can't modify the DTO files as they are received data from MII with uppercase.

  • For ordering imports and keys, is there a VSCode extension to handle it?"

'

Conflicting Rules

  • external_eslint_repo:import/no-default-export conflicts with prefer default export
  • external_eslint_repo:@typescript-eslint/naming-convention for properties from MII and import names
  • for…of instead of .forEach(…). (external_eslint_repo:unicorn/no-array-for-each)
  • iterators/generators require regenerator-runtime, which is too heavyweight for this guide to allow them. Separately, loops should be avoided in favor of array iterations
  • Prefer top-level await over an async function `bootstrap` call  unicorn/prefer-top-level-await

titre: APIs Code Review
description:
UME API Code review

Tuesday, 9 July 2024

4:25 PM

 

General Recommendations and Advice

  1. Consistency in Error Handling and Logging: I recommend ensuring consistency in the way errors are handled and logged across all functions. Using a unified approach throughout the application enhances maintainability and debugging. Please utilize our custom logging service instead of console for logging purposes. Incorporating try-catch blocks for every interaction with the database is essential for robust error handling.
  2. DTO Usage for Validation and Response: Consistently utilize Data Transfer Objects (DTOs) for validating payload inputs and defining structured responses. This approach ensures clarity, validation, and adherence to expected data structures throughout the application.
  3. Parameter Handling: Consider the appropriate use of @Param, @QueryParam, or @Body decorators for API parameters. This ensures parameters are handled securely and appropriately (e.g., using query parameters for sensitive data like emails).

Thank you for your attention to these points, and good job! I'm open to discussing any aspect of this code review.

 

Detailed Code Review

Project Structure Guidelines

  • Project Structure: Please adhere to our NestJS project structure guidelines by organizing modules of the same topic under dedicated folders within the modules directory. For example:
    • permissions-module
    • user-attributes-module
      Each module should include a       dto folder for clarity and consistency.
  • Initialization Folder: Rename and consolidate the existing examples and data folders into a unified initialization folder (seeding and initial-data respectively) for better clarity and organization.

Main.ts

  • Validation DTOs: Ensure validation DTOs work correctly by adding the following code snippet to main.ts:

    app.    useGlobalPipes(
          newValidationPipe({
            transform: true,
            whitelist: true,
            forbidNonWhitelisted: true,
      }),
    );
  • Swagger Configuration: Update the title name and description of Swagger configuration from master-api to ume-api for clarity.

App.module.ts

  • Modularization: Ensure controllers and providers are defined within their respective modules. Import modules directly into app.module.ts for a more modular and maintainable codebase.
  • Configuration Loading: Address the missing loading of URL API configuration for completeness and consistency.

Env.dist

  • Documentation: Include documentation for URL_UME_API in Env.dist for clarity and completeness.

User.service.ts

  • Error Handling: Enhance error handling in methods like createUser and getUserByEmail by adding try-catch blocks for better error management.
  • updateUserLastLogin: Refine updateUserLastLogin to handle specific errors individually rather than catching all errors generically. Consider returning a response object or the updated user entity for consistent return types.

UserController.ts

  • createUser:
    • Consistent Return Types: Ensure all controller methods have consistent return types for clarity and predictability.
    • Error Handling: Improve error handling to provide appropriate status codes and messages to clients.
  • getUserByEmail, updateUserLastLoginByEmail:
    • DTO Validation: Implement DTOs for validating inputs such as email and lastLogin.
    • Error Handling: Enhance error handling to ensure clients receive suitable status codes and error messages.
    • Parameter Usage:
      • GET Requests: Utilize query parameters to filter by email to avoid exposing sensitive data in the URL path.
      • POST/PUT/PATCH Requests: Include email in the request body if part of a larger payload for cleaner and more secure URLs.

UserAttributeService.ts

  • Remove Commented Code: Clean up commented-out code for better code clarity.
  • Consistent Return Types: Ensure consistency in return types across service methods.
  • Error Handling: Improve error handling to provide clear status codes and messages to clients. Use our logging service instead of console.error for improved monitoring and debugging.

UserAttributeController.ts

  • Remove Commented Code: Remove commented-out sections for cleaner and more maintainable code.
  • Consistent Return Types: Ensure all controller methods return consistent data types.
  • Error Handling: Improve error handling to provide appropriate status codes and messages to clients.
  • DTO Usage: Utilize DTOs consistently for structured and validated data transfer.

UserAttributeModule.ts

  • Service Declaration: Avoid providing or exporting services not explicitly declared within the module. Instead, import the module where the service is provided (e.g., DaprConfigModule) to utilize its services. This practice prevents unpredictable behavior and ensures clarity in service dependencies.
  • Module Design: Directly import modules where services are provided rather than exporting unnecessary services.

UserAttributeMappingModule.ts

  • Entity Declaration: Ensure each entity is declared only once within TypeOrmModule.forFeature to maintain clarity and avoid unpredictable behavior.
  • Clean Code Practices: Adhere to clean code principles by organizing imports and declarations straightforwardly.
  • UserAttributeMappingService.ts
    • DTO Usage: Instead of spreading attributes of payload or return functions, consider using a DTO interface for improved readability and maintainability.
    • Interface Placement: Move interfaces inside a separate DTO file to adhere to separation of concerns.
    • Consistent Error Handling: Ensure consistent and appropriate error handling throughout all service methods.
    • Logging: Utilize the application logger for consistent and meaningful logging instead of console.error.

UserAttributeController.ts

  • Consistent Return Types: Ensure uniformity in the return types of controller methods using DTOs.
  • Error Handling: Enhance error handling to provide precise status codes and messages to clients.
  • DTO Usage: Utilize DTOs for structured and validated data transfer.
  • Try-Catch: Implement try-catch blocks for consistent error handling.

 

Implementing these recommendations will enhance the maintainability, readability, and robustness of your NestJS application. Well done on your work so far, and feel free to discuss any aspect of this code review further.

titre: Backend for Front End Violations Cleanup
description:
All UI projects (picking-ui, downtime-ui, ume-ui) are referencing domain apis directly bypassing their respective Backends.


Consider the following diagram (figurative example):


Here picking-ui is calling directly the master domain's api which should be prohibited (red arraow). Instead, picking-backend should provide and endpoint to, for example, read master data. the implementation of the endpoint calls the master api sub-sequently (blue arrow)


While this can be convenient in the short term, it has the following drawbacks:

  • UI is coupled to several api endpoints instead of just being couple to its backend
  • Communication from UI to domain api is difficult if not possible via mutual TLS
  • UI must care about authentication with several endpoints (for each domain api used)

 

In the initial architecture, we decided to use the principle of backend for front end it would be wasteful in my opinion to discard it.
ui projects should only make api calls to their respective backends and to ume-api strictly.

titre: Data Ingestion container apps alignment with eventhub auto-scale rules
auto-scaling rules for master data ingestion
[HA-Capacity]Eventhub based auto-scaling for data ingestion container apps
description:
Principle



Event Hub Auto-Scale Issues

On master-data-ingestion,
  1. After applying a load of ~100000 messages per seconde via debezium snapshot, we did not notice auto-scale of the container app; replica count is always equal to 1
  2. On the following chart we can see that the incoming volume vs outgoing volume should cause an auto scale:

  3. During the tests in the KEDA logs, we observed the following error message:
    unable to get runtimeInfo for metrics: dial tcp: lookup ehn-gptmpxn01-eun-dev-core-01.servicebus.windows.net.servicebus.windows.net on 100.100.244.189:53: no such host
    => Issue caused by not properly naming the eventhub namespace in the auto-scaler config (PR 70022: Eventhub Autoscaler evh-ns name )
  4. In addition, with some homework and reaching out to the KEDA community, we found that auto-scaling requires max replicas = max partitions​
  5. May not be relevant, but there are signs in the documentation that the auto-scaler is maybe not compatible with Node:
    https://keda.sh/docs/2.15/scalers/azure-event-hub/#checkpointing-behaviour     (Effectively not relevant as we managed to scale up)

Conclusion

After further investigation and as of 22/08/2024:
  • The KEDA event hub auto-scaler does not create replicas beyond the event hub partition count
  • Our current throughput needs (given the count of on-boarded plants) does not justify the cost of partition count > 1
  • In the future, we can increase partitions as we deploy to more sites
  • We will keep the current auto-scale configuration which gives us scale to 0 capability

In addition, we tried setting partition count =2 for the MTL topic in dev and we observed scale up + outgoing message rate improvement (the double).

With 1 Replica (around 6k):

With 2 replicas (around 13k):

Given the previous, we will:

  • Investigate further filters for dev, ppr MTL snapshots
  • Keep the auto-scale config as is

description:
Analyze gap and API development

  • To track data changes, create an API that detects modifications. The API requires the following input parameters: plant (mandatory), lastTimeStamp (mandatory). The API will return the changes made in four specific tables: resource_family_assign, cause_family_assign, family, and down_time_cause. The response structure will be as follows:

{
  "causeFamilyAssign": [],
  "downTimeCause": [],
  "family": [],
  "resourceFamilyAssign": []
}

Each of these arrays will contain the data that has changed since the provided lastTimeStamp.

  • At the ingestion level, we will implement a soft delete mechanism. When an event of type 'd' is received, the deleted_at field in the corresponding table will be populated, indicating that the record is soft deleted. For update and read operations, we will exclude soft-deleted records by ensuring that the deleted_at field is null.
@OnEvent('downTimeTicket.d')
  private async softDelete(payload: { ticket: string; plant: string }): Promise<void> {
    if (!payload || !payload.ticket || !payload.plant) {
      return this.logger.error(`Invalid payload for soft delete: ${JSON.stringify(payload)}`);
    }

    const { ticket, plant } = payload;

    try {
      const downTimeTicket = await this.downTimeTicketRepository.findOne({
        where: { ticket, plant, deletedAt: null },
      });

      if (!downTimeTicket) {
        throw new HttpException(
          `Down Time Ticket with ticket ${ticket} and Plant ID ${plant} not found`,
          HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND,
        );
      }

      downTimeTicket.deletedAt = new Date();
      await this.downTimeTicketRepository.save(downTimeTicket);
      this.logger.debug(
        `Down Time Ticket with ticket ${ticket} and Plant ID ${plant} has been soft deleted`,
      );
    } catch (error) {
      this.logger.error(`Error in soft deleting Down Time Ticket: ${error.message}`);
      throw new HttpException(
        `Error in soft deleting data: ${error.message}`,
        HttpStatus.BAD_REQUEST,
      );
    }
  }

// Find the existing entity, excluding soft-deleted ones

description:
Outcome

After investigating the JMeter event hub plugin(pnopjp/jmeter-plugins):

  • Not possible to define dynamic messages only static messages to be sent

After investigating possible use of the JSR223 sampler as suggested here:

  • We did not manage to set the eventhub sdk dependencies correctly even after determining the dependencies via maven:
    java.lang.NoClassDefFoundError: Could not initialize class com.azure.core.amqp.models.CbsAuthorizationType
      at com.azure.messaging.eventhubs.EventHubClientBuilder.getConnectionOptions(EventHubClientBuilder.java:1163) ~[azure-messaging-eventhubs-5.18.6.jar:5.18.6]
  •  In addition, script has to be defined in Java or Groovy

After investigating possible use of Azure-Samples/load-testing-jmeter-plugins:

  • Even though the sampler allow to define a dynamic message via liquid templates with the possibility to declare several samples, it is not possible to generate two messages with the same HANDLE and SHOP_ORDER field
  • each liquid template file has its own context

Furthermore, We realize that the jmeter listeners will not provide useful information during tests, as they are more suited for standard HTTP Workloads and will only measure message sending response time for the case of event hub.

Given the previous constraint, we will move on with applying load using a custom javascript script.

description:
Applying the script on order-di

After creating script to apply load on order-data ingestion, we noticed that applying load from 4 concurrent processes causes strange behavior on order update and creation:
  • Some orders are not created
  • Some orders are not updated
The previous occurred, even after ensuring different and valid timestamps for all events.

Note that, order creation and update works correctly with a single process no matter the delay between event sending.

Note also, that as opposed to initial assumptions (@GHAZOUANI Mohamed Neji ): 
  • WK creation = 1 create shop order + 1 create picking order
  • WK update = 1 update shop order + 1 update picking order
From a scalability point of view:
  • With a 8 processes, 1000 message each and adelay of 50 milliseconds we did not manage to cause the auto-scale
  • 1 replica was able to handle the load reasonably
  • CPU usage and memory usage was reasonable
  • We did not explicitly calculate event processing response time

description:
To investigate the issue of missing data on the picking screen, we executed a script designed to test high data loads. During our investigation, we discovered that the missing data was due to an absence in the Redis cache. This absence was traced back to the picking cache microservice, where a loss of data occurred. The root cause of this data loss in the picking cache microservice was identified as a race condition that happens during data loading. This issue arises from the use of a single key ("plant") for all orders.
As first step to solve the issue we decided  to implement a solution where each order is assigned a separate key with the prefix "plant" (e.g., "plant.order"). However, this approach has introduced a new issue: Dapr State does not provide functionality to query multiple keys efficiently. We’ve identified that Redis, through its API, offers 
1) a solution with the SCAN command , which addresses the read based on a range of key in Redis but does not allow to filter data inside each key that we are still investigating. 
2) a solution with the rediSearch , which provide advanced search, indexing, and querying capabilities, making it a versatile tool for developers needing high-performance search features directly integrated into their Redis environment.
Those solution was rejected as we will eliminate the usage of API dapr to using Redis directly . 
==> those solution was reject as we lose abstraction layer when switching to other components to replace redis
3) solution of implementing a distributed lock API in dapr to prevent concurrent cache update ===> rejected as the API is still in alpha state that could be not fully stable and complete 
4) a solution with rebuilding cache through scheduling ===> rejected we found that using Dapr cron bindings poses several challenges. Specifically, managing separate cron jobs for each plant increases maintenance effort, complicates monitoring and troubleshooting, and raises scalability issues as the number of plants grows.
5)  Lock Management for the Ingestion Microservice with Dead Letter Queue Implementation : --->  To ensure no data is missed, we will manage locks similarly to how we did in the ingestion microservice by implementing the Dead Letter Queue (DLQ) principle
6) Task scheduler : 
Variant 1: build cache from scratch
API composition on huge data increases response time
Variant 2: update cache only on updated objects – manage queue with object IDs
In ingestion microservice, manage a queue (SQL) with list of orders to update
Could be added in ORD service
Job per plant per use case reads the queue based on plant, consumer
Once integrated, record will be deleted if last modified timestamp is not greater that last read to avoid conflicts
Write in cache redis could be by batch
Reduce events processing as for a single order we can receive a lot of operation in CDC
No need to sequence events as already managed in data ingestion
Manage API for rebuild cache from scratch needed for support
Variant 3: retrieve orders to be stored in cache and check if record changed or not before recalculation
N.B:
Consider adding new plants without impact on running ones
Acceptable runtime for real time screens

Analysis
description:
Problem: We observed slowness in the picking screen when displaying data, even when no data is present. 
Analysis: The issue stems from the use of an interceptor that loops through the payload to detect fields of type `date` and performs a conversion; otherwise, it does nothing. This process is resource-intensive, especially when each user interaction triggers a backend call. The risk is compounded by the fact that the screen auto-refreshes every minute, leading to situations where a second call is made before the first one completes, potentially causing the first call to fail.

The primary cause of this slowness is the `transformDatesToUTC` and `transformDatesFromUTC` functions. These functions recursively traverse all properties in the payload, including deeply nested objects and arrays, to find and convert date values. This recursive approach can be inefficient, particularly when handling large datasets or frequent refresh intervals.
Proposed Solution: We plan to shift the date conversion process to the frontend, ensuring that dates are returned in UTC from the backend. This approach should reduce the processing overhead on the backend and improve the responsiveness of the picking screen.

titre: Integrate backend in UI
Analyze backend requirements
description:
Split Feature Implementation:

  • New Split Screen Creation (32h):
    • Develop a new screen specifically for the split functionality. This screen will be accessible via a "Split" button.


    • When a top-level classification is selected, the user will be redirected to view the corresponding sub-levels.
    • Ticket Date Logic:
      • The start date for the first ticket will be inherited from the master ticket's start date.
      • The user can select an end date for the first ticket, but it must fall between the master ticket's start and end dates. If it does not, an error message will be displayed.

      • The start date of the second ticket will be automatically set to the end date of the first ticket and cannot be edited.
      • The end date of the second ticket will match the master ticket's end date and will not be editable. If the master ticket lacks an end date, the second ticket will also remain without an end date.
  • Transaction and API Development (24h):
    • Create a new transaction named SPLIT_DOWNTIME within SC_MES_API/DOWNTIME and expose it under SC_MES_API/INTERFACE.
    • The transaction logic will handle splitting a master ticket into two:
      • The first ticket will have the same start date as the master ticket.
      • The second ticket's start date will be set to the end date of the first ticket.
      • The second ticket’s end date will match the master ticket’s end date. If the master ticket has no end date, the second ticket will not have an end date.
    • This transaction will be implemented in MII, within SC_DMC/DATA_ENTRY/NON_TRS/TRANSACTION/OPERATE_ON_NON_TRS_TICKET, specifically in the sequence Sequence_14: IF_SPLIT_MODE.
  • Backend API Development (16h):
    • Add a new API endpoint to the downtime backend to enable writeback operations to MII. This endpoint will invoke the newly created SPLIT_DOWNTIME transaction.
  • Frontend Integration (16h):
    • On the split screen, implement the functionality so that when the "Save" button is clicked, it triggers the backend API call to execute the split operation.

BR for the transaction under this task: #96043

Remove Feature Implementation:

  • Backend Integration (8​​h):
    • Create a new transaction/query named DELETE_TICKET under SC_MES_API/DOWNTIME and expose it through the INTERFACE to update the ticket status from ACTI or CLSD to DELT. 
  • Frontend Integration (16h):
    • On the downtime screen, the "Remove" button should only be displayed for tickets not created by the system (user_id != 'System'). If the ticket was created by the system, the button should not be shown. When the "Remove" button is clicked, it should trigger the newly created DELETE_TICKET transaction.

BR for the transaction under this task: #96023 


DMC Create Repair Request Feature Implementation:

  • Frontend Integration (16h):
    • Regarding the "Create Repair Request" button in DMC, we plan to trigger the MII screen in a similar way to how the "Kanban Management" button functions on the picking screen. To achieve this, we've initiated discussions with the 9MIII team concerning the authentication process between MES and MII (Please see the attached email).

titre: Management of log
Infra / CodeFlow-DevEx - Backend Projects Local Debugging Guidelines
Debug Builds for backend projects
description:
Initial Target

  • Add a debug build npm script in backend projects
  • Update the pipeline to include a build type switch

Findings

  • Nest builds with sourcemap by default
  • For debugging remotely:
    • app should be launched with debugger listening on 9229
    • src should be packaged in the container for ts debug
  • In the infra 9229 should be mapped and exposed
  • app proxy should map a /debug endpoint to 9229
  • VS Code debugger should authenticate to /debug endpoint or auth should be disabled for auth endpoint

Findings 2

After some prototyping it turns out that:
  • Debugger endpoint is a websocket endpoint
  • Possible to route websocket traffic via Traefik app proxy
  • Container app environment app proxy does not impact websocket traffic
  • Node debugger by design does not allow remote connections with hostnames, only with localhost or a specific IP
    • This has been validated via the troubleshooting container

Conclusion

  • Remote debugging on container app environment via exposing the debugger web-socket endpoint is not possible
  • SSH Tunnels are the supported mechanism
  • Maybe Possible to tunnel the ssh traffic via Traefik TCP Services
    • Need to install ssh server in the container
    • Need to manage credentials for user used to connect to the container
    • Need to manage running 2 services on the container = the app and sshd (with supervisord ?)
    • Need to manage Release/Debug builds by only including the debug machinery in Debug Builds

titre: WK Integration-Job Buffer processing analysis (MII transaction)
description:
-Create new trx SC_MES_API/WKINTEGRATION/TRANSACTION/V1/INTEGRATE_WK_KANBAN:
1.The trx should have an input "InKanbanRequestXML" of type XML, an input "InPlant" of type string and a single output "ResultXML" also of type XML. The input "InKanbanRequestXML" should respect the current structure of node "WithdrawalKanban" coming from Preactor (check attachments). The structure of "ResultXML" can also be found in the attachements. The general structure of this new transaction can replicate the structure of SC_ME/AUTOMATIC_INTEGRATION/TRANSACTION/AUTOMATIC_INTEGRATION (I am referring to the structure of branches: start with a XML DOCUMENT bloc, have a general CATCH branch, a branch executed under a repeater, a CATCH under the repeater, etc)  (WL 2h)
2.The purpose of the trx is to create a new WK in NEO (branch "Creation case" from SC_ME/AUTOMATIC_INTEGRATION/TRANSACTION/AUTOMATIC_INTEGRATION under the switch action block can be used as example):

-create new query which will retrieve the PRODSTRAT (Material setting), BBBMode(Material setting), SFG_FLOW (WC setting), POOLSTOCK (Location setting) and BOM_EXPLOSION (Material setting, official name is GIVE_SEQ_TO_UPSTREAM). Queries SC_ME/AUTOMATIC_INTEGRATION/QUERY/SELECT_ITEM_CUSTOM_FIELD, SC_ME/AUTOMATIC_INTEGRATION/QUERY/SELECT_MATERIAL_GRP_BBB_MODE, SC_ME/COMMON/QUERY/SELECT_CUTOM_FIELDS_BY_ATTRIBUTE and COMMON/INITIALIZATION/QUERY/SELECT_STG_LOC (all 4 queries executed in SC_ME/AUTOMATIC_INTEGRATION/TRANSACTION/AUTOMATIC_INTEGRATION) can be used as examples on how to retrieve these details which are needed for next steps. (WL 6h)

-make a local copy of SC_ME/AUTOMATIC_INTEGRATION/TRANSACTION/CHECK_FIELDS in folder SC_MES_API/WKINTEGRATION/TRANSACTION/V1 (WL 6h)

-make a local copy of SC_ME/AUTOMATIC_INTEGRATION/TRANSACTION/ALTER_KANBAN in SC_MES_API/WKINTEGRATION/TRANSACTION/V1 and rename it CREATE_WK_KANBAN. We need to keep only the creation branch (and make local copies to all used queries + sub-transactions) + the initial part where the OD is updated (in case DeliveryNumber is specified) (WL 8h)

-make a local copy of SC_ME/API/PRODUCTION/TRANSACTION/API_WK_BOM_EXPLOSION (WL 6h)


-the transaction should have a repeater on the node "WithdrawalKanban" from input "InKanbanRequestXML" in order to be able to process one or multiple creation requests. In case multiple WKs are created from same external call, the output "ResultXML" will contain multiple nodes of type <Row>, one for each created WK. (WL 2h)

-under the repeater, replicate the logic of creation branch from SC_ME/AUTOMATIC_INTEGRATION/TRANSACTION/AUTOMATIC_INTEGRATION but use the local copies (from SC_MES_API project) of the objects used under the creation branch. (WL 2h)

-the general flow of the new trx should follow this idea: for each "WithdrawalKanban" node, retrieve the needed details with the new query(PRODSTRAT, BBBMode, SFG_FLOW, etc), check the values from the node with CHECK_FIELDS, create the WK with the provided details, check BOM explosion is needed and if true then explode the BOM with API_WK_BOM_EXPLOSION. In case any steps generate an error, catch the error and put it in the response "ResultXML" and continue with next "WithdrawalKanban" node (if any left)

- General remarks: The new queries should use the new data model (datasource FAURECIA_WIP). When copying a trx in the new prject SC_MES_API, all the used queries and sub-transactions should also be copied under SC_MES_API (in the corresponding QUERY or TRANSACTION folder) and used from here so that there will be no dependency with SC_ME project (or with any other project but SC_ME is most widely used in the replicated objects so SC_ME is our primary focus). In case the sub-transaction that we need to replicate locally in SC_MES_API, has a branch which is not needed, we can remove it (for example SC_ME/API/COMMON/TRANSACTION/CREATE_KANBAN has a branch for PIK creation but in our case we will only create WKs so the PIK branch is not needed in our case, we can remove it during the copying/replicating stage). When making local copies, we also need to remove the part which inserts errors in ERROR_LOG or makes changes in other flows which do no exist in MES.X. We can put generic queries/transactions in SC_MES_API/COMMON (WL 0h)


-Create Xacute wrapper SC_MES_API/INTERFACE/WKINTEGRATION/V1/XCT_INTEGRATE_WK_KANABN to be externally called (WL 0h)

Development- DownTime: Write Back to local MES Logic review
description:
Problem Faced:
  • Writeback and data refresh in MES are not synchronized, leading to discrepancies between MESX and MII, which are not visible.
  • UI data refresh issues, especially during repetitive cases of Debezium stoppage.
  • Objects are unlocked as soon as the API returns a result.

  • Locks are stored in Redis cache per plant key.
Proposed Solution:
  • Remove Redis Lock Logic
Eliminate the current lock logic stored in Redis cache.
  • Add 'lock_status' Column
    • Introduce a new column named lock_status in the downtime ticket table.
    • Default value: 0 (unlocked).
  • Add 'last_processed_timestamp' Column
    • Add a new column named last_processed_timestamp in downtime ticket table of type datetime (nullable).
    • This column indicates the time of the last writeback call to MII.
  • Backend Lock Management
    • Before Writeback to MII: 
      • Update  last_processed_timestamp to current timestamp (in UTC)
      • Set lock_status to 1 (indicating the ticket is being updated).
    • In the case of a successful response from MII:
      • No Immediate Unlock in Downtime UI.
      • Adapt the data ingestion process to compare last_processed_timestamp with updated_at. If last_processed_timestamp is less than updated_at, unlock the object by setting last_processed_timestamp to null and lock_status to 0.
      • Long-term solution: Unlock the object after a certain period using a scheduled job.
    • In the case of an error response:
      • Functional Error: No Updates on Downtime Ticket.
      • Unlock the object by setting last_processed_timestamp to null and lock_status to 0.
      • Long-term solution: The MII transaction will indicate if the object has been modified or not to manage the unlock process accordingly.
  • Frontend Auto-Refresh Logic:
    • Check if lock_status is 1, then disable buttons (e.g., save) and display a pop-up: "Ticket is being processed."
    • Implement a timeout mechanism as the first action to refresh the downtime tickets by recalling the API after X seconds (long-term goal: implement WebSocket mechanism).
    • This ensures the system can correct itself in case of synchronization latency.

titre: 5. [MES X.0] Update logic
description:
the user can have the possibility to perform some update on the WK integration  
those updates can be from logistic side or production side.

and the update is based on the custom status of the WK 
for the logistic side these are the data needs to be updated 
TPA
DELIVERY
DESTINATION LOCATION
START PICKING
END PICKING
CUSTOMER

these data are relevant for update no matter what the status of the WK is. 
for Delivery it depends on a flag at server config level 
if it's set to no then the update is possible for all case. if it's set to yes then allow update only in case of custom status (OPEN, PIK_CREATED, TAKE_FROM_STOCK)
for the production side these are the data needs to be updated 
Change Production line
production line upstream
source location
start production
end production
quantity 

these ones are relevant for update only if the WK is open, PIK_CREATED, PIK_RELEASABLE, TAKE_FROM_STOCK
BUFFER STATUS NEO STATUS Action
received   insert line in the buffer table and the job will do the update (if we have multiple lines with same WK that are not treated yet the job will take the last line )
success ERROR insert line in the buffer table and the job will do the update
Open, PIK_CREATED,PIK_RELEASD,TAKE_FROM_STOCK  No matter what is the value that is updated, the API will do the update directly and insert a line in the buffer with sucess
PIK_LAUNCHED,PICKED,PALLETIZED if the logistic info are updated, the API will do the update directly and insert a line in the buffer with sucess. If the production info are updated, an error will be returned and error will be logged in buffer table
PIK_CLOSED,CLOSED no update an error line will be logged
ERROR   insert line in the buffer table and the job will do the update
IN progress   insert line in the buffer table and the job will do the update

titre: Time Frame coloring
description:
•Colour coding will be applicable only for TPA view:


regarding the coloring code is based on different factors such as the TPA ASSIGNEMENT, date now and the picking time of the WK 
the color of the time frame will only appear when we select the truck as a grouping property. 
the truck is the TPA Id = concatenation of Customer Description and Truck departure timestamp in local time) OR Pool

in the coloring code we have 5 colors 
1-Dark blue: the WK are in the past and considered late (the picking time of the WK is in the past and exceeded the tolerance value).  
from the date selected in the timeline until X it will be Dark blue 
2-light blue: the WK are in the past and not considered late (the picking time of the WK is in the past and didn't exceed the tolerance value) 
it means date now -past_late_acceptance(in plant config: SHP domain) =X
so, from X until date now it will be light blue 

3-yellow: difference between begin and end preparation of the TPA
if they are overlapped, we keep the orange
if the blue and yellow are overlapped we keep the blue 

4-Orange: the remaining preparation time of the TPA (current hour and end preparation)
difference between current hour and end preparation of the TPA

if the date now is not in between the begin preparation and end preparation we neglect the orange  

5-Red: the Picking Time of the WK is after the end preparation time of the TPA

from the end preparation of the TPA until the TO date selected from the timeline it will be red

titre: Sprint Release Automation
description:
Current end of sprint release process is manual, the aim of this user story is to automate the process as much as possible

Observations

  • MES X.0 is released every sprint (sprint is the cycle of release)
  • Automated full release should be doable multiple times per sprint
  • Process should allow for manual release of the subset of the services
  • Release notes can be generated at the application level and consolidated at the infra pipeline level

Process

  1. For each service, a stable version is released
    1. => Can be automated by calculating versions depending on work items referenced
  2. In Infra repo, each service's version is referenced for ppr in _service_versions.json
    1. => _service_versions.json can be generated automatically based on latest tag for each service with inclusion and exclusion capabilities 
  3. Infra repo is tagged to engage ppr deployment
    1. => Can be automated by tagging latest minor + 1

titre: Create api to retreive material_group and bbb_mode by plant and material_id in order domain
description:
0To create a GET API for retrieving the `material_group` and `bbb_mode` based on `material_id` and `plant` as input, we need to establish three tables within the `ORD` domain:
`material_dtl`, `material_group`, and `material_group_member`. 
The `material_dtl` table will store the details of each material, while the `material_group` table will contain the `bbb_mode` for each material group. The `material_group_member` table will serve as the association between materials and material groups. Each material group can be linked to multiple materials, and each material can belong to multiple material groups, representing a many-to-many relationship.





 The API will accept `material_id` and `plant` as parameters and perform a join operation across these tables to fetch the required `material_group` and `bbb_mode`.

titre: [Downtime] Access via URL
description:
Technical Analysis :

 

Frontend:

  1. Route Configuration:

    • Define a route that optionally accepts a resourceId parameter (e.g., /downtime/:resourceId?). This allows the page to load with or without a resourceId:
      • /downtime (without resourceId).
      • /downtime/:resourceId (with a specific resourceId).

  2. Extracting resourceId:

    • In the mounted() lifecycle hook of the Vue component:
      • Check if a resourceId is entered in the URL.
      • If no resourceId is provided, load the page normally without making an API call.
      • If a resourceId is provided, proceed to validate it against the plant hierarchy.

  3. Validating the resourceId using existing plant hierarchy data:

    • Use the existing plant hierarchy data (fetched from the API) to validate the entered resourceId.

    • If the resourceId is valid:

      • Display the downtime screen with the resourceId pre-filled in the input field.

    • If the resourceId is invalid:

      • Show an error message (e.g., a toast saying "Resource does not exist").
      • Redirect the user back to /downtime-ui.

titre: Analyzing for reducing call api backend
Analyze Event driven issue to update cache (on tpa update, etc ..)
description:
Problem:  

Currently, in the leveling board, updates triggered on other tables linked to WK information (e.g., `outbound_delivery`, `tpa_assignment`, `storage_location`, `material_dtl`) are not reflected in the leveling board. This results in inconsistencies where changes are not displayed on the screen in real-time, causing confusion for users who expect immediate updates.  

 

Examples:

- Case 1: 

  1. A WK is integrated without a TPA assignment, resulting in fields related to TPA assignment being left empty.  

  2. When the TPA assignment is performed later, WK data remains outdated, even though this information is essential for tasks like managing coloring in the leveling board.  

 

- Case 2: 

  1. A WK is integrated with a TPA assignment.  

  2. Later, an update is made to the TPA assignment.  

  3. WK data is not updated to reflect the new TPA assignment changes.  

 

Solution:  

Ensure that any updates performed on the tables linked to WK information (`outbound_delivery`, `tpa_assignment`, `storage_location`, `material_dtl`) are propagated to the relevant WK data. This will allow real-time updates to be reflected in the leveling board, ensuring accuracy and consistency for users.  



Analysis of Technical Proposed Solution:

1- Scheduled Job Execution:

  • Frequency: A scheduled job will run every x time to ensure timely detection and handling of changes.
  • Tasks: The job will perform the following:
  1. Inputs:
    • ​Plant: Specifies the plant context for the operation.
    • Last Update Time: Indicates the timestamp of the job's last successful execution, serving as a reference to identify subsequent changes.
  2. Change Detection:
    • Monitor relevant tables for any modifications (inserts, updates, or deletions) since the lastUpdateTime.
    • Focus only on changes related to the specified plant.
  3. API Interaction:
    • Call a designated API to fetch WKs associated with the detected changes.
    • These may include:
      • Current WKs: Represent ongoing operations.
      • Future WKs: Represent scheduled operations yet to begin.
  4. Update WKs:
    • Ensure the updated_at timestamp of each modified WK is updated to reflect the changes.
  5. Trigger Processing:
    • The processor will detect modified WKs based on their updated updated_at timestamps.
    • The processor will:
      • Execute the required business logic.
      • Synchronize changes to Cosmos DB as per the defined workflow.
=> We did not choose this solution because it does not provide real-time updates.

2- Use Pub/Sub:
The pub/sub model is a communication pattern where:

  • Publishers: Send messages (or events) without knowing who will consume them.
  • Subscribers: Listen for specific messages or events they are interested in.
  • Message Broker: Acts as an intermediary to manage and distribute messages between publishers and subscribers.

·  Publisher:

  • The data ingestion of the services (shipment, master) are the publisher.
  • It emits an event whenever a relevant change is made to the table.

·  Message Broker:

  • Dapr can handle message distribution, durability, and scaling.

·  Subscriber:

  • The event listener subscribes to the topic of the events.
  • When it detects the event, it executes logic to map changes to the relevant WK(s), updates their updated_at, and syncs them with the Cosmos DB.

=>Placing the subscriber within the use case's backend (e.g., the leveling backend) would cause delays, as the backend would already have read outdated data from Cosmos DB. On the other hand, placing the subscriber at the processor level could create confusion between events originating from the orchestrator and those generated by the subscriber.
=> This approach is currently being evaluated.

3- Processor-Worker Design:
  • At the worker level, we introduce logic to call an API to detect changes in specific tables based on the `lastRunProcessor` timestamp. This information would need to be recorded at the start of the processor's run. We can derive it from the orchestrator's publish time (with millisecond precision) or explore other solutions to persist this data when the processor starts. Once the changes are identified, another API is called to retrieve the relevant WKs and update their `updated_at` timestamp, allowing them to be detected by the `getOrdersByDate` API.
  • The challenge with this approach is that it increases the processing load on the processor, as updates are infrequent, and numerous checks would need to be performed. To address this, we propose incorporating Cosmos DB at the ingestion level. Upon detecting a creation or update in the designated tables, an entry would be added to Cosmos DB with the structure `{plant, table, lastModifiedTime}`.

  • On the processor side, the logic for detecting updates and updating the relevant WKs would only be triggered if a corresponding entry exists in Cosmos DB. This ensures updates are processed efficiently and only when necessary, reducing the processor's overall workload.

=> We did not choose this solution because we wanted to avoid adding inserts into Cosmos DB at the ingestion level.

4- Ingestion:

Incorporating checks and updates at the ingestion level for the specified domains (SHP, MASTER). If updates are detected, an API is called to fetch the relevant WKs and update their updated_at field. Once these updates are completed, the processor is triggered to execute the business logic using the updated data.

=> We did not choose this solution because the ingestion process would be too heavy, and calling the API from different domains would tightly couple it to specific use cases.

Hotfix Flow in Branching Strategy
description:
Establish a Git Flow Branching Strategy for MES X.0 services and infrastructure.

The idea is to have more change protection on the main branch and to enable a hotfix flow for applying defect fixes.

Resources

  • https://github.com/rollerworks/Release-Management-GuideBook
  • https://www.peerbits.com/blog/complete-guide-to-release-management-in-devops.html
  • https://www.smartsheet.com/sites/default/files/styles/1300px/public/IC-Simple-Release-Management-Template_WORD.webp?itok=TjLZDCyT
  • https://www.apache.org/legal/release-policy.html
  • 01.png (800×523) Gitflow Workflow | Git tutorial | Nulab

Observations

When performing hotfix for #104163 we noticed that:

  • Github flow is mostly sufficient for hotfixing services if we introduce long lived hotfix branches
    • Long lived hotfix branches ?
    • Tagging hotfix branches ?
    • Merge back to main ?
  • Git Flow will be necessary in infra repo to manage hotfixing pro independently of ppr and deploying to ppr independently of pro
While troubleshooting #103894  a need for updating configuration values (noee api key) in production only turned out to be problematic since in order to update the value we need to run the pipeline on PPR then on PRO forcing upgrade of not yet validated application versions.


Seperate ppr and pro versions are now available for container apps, no need for Git Flow Then ?

Conclusion

  • For Microservices projects:
    • Github Flow is sufficient for a hot fixing flow
    • To Hotfix a specific tag:
      1. Create a long lived hotfix branch
      2. Apply + Commit the hotfixes in the hotfix branch
      3. Release the hotfix by tagging the head of the hotfix branch
      4. Create a fix branch from the hotfix branch
      5. Rebase main into the fix branch
      6. Create and complete a PR from the fix branch to main
    • The previous process should ensure that:
      • Hotfix version is released
      • Hotfix is applied in the main line
      • Hotfix Version history is available in the long lived hotfix branch
      • Version tag sequence is preserved in the main branch
  • For infrastructure:
    • Github Flow is sufficient for hotfixing flow
    • ppr and pro versions can be specified independently
    • Extract container tags in a seperate script and user friendly file
    • As a Development Policy infrastructure must remain backwards compatible with all environments

titre: [Analysis] Creating a new API to fetch WKs linked to updates in outbound_delivery
description:
API Name: GetWkByOdAndByPlant 


Purpose: Retrieve relevant WK records associated with the same OD and plant, where their custom status is not equal to "CLOSED" and their status not equal to "504"


Overview:  This endpoint is designed to fetch relevant WK records by matching the OD and plant, where the custom status is not "CLOSED" and the status is not "504".

1. Endpoint:  /get-wk-by-od-plant

2. Method:  Get

3. Parameters:

  • plant: This is a required parameter of type Number, representing the plant identifier. Example: 1355.
  • outbound: This is a required parameter of type String, representing the outbound delivery identifier. Example: "1".
4. Request Example:
  • GET /get-wk-by-od-plant?plant=1355&outbound=1
5. Responses
  • 200 SUCCESS
    • The request was successful, and the relevant WK are returned. Example response
                  {
                    
                  }

  • 404 Not Found
    • No matching WK was found for the specified plant and outbound. Example response:
      • {
      •   "statusCode": 404, 
      •   "message": "No WK found for the specified criteria".
      • "}
  • 500 Internal Server Error
    The server encountered an error while processing the request. Example response:
    • { "statusCode": 500, 
    •   "message": "Failed to retrieve WK by plant and outbound"}
Successful Request:

  • The GET request should retrieve relevant WK when valid plant and outbound values are provided.


Error Scenarios:

  • A 404 Not Found response should be returned if no matching WK exists for the given parameters.
  • A 500 Internal Server Error response should be returned if there is an issue processing the request.

API Name: GetoutboundRelatedtoTPA

Purpose: Retrieve the correct outbound associated to the TPA assignment field

Overview:  This endpoint is designed to fetch outbound relevant for the TPA assignment
1. Endpoint:  /get-outbound-by-assign-tpa
2. Method:  Get

3. Parameters:

plant: This is a required parameter of type Number, representing the plant identifier. Example: 1355.
assingid : This is a required parameter of type number, representing the assgin id tpa 
4. Request Example:
GET /get-outbound-by-assign-tpa?plant=1355&assingid=674
5. Responses
200 SUCCESS
The request was successful, and the relevant outbound is returned. Example response
                  {
                   
                  }

404 Not Found
No matching outbound was found for the specified parameters. Example response:
{
  "statusCode": 404,
  "message": "No outbound found for the specified criteria".
"}
500 Internal Server Error
The server encountered an error while processing the request. Example response:
{ "statusCode": 500,
  "message": "Failed to retrieve outbound by specified criteria "}
Successful Request:

The GET request should retrieve relevant outbound when valid criteria are provided.

Error Scenarios:

A 404 Not Found response should be returned if no matching outbound exists for the given parameters.
A 500 Internal Server Error response should be returned if there is an issue processing the request.

Investigation : multiple api calls for every cause in downtime be
description:
Current Implementation

The current implementation of the findListOfFamilyByPlantAndByCause function supports fetching families associated with a single cause and plant. The function is designed as follows:

  1. Input: Accepts a single plant and cause.
  2. Query: Executes a database query with an equality condition on the cause.
  3. Output: Returns an array of families for the provided cause and plant.
  4. Usage: For multiple causes, this function is called repeatedly in a loop, resulting in multiple database queries.

Identified Problems

  1. Performance Bottleneck:

    • Repeated database queries for each cause significantly increase latency, particularly when the list of causes is large.

  2. Scalability Issues:

    • The current implementation is inefficient and does not scale well with a high number of causes.

  3. Increased Complexity:

    • Multiple API calls and database queries add unnecessary complexity to both the frontend and backend logic.

Proposed Changes

  1. Backend Updates:

    • Modify the findListOfFamilyByPlantAndByCause function to handle an array of causes instead of a single cause.
    • Use the SQL IN clause to fetch families for all causes in a single query:
    • SELECT cause, family FROM cause_family_assign WHERE plant = :plant AND cause IN (:...causes);
    • Update the function signature to accept an array of cause as a parameter.

  2. Frontend Updates:

    • Update API calls to pass an array of causes instead of making individual calls for each cause.
    • Modify logic to handle the updated response structure, which now includes families grouped by cause.
    • Adjust parameters sent to the backend and update the response-handling logic accordingly.


  3. Response Structure:

    • Include the cause in the response to map families to their respective causes.
    • Example of the updated response format:

    • [
        { "cause": "cause1", "family": "familyA" },
        { "cause": "cause1", "family": "familyB" },
        { "cause": "cause2", "family": "familyC" }
      ]

description:
For the TPA/Outbound, handle the updates similarly to the leveling board:

  • Add the relevant topics to the picking-mo (Outbound, TPA).
  • In the picking-mp, implement the handling of updates:
    • Manage the in-memory caches.

For container updates, we will manage the pub/sub as follows:

  • Add the appropriate topic for pub/sub.
  • Publish the event during the production data ingestion:
    • For the Create operation (onEvent c): When creating the container, we will check if the book date and picking order ID are available. If they are, we will publish the message.
    • For the Update operation (onEvent u): We will check if the book date and picking order ID are not null and if the book date is different from the existing (current) book date. If so, we will publish the message.
  • Subscribe at the orchestrator level to the container topic and forward the received message to the processor via the task topic.
  • In the picking processor, we will manage the in-memory queue for the container, similar to how we handle TPA and outbound, and we will append the list of picking orders to the previously fetched ones.

For the alert and reschedule WK history:

we will introduce a new API to fetch picking orders based on the plant and the "updated at" field, then combine this data with alerts (also filtered by plant and "updated at") to return the alert status. Additionally, we will combine it with the reschedule WK history based on the plant and either "updated at" or "created at" fields, ensuring we retrieve the latest picking time (having the max created_at).

We are currently considering two options for this process:

  1. Combining everything into a single query.
  2. Using separate queries, followed by a function to merge the results and return the required information.

We will decide on the best approach during our discussions.

titre: Analyse Cleansing Job by batch Limit
description:
Considering the limitations in TypeORM, I tested the solution using limit or take, but these methods are not supported on DeleteQueryBuilder in TypeORM. Unfortunately, TypeORM's DeleteQueryBuilder does not provide a direct way to limit the number of rows to be deleted in the SQL Server Driver.

To address this, we have two options:

  1. Using TypeORM: Perform two queries for every batch. First, select a list of IDs with the desired batch limit, then delete the rows corresponding to this list of IDs.
  2. Using Raw SQL: Execute a single query directly, such as:However, using raw queries bypasses TypeORM's abstraction layer, which could lead to maintainability challenges. 
typescriptCopy code const query = `DELETE TOP (${limit}) FROM ${tableName} WHERE ${whereClause}`;

After discussing with the team, we decided to move forward with the stocked function via migration, using the same API call to invoke it.
We will use the same cleansing delete query proposed by Jiri in MII, with the batch size configured through Azure App Configuration.
This task will be implemented in the upcoming sprints.

Analysis
description:
1. Create a Scheduled Job

    • Implement a job scheduled to run every 2 minutes that calls the endpoint POST /picking/checkForAlertEscalation/{plant}.
    • This task will be handled by Chedy.

  2. Develop a New API in ORD API (GET)

    • Create an API named wkToBeEscalated in the order api service.
    • This API should accept a plant as input and return a list of WK records that meet the following conditions:
      • customs status is not CLOSED and status is not 504 and status is not 503.
      • An alert is already created (alert created = 1).
      • new_picking_time (column in the rescheduler_wk_history table) is not null.
      • The status of the alert assigned to the WK is not CLOSED.
      • in the select add a field named "alertEscalateLevel": 
        • If new picking time < end preparation time:  Yellow.
        • Else, if new picking time > end preparation time, we will check if new picking time < truck departure time:   Orange.
          • Otherwise, Red.

  3. Create an API in Picking Backend (POST)

    • Implement the endpoint POST /picking/checkForAlertEscalation/{plant} in the picking service.
    • This API should:
      • Take plant as input.
      • Call the wkToBeEscalated API to fetch eligible WK records.
      • Write back to MII and pass to it the list of WKs.

  4. Create a Transaction in MII

    • Develop an MII transaction that takes a list of WK as input and loop on these WKs to update the ALERT_LEVEL of an alert for each WK and manage SMS notifications.
    • Use the transaction SC_DMC/ALERTING/ALERT_CREATION_BACKGROUND/TRANSACTION/ALERT_AUTO_ESCALATE as a reference for SMS sending, especially the sequence Cond_Time_To_much_Inform_Third_Party.s
    • SMS management will be addressed later as a secondary priority.

  5. Enhance Picking UI

    • Add a visual indicator for alerts:
      • If new picking time != null and alert created = 1, the bell icon should be black.
      • If new picking time = null and alert created = 1, the bell icon should be red.
    • Further exploration will determine how to trigger SMS notifications when the bell icon is red (e.g., integrating it with the job or creating a separate API).

  6. Priority and Next Steps

    • The primary focus is implementing the escalation job.
    • SMS notification handling will be addressed in the next priority phase.

Analyse EWM logic
description:
This analysis is divided into three main parts to address the requirements systematically:

  1. Ingestion and New Fields: Focuses on the data ingestion process and the addition of new fields across relevant domains.
  2. UI Development: Covers the creation of new screens for material and work center configurations, as well as enhancements to support mass upload functionality.
  3. Sending Data to Event Hub: Details the logic required to transmit Handling Unit (HU) data to the Event Hub for EWM integration.

The following sections elaborate on each part in detail.

1. Ingestion of New Columns

Objective

Update the schema across relevant domains to support the ingestion of new data fields required for the EWM flow.

Details
  • Fields and Mapping:
    • Work Center
      • Source: HU_DTL_CONTENT table, WORKCENTER column (MII).
      • Target: workcenter field in the container table (PRD domain).
      • Type: NVARCHAR(50).
    • Packaging Material (Optional)
      • Source: HU_DTL_CONTENT table, PI_ID column (MII).
      • Target: packaging_material field in the container table (PRD domain).
      • Type: NVARCHAR(20).
    • EWM Processed Flag
      • New Field: EWM_PROCESSED in the container table (PRD domain).
      • Purpose: Track whether an HU has been sent to EWM (1 = sent, 0 = not sent).
      • Type: boolean
    • WIP_EWM_Enable
      • New Field: WIP_EWM_Enable in the material_dtl table (ORD domain).
      • Purpose: Toggle flow activation at the material level.
      • Type: boolean
    • WIP_EWM_FLOW
      • New Field: WIP_EWM_FLOW in the workcenter table (HRY domain).
      • Purpose: Toggle flow activation at the work center level.
      • Type: boolean

2. UI Development

Objective

Extend the existing Workcenter Config UI template to create screens for material and work center configurations, enabling CRUD operations and mass upload functionality.

Material Maintenance Screen
  • Purpose: Manage the WIP_EWM_Enable field for materials.
  • Fields:
    • Material ID
    • Material Name/Description
    • WIP_EWM_Enable (toggle/checkbox).
  • Features:
    • CRUD operations for individual material configurations.
    • Mass upload support for bulk configuration.
Mass Upload Functionality
  • File Upload Component:
    • Supports CSV files. ( or any other mass upload solution to be discussed later)

3. Sending Data to Event Hub

Objective

Implement the logic to send HU data to the Event Hub topic for EWM consumption.

Steps

  1. Identify Eligible HUs:

    • EWM_PROCESSED = 0
    • WIP_EWM_Enable = 1 for the corresponding material.
    • WIP_EWM_FLOW = 1 for the corresponding work center.
    • HU Type = "P" and Status = "Produced".

  2. Data Mapping:

    • Plant: plant column.
    • HU ID: container_id column.
    • Part Number: material column.
    • HU Quantity: quantity column.
    • Unit of Measure: unit column.
    • Work Center: WORKCENTER 
    • Packaging Material: PI_ID 
    • Flow (optional): default value "WIP". ( correct me if i'm wrong here)
    • Current Storage Location: current_storage_location column.

  3. Event Hub Integration

    • Construct payload with the above data fields.
    • Publish to the designated Event Hub topic.

  4. Update EWM_PROCESSED Field

    • Set to 1 after successful transmission.

  5. Reprocessing Logic

    • If current_storage_location changes for a previously processed HU, reset EWM_PROCESSED to 0.

Analyse + Dev: Switch changelsn Verfication for SQL suery to Redis SDK
description:
As an initial technical analysis, integrating the Redis SDK with the Identity Manager is feasible, and we successfully connected to the development Redis instance.

The implementation of the switching technical solution has been completed and tested locally using a simple test setup.

Key Points to Consider:

  1. Retry Mechanism:

    • Implement a retry mechanism to handle scenarios involving short Redis downtimes or latency issues effectively.
    • I used the Exponential Backoff Retry for the retry Mechanism Thanks to @Chedy MISSAOUI Suggestion

  2. Circuit Breaker Pattern:

    • Evaluate the use of the circuit breaker pattern, potentially leveraging the opossum package to prevent cascading failures.
    • A critical decision point is determining how to proceed when the circuit breaker is open. Options include:
      • Halting queue processing and resuming later.
      • Exploring alternative strategies for managing queue processing.
    • It is advisable to conduct extensive testing with the retry mechanism before deciding whether to adopt the circuit breaker pattern.

  3. Redis Memory Management:

    • As Redis is an in-memory cache, it may evict elements (using the configured eviction policy) when memory capacity is exceeded, even if their TTLs have not yet expired.
    • Current usage during development has not exceeded 300 MB, while the allocated capacity is 1 GB. Nevertheless, this behavior should be monitored and tested under load to ensure stability.

  4. Container Shutdown and TTL Expiration:

    • When a container shuts down, Redis cache entries may expire due to their TTLs.
    • If the container resumes normal operation, it will not automatically handle expired events. It is important to:
      • Decide on an appropriate TTL configuration.
      • Determine whether this behavior is acceptable or requires additional handling to address expired events after a container crash.
  5. Credential Refresh Logic:
    • Refactor the Redis connection to handle the use of Azure tokens with expiry.
    • Implement a robust token refresh logic to avoid credential errors, as encountered in the development environment.

  6. Redis Connection Pool Management:

    • Manage the number of Redis connections effectively to prevent resource exhaustion.
    • Investigate the use of the redis-connection-pool - npm package for connection pooling.
    • Prioritize this for evaluation in upcoming sprint

description:
EWM Gateway Backend Overview: 

The EWM Gateway backend will function similarly to production data ingestion, Dapr server, meaning there will be no explicit router (endpoint) exports.

Event Processing in the Microservice

  • This microservice will handle creation and update events for hu_dtl_content.
  • It will implement mechanisms similar to those in the data ingestion side, including:
    • Queue management
    • Event tracking order management
    • Application shutdown handling
    • Plant consistency checks ...

Data Insertion & Validation Logic

  • Instead of inserting data into SQL, relevant containers will be inserted into Cosmos DB for EWM transmission.
  • The insertion will follow these validation checks:
    1. Check if ewm_flow is set to true at the plant level.
    2. Check if ewm_flow is set to true workcenter level.
    3. Check if ewm_flow is set to true material level.
    4. Ensure the container meets the following criteria:
      • Status: Must be produced
      • Type: Must be P
      • Printed: Must be true
  • If all conditions are met, the container will be:
    • Inserted into Cosmos DB
    • An event will be sent via EWM Event Hub Topic
  • If conditions are not met, no action will be taken.

Update Handling

  • If a container update includes a storage location change, it will:
    • Check the existence of container in cosmos => Update Cosmos DB
    • Trigger an event to the EWM Event Topic
  • If any other field is updated, no action will be taken.
Container Deletion
  • If a container’s status changes from "produced", it will be deleted from Cosmos DB.

Key Points to Validate

  1. Container structure in Cosmos DB
  2. Event tracking management in Cosmos DB
  3. Optimizing EWM flow retrieval
    • Avoid multiple API calls to fetch ewm_flow
    • Explore in-memory caching or other solutions

titre: Analysis for API calls (get ewm_flow information from plant, workcenter, material)
description:
Context:

Our current architecture is designed to process events related to container movements, specifically within the context of EWM system. These events provide information about a plant, workcenter, and material, but the value for the ewm_flow field for each of these entities must be fetched through API calls as it's not present in the event payload. We have two main strategies for caching these values, aimed at minimizing the number of API calls, improving performance, and reducing operational costs.

Proposition 1: Cache Per Event (On-Demand Caching)

Overview:
In this approach, each time an event is received, we will check the cache (Redis for example) for the ewm_flow value associated with the plant, workcenter, and material entities included in the event. If any of these values are missing from the cache, we make an API call to fetch the missing value, cache it, and then proceed with processing the event.

Flow:
Event Processing:
  1. Upon receiving an event (e.g., for containerId = HU123456 with plant = 1146, workcenter = WC001, and material = MAT12345), we first check the cache for ewm_flow for each entity:
      • Check Redis for ewm_flow_plant:1146
      • Check Redis for ewm_flow_workcenter:WC001
      • Check Redis for ewm_flow_material:MAT12345

  2. If all the ewm_flow values are found (i.e., the cache hits for all), proceed with processing the event.
  3. If any of the values are missing, we make API calls to retrieve the ewm_flow values, cache them, and then continue with event processing.
  4. If all ewm_flow values are valid (i.e., true), the event data will be inserted into Cosmos DB and sent to the EventHub.
Redis Cache Structure:
Cache Key:
    Each entity (plant, workcenter, material) will have a separate cache key:
  • ewm_flow_plant:<plant_id>
  • ewm_flow_workcenter:<workcenter_id>
  • ewm_flow_material:<material_id>
Cache Value:
The cache value will be a simple Boolean (true or false), representing whether the entity is in the ewm_flow state.

Example:

  • ewm_flow_plant:1146 true (cached after an API call)
  • ewm_flow_workcenter:WC001 false (cached after an API call)
  • ewm_flow_material:MAT12345 true (cached after an API call)

Proposition 2: Periodic Job to Pre-Populate Cache (Batch Caching)

Overview:
In this approach, a separate scheduled job runs periodically (e.g., every few minutes or hours) to fetch the ewm_flow status for all plant, workcenter, and material entities that might be involved in upcoming events. These values are pre-cached and made available for the system to use when processing events. This reduces the number of API calls during event processing by ensuring the cache is populated with the most current data.

Flow:
Pre-Population Job:
The job queries the relevant tables (e.g., plant, workcenter, material) in the database to fetch the ewm_flow status for each entity. For instance:
  • Fetch all ewm_flow values for plants.
  • Fetch all ewm_flow values for work centers.
  • Fetch all ewm_flow values for materials.
These values are stored in the Redis cache:
  • ewm_flow_plant:<plant_id> <value>
  • ewm_flow_workcenter:<workcenter_id> <value>
  • ewm_flow_material:<material_id> <value>
Event Processing:
When an event arrives, the system simply checks the cache for the required values (as in the first proposition):
  1. Check Redis for ewm_flow_plant:1146
  2. Check Redis for ewm_flow_workcenter:WC001
  3. Check Redis for ewm_flow_material:MAT12345
If all values are present, the event proceeds without any API calls.
If any values are missing, fallback logic could involve making API calls to update the cache.
The event is processed (inserted into Cosmos DB and sent to EventHub) once all values are confirmed to be valid.
Redis Cache Structure:
Cache Key:
The cache structure remains the same as in the first approach, but now the cache is populated before events are processed.
  • ewm_flow_plant:<plant_id>
  • ewm_flow_workcenter:<workcenter_id>
  • ewm_flow_material:<material_id>
