[Design] Aggregator pattern
description:
This email summarizes the two proposed architectures for our high-throughput aggregation service and confirms the decision to move forward with Approach 2: Dapr Virtual Actors.

The selection is driven by the need to achieve maximum horizontal scalability through logical partitioning. It guaranteed isolation (no impact) per plant for our approx 100-200 plants. 

1. Architectural Approach Comparison

We evaluated two distinct approaches for processing events from three topics, performing database checks (for Shop Order events), and ensuring state consistency for the final aggregation logic (Microservice 2).

Approach 1: Shared Cache and Distributed Lock


 

Aspect

Microservice 1 (Aggregator)

Microservice 2 (Ingestion)

Risk/Bottleneck

Concurrency/State

Uses a Shared Redis Cache for aggregation state.

Receives events partitioned by Order ID (4-8 partitions).

Distributed Lock Contention

Consistency

Achieved via an external Distributed Lock (e.g., in Redis) before reading/writing the shared state.

No built-in concurrency control; relies on Order ID partitioning.

High Latency/Overhead

Plant Isolation

Low. All 100+ plants contend for the same centralized lock/cache resource.

Low. Events are grouped by Order, not the more isolated Plant.

Scaling Limit

Conclusion This is a Contention-Based Model where every single event across all plants must queue to acquire the same lock, creating a bottleneck that limits horizontal scalability and increases latency under load.

 

 

Approach 2: Dapr Virtual Actor Model with Redis Stream


 

Aspect

Microservice 1 (Singleton/Ingestion)

Microservice 2 (Ingestion/Actor Host)

Benefit

Data Routing

Parses events, verifies Shop Order data, and publishes to a Redis Stream using the Plant ID as the key/stream name.

Dapr Actors are activated by the client's (Microservice 1's) permanent activation calls, enabling direct actor-to-actor invocation.

Decoupled Messaging

Concurrency/State

N/A

Hosts Dapr Actors, one instance per Plant ID (approx 100-200 Actors). The actor safely encapsulates its plant's state.

Inherent State Encapsulation

Consistency

N/A

Achieved via the Actor's Turn-Based Concurrency Model.

Zero Distributed Lock

Plant Isolation

High. Events are specifically routed to the correct Plant's stream/actor.

Perfect Isolation. Each actor is a single-threaded entity dedicated to its plant.

Linear Scalability

Conclusion This is an Isolation-Based Model that leverages Dapr's power to create concurrent, safe processing streams that are perfectly aligned with our business domain (the Plant).

 

2. Rationale for Selecting Approach 2 🎯

We are choosing Approach 2: Dapr Virtual Actors because it fundamentally aligns with our requirement for Plant Independence and provides a superior model for horizontal scaling by eliminating the most expensive operation in a distributed system: the distributed lock.

A. Eliminating the Bottleneck: The Distributed Lock

The main drawback of Approach 1 is the reliance on a Distributed Lock. As concurrent throughput increases across the 100+ plants, the time spent waiting for the lock (contention) increases non-linearly, severely limiting overall performance.

  • Approach 2 achieves concurrency safety automatically via the Dapr Actor's turn-based model. Because an actor processes all operations for its Plant sequentially (one at a time), its internal state is always consistent, removing the need for an external, high-latency lock.

B. True Plant Independence and Parallelism

The Dapr Actor model makes isolation the primary scaling primitive:

  1. Guaranteed Isolation: By assigning the Plant ID as the Actor ID, Dapr guarantees that all operations for Plant X are handled solely by Actor X. This means high load or a processing failure at Plant A cannot cause a race condition, contention, or performance degradation for Plant B.
  2. Scalable Distribution: The Dapr runtime automatically distributes the approx 100-200 Plant Actors across all replicas of Microservice 2. To increase system throughput, we simply scale the number of Microservice 2 instances horizontally, and Dapr handles the load balancing and re-distribution of the Plant Actors seamlessly.
  3. Redis Stream Role: The use of Redis Streams/PubSub keyed by Plant in Microservice 1 provides an additional benefit: it ensures that all events are grouped by Plant for eventual processing by the correct Actor instance. While the Actor model's isolation handles the concurrency, the stream (or direct invocation/PubSub to the actor) handles the routing of all plant-specific messages.

In summary, Approach 2 replaces a bottlenecked, contention-based design with an isolated, massively parallel, and self-managing architecture perfectly suited for our needs.

Please prepare for a deep dive session next week on the Dapr Actor pattern and its implementation details.

Consequent implications for infrastructure part:

  1. Ingestion layer will be divided into multiple container app: one for managing actors and one for current implementation using dapr binding. In fact, focus for dapr actor retrofit will be for high volume tables
  2. Changes in KEDA rule: initially, it was intended to use KEDA on events queue length. With this new approach, custom KEDA rule based on redis queue length is required

description:
0Analysis : Live Status Screen

Business Context

Gap Leaders currently switch between several dashboards to track their routines and resources.
The goal is to simplify their experience by offering a single “Live Status” view that adapts to their scope.

Main Objective

Create a new Live Status domain that shows the status and KPIs of a selected Gap.
The data will depend on the selected gap, and the view will reuse parts of the ePartBoard system.

Functional Requirements

  1. The Gap Leader can select a Gap:

    • Either passed in the URL (/live-status-ui/:gapId)

    • Or selected manually from a dropdown.

  2. Based on the selected Gap:

    • The system loads related data (Shift Tracking, KPIs, etc.).

    • Data will be fetched via our backend, which invokes ePartBoard APIs.

  3. The ePartBoard view is already displayed on the Live Status screen; it will update dynamically depending on the selected Gap (no redirection).

  4. KPI Bar will be visible again with the final KPI list:

    • First OK part

    • Routines

    • TPM

    • Management Control

    • Shift Delta

    • Alert Status

Technical Approach

🧱 New Domain

We will create a new domain called live-status:

  • Frontend: new page, store, and components.

  • Backend: new service and controller. | live-status-be/* endpoints.

  • API: /live-status-api/* endpoints.

🔁 Backend Behavior

  • The Live Status backend will call the existing ePartBoard API to fetch shift tracking information.

  • For now, the gap–resource mapping will be handled in another story.

🖥️ Frontend Behavior

  • When a Gap is selected:

    • The system requests data from /api/live-status.

    • The embedded ePartBoard section updates with new data.

    • The KPI bar reloads its values.

KPI Bar Note

  • We will reuse the KPI bar that was implemented in the very first version of the ePartBoard. you can find it below : 


  • If the existing version is validated, we will simply make it visible again and adjust its configuration (KPI list to be displayed)

  • If not validated, a new UI design will need to be done before development.

Impact Note:

Since we are adding the KPI bar to the Live Status screen, the overall layout height of the page will change.
This affects:

  • The Shift Tracking Table section, whose height will need adjustment.

  • The KPI widgets, which may require resizing or repositioning to maintain visual balance.
    These adjustments should be reviewed and fine-tuned once the KPI bar is reintroduced.

In the mLean APIs, the team acts as a key input parameter for retrieving KPI-related data. The system architecture requires that all API calls dependent on team context explicitly include this parameter to ensure accurate data resolution and filtering.

2. Implementation Details

  • Parameter Requirement:
    Most mLean API endpoints require the team information as part of their input payload.

  • Integration Approach:
    The team parameter must be passed at the URL level (refer to the attached screenshot example) and subsequently forwarded as an input parameter to the relevant API calls:


  • Data Dependency:
    The KPI values returned by mLean are dynamically computed based on the team parameter provided. Missing or incorrect team information directly impacts the data accuracy and integrity.

3. Error Handling & Fallback Strategy

  • If the team information is missing or undefined, no request should be initiated to mLean, as the API contract enforces the team parameter as mandatory.

  • In such cases, the system should:

    • Skip the API call to prevent unnecessary traffic or errors.

    • Display the KPI value as “Data Unavailable”, indicating the absence of the required input.

1. Objective

The purpose of this API is to display the current status of the first part produced after key production events, such as:

  • Shift start

  • Reference change

  • Line issue

The API should clearly indicate whether the first produced part is OK or Not OK.

description:
endpoint: 

https://psk-mlean.app.corp/gemba-walk-checkpoints-for-board/?team=$value&date_begin=$shiftStartN&date_end=$shiftEndN

inputs:

team (will be taken from the URL),

shift date start,

shift date end,

The KPI displays a fraction representing ControlAssessed / Number of Items​

  • ControlAssessed: Calculated based on the item status, considering only statuses 1, 0, and -2.

  • Number of Items: Includes all statuses — 1, 0, -2, and NULL.

  • General Rule (except for the first hour of a shift):

    • 🟥 RED:

      • There is at least one NOK (Not OK) item in the current hour, or

      • There was at least one NOK item in the previous hour.

    • 🟧 ORANGE:

      • There is at least one Not Assessed item in the previous hour.

    • 🟨 YELLOW:

      • There is at least one Not Assessed item in the current hour.

    • 🟩 GREEN:

      • Only OK and N/A items remain (no NOK and no Not Assessed).


  • Special Case — First Hour of the Shift:

    Since only the current shift is relevant, the previous hour is not considered.

    • 🟥 RED: If there is at least one NOK item in the current hour.

    • 🟨 YELLOW: If there is at least one Not Assessed item in the current hour.

    • 🟩 GREEN: If all items are OK (no NOK, no Not Assessed).

    • The label represents the hour of the shift. For example, during the first hour, we retrieve the statuses associated with label 1 for the various IDs we have. The labels then increment by one for each hour.

      In other words, label 1 always corresponds to the first hour of the current shift, label 2 to the second hour, and so on.

description:
API Overview – Daily Routines KPI

1. Overview

The mLean system provides an API exposing routine data with their ID and status.

The widget displays:

  • The total number of routines (Y) assigned for the selected shift.

  • The number of routines completed (X).

  • The calculated ratio X/Y.

  • The background color of the widget changes dynamically based on completion status and shift timing.

2. Implementation Details

Location: Implemented in epb-be
External Service: mLean API
Endpoint: 

 
 
 
https://psk-mlean.app.corp/daily-round-assessments-for-board

Request Parameters:

Parameter

Description

Format / Example

team

Team identifier, taken from the URL

Mandatory; skip API call if missing

date_begin

Shift start date

yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.000Z

date_end

Shift end date

yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.000Z


Headers:

  • Authorization: Bearer <token>

  • Content-Type: application/json;charset=UTF-8

Behavior:

  • If the team parameter is missing, the API call is skipped, as it is mandatory.

  • If present, the value is passed to the mLean API along with the shift start and end times.

3. Expected Output and KPI Calculation

  • Done routines: status = OK or N/A → count as X

  • Not done routines: any other status

  • Compute ratio:

    X=count of Done routines,Y=total routines (total number of schedule_entry_id)

  • Display: X / Y

  • Background color logic:

    • X = Y → green

    • X < Y → yellow

Output Structure Example: 

 
 
 
{
  "routines": "X/Y",
  "backgroundColor": "green" | "yellow"
}

description:
API Overview – Alerts Levels Status

1. Overview

The Alerts Levels Status widget is displayed in the header section of the Gap Dashboard.

It contains four cells, each representing one alert severity level:

  • Grey

  • Yellow

  • Orange

  • Red

Each cell displays the number of active alerts for its corresponding level.

2. Implementation Details

Location: Implemented across multiple services:

  • order-api

  • plant-hry-api

  • epb-be

2.1. order-api

A new API named getAlertLevelsSummary will be created to retrieve the number of alerts per level (Grey, Yellow, Orange, Red) from the alert table in the ORD domain.

Request Parameters:

Parameter

Description

Required

plantId

Identifier of the plant

✅

workcenterId

Identifier of the workcenter

✅


Filter Condition:

  • Only include alerts where status != 'Closed'

  • If no alerts exist for the level, the count is returned as 0

Output Structure Example: 

 
 
 
{
  "grey": 3,
  "yellow": 1,
  "orange": 0,
  "red": 2
}
2.2. plant-hry-api

A new endpoint named getWorkcenterByResource will be added to retrieve the workcenterId associated with a given resource.

Request Parameters:

Parameter

Description

plantId

Identifier of the plant

resourceId

Identifier of the resource


Output Example: 
 
 
 
{
  "workcenterId": "WC1234"
}
this API will accept one or more resources and for each resource it returns the corresponding workcenter
2.3. epb-be

In epb-be, a new endpoint named getAlertLevelsStatus will be implemented.
This endpoint will:

  1. Invoke getWorkcenterByResource (from plant-hry-api) using plantId and resourceId.

  2. Use the returned workcenterId to call getAlertLevelsSummary (from order-api).

  3. Aggregate and return the final counts of alerts per level.

Request Parameters:

Parameter

Description

Required

plantId

Identifier of the plant

✅

resourceId

Identifier of the resource

✅


Output Structure Example: 

 
 
 
{
  "grey": 3,
  "yellow": 1,
  "orange": 0,
  "red": 2
}

3. Architectural Considerations

  • The epb-be endpoint will aggregate and standardize the data returned by multiple APIs to provide a single, frontend-ready response.

  • Error handling must ensure that if either API fails, the response gracefully defaults to zeros (e.g., "grey":0, "yellow":0, "orange":0, "red":0).

4. Frontend

  • A new KPI widget will be added to the Gap Dashboard header to visualize the alerts per level.

  • The widget will map each color (Grey, Yellow, Orange, Red) to its corresponding count from the API output.

  • If no alerts are present, all four cells will display 0.

description:
API Overview – TPM Status

1. Overview

The TPM Status widget provides visibility into the number of Total Productive Maintenance (TPM) actions to perform during the selected shift for the current gap.

The widget calculates the ratio of successfully performed TPM actions (TpmOk / Total TPM items) based on data retrieved for the given ShiftStart and ShiftEnd time window and the gap perimeter, using the mLean external API.

2. Implementation Details

Location: Implemented in epb-be
External Service: mLean API
Endpoint: 

 
 
 
https://psk-mlean.app.corp/check-point-assessments

Request Parameters:

Parameter

Description

Format / Example

search

Optional search filter

—

created_range_after

Shift start date

yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.000Z

created_range_before

Shift end date

yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.000Z

perimeters

Gap perimeter (from URL)

—

assessment_result

Filter for result codes

0,-2,1

by_current_shift

Only include current shift items

true

q_factor

Include Q factor

false

s_point

Include S point

false

non_conformities_require_action

Include non-conformities requiring action

false

without_actions

Include items without actions

false

without_improvement_ideas

Include items without improvement ideas

false

format

Output format

table

ordering

Sort order

-created


Headers:

  • Authorization: Bearer <token>

  • Content-Type: application/json;charset=UTF-8

3. Expected Output and KPI Calculation

Evaluation of each TPM item:

  • 0 → NOK (Not OK)

  • -2 → Not Assessed

  • Any other value → OK

KPI Calculation:

  • TpmOk = Count of items where result ≠ -2

  • Total items Y = Count of all IDs

  • Displayed Metric = X / Y (e.g., 5/7)

Widget Background Logic:

  • If any NOK (0) → background RED

  • If no NOK, but at least one Not Assessed (-2) → background YELLOW

  • If all items OK → background GREEN

  • In case of data retrieval issues → display “Data unavailable” with gray background

{
  "tpmStatus": "X/Y",
  "backgroundColor": "red|yellow|green|gray"
}

[DEV] Refactor material and customer related APIs
description:
35Summary of API Impacts and Required Refactoring

the following updates are required to handle the introduction of the sap_server column in the related tables and to prevent data inconsistencies across SAP servers.

 

1. Table: material


Three APIs will be impacted:

  • getMaterialById → Must be updated to retrieve data by both material_id and sap_server.
  • updateMaterial → Must be updated to perform updates based on both material_id and sap_server.

Impacted components: master-api, admin-be, admin-ui.

 

2. API: getMaterialEwmFlow


This API retrieves materials for specified plants from material_dtl and performs a join with the material table to fetch materials with ewm_flow = 1.


Current Issue

The API currently joins only on material_id, without considering the sap_server.

This can lead to data conflicts when the same material exists on multiple SAP servers.

Example scenario:

  • MAT1 (EWM = true) linked to FC1 → Plant 1 (non-EWM)
  • MAT1 linked to FC2 → Plant 2 (EWM)

When executing the current getMaterialEwmFlow, the API may incorrectly return MAT1 from FC1 for Plant 2, resulting in cross-server data discrepancies.

 

Required Refactor

  • Add the sap_server field to the material table.
  • Remove the join with material_dtl, since we can now retrieve the plant information directly from the sap_server.
  • Update the API logic to query materials based on the sap_server instead of relying on plant-level joins.
  • Update the function signature to accept the sapServer parameter.

 

Impacted Components

  • nmater-api
  • ewm-gateway-backend

 

3. Table: customer_def (in ship-api)

Three APIs need to be refactored:

  • getCustomerByCode
  • getCustomersByCodes
  • getCustomerDescByCustomerCodes

Impacted components: picking-processor, levelling-processor, and wk-integration-be


Additional note:

The API getCustomerByCode should only return name1 (the customer description) and not the full Customer DTO.

description:
9Goal: Use gateway information from CDC events to determine the correct SAP server and ensure unique record identification.

Steps:

  1. Update the DTO in the fetchPlant function to include sap_server and gateway.
  1. In the function append-and-save-to-cache-queue: 
    • When processing CDC events, call findSapServerByGateway(cdc.__gtw) to retrieve the corresponding SAP server.
    • Apply this logic only when source_table = "MTL".
    • after find sap server do append (mappedData +sap server only in case src=MTL)
  1. Add a new column sap_server in the Material table.
  1. During an insert event (cdc.op = 'c'):

  @OnEvent('material.c')

  • Insert the record in the database.
  • Populate the sap_server column with the retrieved value.
  1. Update logic:

@OnEvent('material.u')

  • Modify the primary key to be a composite key of (material_id, sap_server).
  • Updates will be performed based on this combination to avoid cross-plant data conflicts.
  1. Read logic:

 @OnEvent('material.r')

  • Update the WHERE clause to include sap_server.

titre: [eDashBoard] Dynamic data manage by tool - Review race condition logic between shiftTracking and shiftTrackingStatus
description:
We identified a “Violation of PRIMARY KEY” issue caused by a race condition between the SHIFT_TRACKING and SHIFT_TRACKING_STATUS tables.

Root Cause:
The issue occurred when concurrent processes attempted to insert records simultaneously in both tables, leading to duplicate primary key entries.

Proposed Technical Solution to Prevent the Race Condition:

  • Manage the existing record check using a query builder within an SQL transaction.

  • Apply the following logic:

    1. Select the id from the SHIFT_TRACKING master table based on key columns.

    2. If the id exists, update the corresponding shift_tracking_details record.

    3. If the id does not exist, insert a new header record, then insert the related shift_tracking_details.

  • Retain the logic only within the Shift Details Service to ensure consistency.


Technical solution needs to be reviewed and validated before the implementation.

Note:
A temporary quick fix has already been deployed to catch the error and prevent excessive error logs until the permanent solution is implemented.

NTR Scope:
eDashboard Logsheet – Test the display of data for both “Managed by Tool” and “Managed by Part” cases.

description:
issue 1 et 2 (they are related)

Issue with a cause that does not have cause 3 yet the old list appears, then the causes are updated correctly.

Analysis: 

After reviewing the issue, I found that the root cause is that imageslvl2 is not being stored anywhere. The function that updates classificationTableStore.imagesLvl2 is not resetting or updating the stored data. As a result, when we click on Level 2, the application temporarily displays the previously loaded card before the function finishes updating the new data

titre: [Dev] [live Status] Manage the cache mechanism for the mLean token
[Analysis] [live Status] Manage the cache mechanism for the mLean token
description:
Current Implementation

  • The system requires a POST login request to obtain an authentication token before accessing any mLean endpoints.
  • Currently, there is a single entry point responsible for generating the token and passing it to downstream functions that call various mLean GET endpoints.

Improvement

  • Introduce a Redis-based caching mechanism to prevent requesting a new token on every screen refresh.
  • The goal is to avoid repeated calls to the mLean login endpoint by storing the token in Redis and retrieving it when needed, rather than triggering a new login each time.

Observations from mpx Repositories

  • Redis is not used for token caching in the shared code.
  • The token is always regenerated inside get_mlean_token() without any TTL (Time-To-Live) or persistence.
  • Redis is currently only used to cache GET responses, not authentication tokens.

Token Expiration Behavior

  • Token expiration varies by plant:
    • PISEK (1062): TTL ≈ 1 week.


    • BRAGANCA (1361): TTL ≈ 30 days.


  • This variability suggests that caching tokens with an appropriate TTL could significantly reduce unnecessary login calls.

Proposed Solution

Implement a Redis-based caching mechanism for the authentication token with the following logic:

  1. Store the token and its expiration time in Redis after a successful login.
  2. When a token is requested:
    • Check Redis:
      • If the token exists and its expiration time has not been reached, retrieve it from Redis.
      • If the expiration time is approaching (e.g., within 10 minutes) or has expired, call the mLean login endpoint to refresh the token and update Redis.
  3. Error Handling:
    • In case of any Redis failure (read/write/connection error), do not block the process. Instead, fall back to calling the mLean login endpoint to generate a new token.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

We still have two points to validate with the dedicated team to ensure proper alignment with our solution design:

  1. What is the rationale for caching the GET requests?
  2. What is the update frequency for mLean data (e.g., every minute, every hour, etc.)?

This information is essential for adjusting our technical approach if required.

[Analysis]Remove S_PRODUCTION_ORDER Ingestion
description:
order-di:
-since S_PRODUCTION_ORDER has cacheTreatment enabled in combination with SHOP_ORDER, we need to find a way to ignore the events from SHOP_ORDER which are related to production orders but there is no easy solution to differentiate. Most likely we would have to keeps current logic in which the events will be automatically deleted after ttl expires or maybe from cdc we can filter directly (I dont know how it is configured in debezium and if it possible to maybe JOIN with custom_data and to ignore KANBAN_TYPE != WK)
-we would lose the information from leveling-ui if the WK has any linked production orders that are on hold (the link is from PIK.RELATED_ORDER = WK). This was requested specifically for leveling-ui so business decision might be required to see if it is acceptable to lose this information. The update is performed when a production-order is created or updated and it has a relatedOrder


order-api:
-exposes buffer/getShopOrderList which is calling getFilteredProductionData from production-order.service. The endpoint seems to be used by mesx-wk-integration-backend + possible external calls
-exposes production-order/minSeqNumByPickingOrder/:plant/:relatedOrder which is called by method fetchMinSeqNum from leveling-board-mv-processor (dead end) + possible external calls
-exposes production-order/getGhostByWorkcenters which is called by method getGhostByWorkcenterDto from leveling-board-be (dead end) + possible external calls
-exposes production-order/minSeqNumsByRelatedOrders which is called by method fetchMinSeqNumList from leveling-board-mv-processor + possible external calls
-exposes production-order/workcentersByPickingOrder which is called by method getWorkcentersByPlantAndPickingOrderIds from picking-be + possible external calls
-exposes production-order/run-delete-production-order-procedure which is called by method runDeleteProductionOrderProcedure from picking-be + possible external calls


leveling-board-be:
-mesx-leveling-board-backend/src/order/order.service.ts has method getGhostByWorkcenterDto which executes production-order/getGhostByWorkcenters from order-api but I don't see thie method getGhostByWorkcenterDto being executed anywhere. Linked to US 115598


leveling-board-mv-processor:
-mesx-leveling-board-mv-processor/src/api/order-api.ts has method fetchMinSeqNum which executes production-order/minSeqNumByPickingOrder from order-api but I do not see a direct call of this method fetchMinSeqNum in any app


leveling-board-mv-processor:
-mesx-picking-mv-processor/src/api/order-api.ts has method fetchMinSeqNumList which executes production-order/minSeqNumsByRelatedOrders from order-api and this method fetchMinSeqNumList is executed in case mode is FULL not INCREMENT


picking-be:
-mesx-picking-backend/src/common/api/order.api.ts has method getWorkcentersByPlantAndPickingOrderIds which executes production-order/workcentersByPickingOrder from order-api which is executed by createAlert and automaticAlertCreation
-mesx-picking-backend/src/common/api/order.api.ts has method runDeleteProductionOrderProcedure which executes production-order/run-delete-production-order-procedure from order-api which ends up being exposed as enpoint cleansing/delete-closed-production-orders


Conclusion:
-there are 2 clear functional topics that will be impacted so bussiness decision is needed: red border on leveling-ui + alert creation for SFG workcenter
-there is 1 clear technical topic which will require changes to optimize or we could ignore and let ttl handle the data from SHOP_ORDER table related to production orders.
-there might be hidden third party apps calling the endpoint but I am not aware so I could not asses the impact

[Analysis] Revert functions implemented in user story : 122018
description:
The rule currently implemented is as follows:

  • Start Picking + Advance Picking Duration > now → White (valid)

  • Start Picking + Advance Picking Duration < now → Grey (valid)

  • If Start Preparation < Start Picking < End Preparation and End Preparation > now → Yellow
    (Alert is created automatically)
    OR
    If New Promise Time < End Preparation and End Preparation > now → Yellow

  • If End of Preparation < Start Picking < Truck Departure → Orange
    (Alert is created automatically)
    OR
    If New Promise Time < End Preparation and End Preparation < now < Truck Departure → Orange
    (In this case, New Promise Time may be empty)
    OR
    If End Preparation < New Promise Time < Truck Departure and Truck Departure > now → Orange

  • If Start Picking > Truck Departure → Red (Alert is created automatically)

    • OR Truck Departure < New Promise Time → Red
    OR Truck Departure < now → Red

To revert the logic introduced under this user story 122018, all checks involving the Start Picking time must be removed. Only the rules based on the New Promise Time should remain. The updated rules to be implemented are therefore:

  • Start Picking + Advance Picking Duration > now → White (valid)

  • Start Picking + Advance Picking Duration < now → Grey (valid)

  • If New Promise Time < End Preparation and End Preparation > now → Yellow

  • If New Promise Time < End Preparation and End Preparation < now < Truck Departure → Orange
    (New Promise Time can be empty in this case)

  • If End Preparation < New Promise Time < Truck Departure and Truck Departure > now → Orange

  • If Truck Departure < New Promise Time → Red
    OR
    If Truck Departure < now → Red

Therefore, we need to remove all changes introduced in the referenced commits that apply Start Picking–based checks: 

Commit c2968e1e: Merged PR 93057: manage color code for WK outside TPA schedule interval... - Repos

Commit 617a0434: Merged PR 93371: refactor: enhance preparation time handling in alert and pic... - Repos
Commit f0335ce5: Merged PR 93875: fix: correct picking time comparison logic in alert and vali... - Repos

titre: [Analysis] [Live status] The KPI alert is showing significant number of alerts
description:
Following the point highlighted in this task #137830, here are my findings. The purpose of the automatic alert-closure job is to update the alert status to “Closed” for two cases: alerts that meet the rescheduling rules and alerts linked to WKs that have already been closed. Before triggering the automatic alert closure job, I extracted the list of alerts linked to closed WKs(alert-list-with-closed-wk/:plant), and there are 25324 alerts


and check the alerts with reschedule check (alert-with-rescheduler-check/:plant)there are 523 entries, as shown below: 


I then executed the “close automatic alert” job using Postman, and it returned the following response: 


{
  "statusCode": "SUCCESS",
  "statusMessage": "No row updated",
  "updatedRow": 0
}

I verified again the number of alerts that should be closed, and the count remains unchanged for both:



After further investigation, I found that these alerts no longer exist in MII, which explains why they are not being updated. As a result, each time we run a SELECT TOP 200, the batch always returns the same alerts. I validated this by checking one alert from the beginning, one from the middle, and one from the end of the list, and none of them exist in MII, as shown below:

  • from the beginning:
    • alerts with reschedule check:


    • alerts with closed WK:


  • from the middle:
    • alerts with reschedule check:

    • alerts with closed WK:


  • from the end:
    • alerts with reschedule check:


    • alerts with closed WK: 


Additionally, within the top 200 selected alerts with reschedule check, 13 of them still exist in MII and their status is already Closed. However, in MES they remain with an outdated status. This explains why, when the job runs, there is no action to perform on the MII side for these alerts.


I also suspect that these alerts are not being updated because their alert level is null on the MII side, while the same column is non-nullable in MES. This likely causes issues during ingestion. When I attempted to perform updates on the MII side at the ingestion layer, I found multiple errors such as:
"Error updating Alert: Error: Cannot insert the value NULL into column 'alert_level', table 'ORD.dbo.alert'; column does not allow nulls. UPDATE fails.


It appears that the alerts are correctly updated, closed, and then archived on the MII side, but remain outdated in MES due to ingestion issues. For example, errors such as “Cannot insert the value NULL into column 'alert_level'… UPDATE fails” indicate that some updates are rejected. Similar ingestion errors may also be occurring, preventing MES from receiving the updated alert data.
Another issue is that the WKs are deleted from MES while their corresponding alerts remain, resulting in orphaned alert records.

|BA Design] [eDashBoard] Shift details variant - Comments counter new rule
description:
📌Comments counter new rule

This user story focuses on two aspects:

  1. Notification rules

  2. Calculation of the number of required comments

The logic below applies per resource X and per hour X.

✔️New rules:

  • For Downtime tickets:

For a resource X, add a count into the comment in case there's a ticket in down_time_ticket table in PRD domain and ticket start_date is in the hour X,

and ticket is classified with:

  • cause =5 (Non quality) & cause_1 is NULL & remark is NULL or empty

or 

  • cause =1 (Organizational problem) & cause_1 is NULL & remark is NULL or empty

or

  • cause =4 (Line stoppage) & cause_1 is NULL & remark is NULL or empty

📝 Notes:

Maintain today’s ticket‐status check as follows:

➤From down_time_ticket, consider only tickets status!='DELT'.

➤ For cause =5 (non-quality), continue checking the NON_QUALITY_FLAG field and include only tickets where NON_QUALITY_FLAG = 0.

➤ For cause =6 (not classified) must be ignored, it will not be no more taken into consideration in the comment calculation rule (no comment required).

❗Attention point:

➤ The remark will be taken from the down_time_ticket table in the PRD domain.

  • For Slowdown:

For a resource X, for the hour X, add a count into the comment if there's

  • SD!= 0 and SD = < -5 min or SD >= 5 min in the shift_tracking table in the RSRCE domain

else if 

  • SD! = 0 and SD =< -5 min or SD >= 5 min in the shift_tracking table in the RSRCE domain for hour X, and there is a comment for the same hour
          → then it will not be considered in the comment calculation rule.

else

  • SD = 0 or SD is not =< -5 min or >= 5 min in the shift_tracking table in the RSRCE domain for hour X)

→ then it will not be considered in the comment calculation rule 

❗Attention point:
➤ The comment will be ingested from the new table [CPT_FAURECIA].[dbo].[ACTIONS_ON_PROD].

The needed columns are:
PLANT
MACHINE_ID
FROM_TIMESTAMP
TO_TIMESTAMP
DESCRIPTION

➤ The ingestion should be filtered by the column ACTION, take only the ACTION=HOUR_ACTION

➤ If there's a row for the MACHINE_ID on the HOUR X then consider it as a comment.

titre: [BA Design] [eDashboard] Widget Production - PartS in production at the current moment only
description:
The “Reference in Prod” widget should display only the references that are being produced simultaneously within the same cycle, that is, the ones belonging to the same batch. These are the references the operator is currently producing.

Example:


For managed by part:

  • At moment t, Ref A is being produced → the widget should display Ref A.

  • At moment t+1, after a part change, Ref B is now being produced → the widget should display Ref B only.

  • At moment t+2, after another part change, Ref C is being produced → the widget should display Ref C.

For managed by Tool:

  • At moment t, Ref A&B are being produced → the widget should display Ref A&B.

  • At moment t+1, after a part change, Ref C&D is now being produced → the widget should display Ref C&D only.

  • At moment t+1, after a part change, Ref E is now being produced → the widget should display Ref E only.

→ The retrieve of reference(s) that's currently produced is based on CHANGE_TOOLS table in MII

Rule

  • Retrieve the reference that's in production from the column PARTS on the PLC_ID

  • If have multiple parts produced in different cycle, we can be based on the DATE_TO of the reference to get the most recent produced part: The current part in production is the row whose DATE_TO is set to the = 9999-12-31 23:59:59.000.
  • It's the same for managed by TOOL, just we'll be retrieving a list of rows instead of one row.

❗ Attention point:

  • Ingest the table CHANGE_TOOLS from MII to MES

titre: [Analysis] automatic alert is on the wrong workcenter
description:
Analysis for:
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
case 1: 
1/ SFG flow = 1 and WK with status pik created
expected:
alert is opened on the pik's workcenter: SFG workcenter
Actual:
alert is opened on the FG workcenter ( works correctly for manual alert)
data:  

WKSFG_GTF_TEST_041125_22222222222
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
After reviewing the data, I confirmed that the alert was generated on the correct workcenter, which corresponds to the SFG workcenter. The WK is linked to workcenter WC13223, its PIK is linked to WCM0825, and the alert was correctly created on WCM0825. I also checked the Cosmos records, and the svgWorkcenter for this WK is indeed WCM0825 as shown below:


Please note that the workcenter displayed in the alert screen reflects the WK’s workcenter, not the one where the alert was actually created.

While reproducing the previous scenario, I noticed that no alert was generated for the WK MWK01016_HJ_02120125. Although this WK should be considered late, the job does not pick it up. After analysis, I found that the issue is caused by a filter that only considers shop orders whose planned start date + the advance picking duration of the workcenter is earlier than the current date. Because of this condition, the WK is not treated as late.

In this case, the system is using the advance picking duration of the workcenter assigned to the PIK, which is 480 minutes (8 hours). As a result:

  • Planned start date: 2025-12-03 07:40

    • 8 hours → 2025-12-03 15:40

  • When compared with the current time, the WK is not considered late, so the job ignores it.

This behavior is incorrect. The expected logic is to use the advance picking duration of the WK’s workcenter, not the PIK’s. A separate bug will be opened to address and correct this logic.

To bypass the issue temporarily and validate the scenario, I updated the advance picking duration of the PIK’s workcenter to 0. After this adjustment, the job correctly processed the WK and generated the corresponding alert on the PIK workcenter as shown below: 




=> So, the first case turns out to be a fake bug.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  • case 2:
1/ SFG flow=1 and automatic alert is already opened for WK with status pik in production ( alert is on the SFG workcenter as expected) and then WK status is changed to SFG_PIK_CLOSED

expected:
the workcenter of the existing alert  is automatically  updated from SFG workcenter to FG workcenter
Actual:
the workcenter of the existing alert is not changed ( same behavior for automatic and manual alert)
data:

WKSFG_GTF_TEST_041125_33333333333

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

I attempted to reproduce the issue using this WK MWK01016_HJ_02120125. I updated its status to SFG_PIK_CLOSED from ME Shop Order Maintenance, and the corresponding event was correctly published by the Order Data Ingestion service, as shown below:


I also checked the query “Get Shop Orders with Alerts by Plant and Picking Order IDs”, and the WK is returned as expected:


Next, I executed the related transaction directly on the MII side. The transaction fails with the following error: 


com.sap.xmii.Illuminator.logging.LHException: java.sql.SQLException:
Unable to parse string value for property Param.6 at index 4

The error occurs during execution of this query: 

UPDATE ALERT_LIST
SET ALERT_LIST.WORKCENTER = [Param.1],
    ALERT_LIST.MODIFIED_BY = 'MESXSystem',
    ALERT_LIST.MODIFIED_TIMESTAMP = [Param.4],
    ALERT_LIST.PLC_ID = [Param.5],
    ALERT_LIST.UAP = [Param.6],
    ALERT_LIST.PROD_LINE = [Param.7]
WHERE ALERT_LIST.ALERT_ID IN (
    SELECT TRY_CAST(value AS INT)
    FROM STRING_SPLIT([Param.2], ',')
)
AND ALERT_LIST.PLANT = [Param.3];

The root cause is that UAP_CODE and PROD_LINE are received as ---, as shown below:


When I manually replaced UAP_CODE and PROD_LINE with valid values and retried the update from ME, the transaction executed successfully:



=> So, the second case is caused by incorrect UAP code and production line values stored in MII.

titre: [BA Design] [eDashBoard] Shift details variant - UC ticket interaction
description:
This user story defines the navigation and filtering rules when interacting with the UC ticket counter.

Rule - UC Ticket Classification

1. Single UC Ticket

When the user clicks on the UC ticket counter:

  • The system redirects the user to the Downtime Classification screen in MES


  • The screen is automatically filtered by:

    • Resource

    • Ticket ID

This ensures the user directly accesses the correct ticket classification view.



2. Multiple UC Tickets (Counter > 1)

If more than one UC ticket exists for the selected hour:

  • The system will open the most recent UC ticket, determined by the latest start_date.

  • The MES Downtime Classification screen will also be filtered by:

    • Resource

    • Selected (most recent) Ticket ID

✔️Rules for Ticket Handling, Comments, and Navigation

The rule of display tickets or slowdown is mentioned in this task:

✔️Order of Classification Logic

The system must display items in the following order:

  1. Tickets, sorted by oldest start date first

  2. Slowdowns, shown after all tickets

✔️ Request message:

  • For Ticket insufficiently justified
    • No cause Level 2: Your "cause L1" isn't sufficiently detailed, please provide more info  
    • With Cause L2: Your "cause L1" isn't sufficiently detailed, click to select deeper cause

📝 Notes:

➤ The cause L1 will be dynamic according to the ticket cause in down_time_cause

  • For slowdown
    • Overspeed (negative SD): You have min:sec of Overspeed (max:5min), justify it
    • Slowdown (Positive SD): You have mm:sec  of Slowdown (max:5min), justify it
❗ Attention point:
➤ The text may need to be reviewed by the UX/UI design team to make it more user-friendly.

✔️ Ticket comment logic: 

 If a ticket is classified only with Level 1 (column: cause): in Table down_time_ticket in PRD domain, columns cause_1 & cause_2 are NULL, means that we have 2 possibilities:

Case 1-The sublevels (cause_1 & cause_2) are configured but not used in the first ticket classification:

How to check that?

  • From Table down_time_ticket in the PRD domain

  • Where cause Level 1 = parent_cause (in Table down_time_cause, PRD domain)

  • Return at least one row
➤ In this case, user should go to the downtime classification, classify the ticket with the existing sublevels and can add remark.


Case 2 - The sublevels (cause_1 & cause_2) are not configured:

How to check that?

  • From Table down_time_ticket in the PRD domain

  • Where cause Level 1 = parent_cause (in Table down_time_cause, PRD domain)

  • Doesn’t return any row
➤ In this case, user should go to the downtime classification, add a remark on the ticket.

📝 Notes:

➤ For the SD: display text field to insert remark for the hour

✔️ Interaction with downtime classification:

  • Opening Behavior

    • The Downtime Classification screen must open in the same browser tab as the eDashboard / Live Status for the selected ticket - sublevel 1 of cause assigned (Case 1 mentioned above)

    • The Downtime Classification screen must open in the same browser tab as the eDashboard / Live Status for the selected ticket - level 1 of cause assigned (Case 2 mentioned above)


  • Return Navigation
The system must redirect the user back to the eDashboard / Live Status screen with selected resource when:

    When the user clicks one of the following buttons in the Downtime Classification screen:

    • Cancel

    • Save

    • Previous

    When the user clicks one of the following buttons in the Downtime Split screen:

    • Cancel

    • Save

    • Previous


✔️Rule - Comment counter update after classification:

  • Ticket classification
When the user classifies a ticket with the sublevels in the Downtime Classification screen and clicks the Save button:

    • The comment counter displayed in the eDashboard / Live Status page must be decremented by 1.

    • This decrement reflects that the classification has been successfully processed for the selected ticket.

  • Comment added on a ticket
When the user adds a remark for the ticket in the Downtime Classification screen and clicks the Save button:

    • The comment counter displayed in the eDashboard / Live Status page must be decremented by 1.

    • This decrement reflects that the justification has been successfully processed for the selected ticket.

📝 Notes:

➤ New tickets created by splitting the main ticket should not be included in the comment-calculation rule when they are assigned to causes 1, 4, or 5 and have a defined Level 1.

Therefore, the comment count should only increase (during a split) when new tickets are generated with only Main Level (1,4 or 5) classification.

✔️Comment Synchronization with MII

  • Ticket classification

    • The classification done must be written back to MII 

    • Stored in the table [MES_FAURECIA]. [dbo]. [NON_TRS_TICKET]

  • Comment added on a ticket

    • The remark information must be written back to MII

    • Stored in the REMARK field of [MES_FAURECIA]. [dbo]. [NON_TRS_TICKET]

  • Comment added on an SD 

    • The comment must be written back to MII

    • Stored in [CPT_FAURECIA]. [dbo]. [ACTIONS_ON_PROD]

    • For the selected resource and the corresponding hour

✔️ Drawer Behavior
  • Submitting a ticket
    • If the user justifies the slowdown and clicks Submit
    • And other tickets still require justification
    • The drawer must remain open so the user can continue processing the remaining items.
  • Automatic drawer closing 
    • There are no remaining tickets left to justify, and
    • There are no remaining slowdowns left to justify.
  • Automatic drawer closing by clicking outside
    • If the user clicks anywhere outside the drawer, it should be closed.

description:
While reproducing the case 1 under this task #138183 , I noticed that no alert was generated for the WK MWK01016_HJ_02120125. Although this WK should be considered late, the job does not pick it up. After analysis, I found that the issue is caused by a filter that only considers shop orders whose planned start date + the advance picking duration of the workcenter is earlier than the current date. Because of this condition, the WK is not treated as late.

In this case, the system is using the advance picking duration of the workcenter assigned to the PIK, which is 480 minutes (8 hours). As a result:

  • Planned start date: 2025-12-03 07:40

    • 8 hours → 2025-12-03 15:40

  • When compared with the current time, the WK is not considered late, so the job ignores it.

This behavior is incorrect. The expected logic is to use the advance picking duration of the WK’s workcenter, not the PIK’s.

description:
I reviewed the issue highlighted in this incident, specifically the conversion exception that occurs in the WK table buffer during rescheduling. After an in-depth investigation, I identified the root cause on the MII side. I executed the transaction SC_MES_API/WKINTEGRATION/TRANSACTION/V1/UPDATE_WK_KANBAN directly using the following input:

  • InKanbanRequestXML: 

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<Row>
  <WithdrawalKanban>
    <Action>Rescheduling</Action>
    <Kanban_type>WK</Kanban_type>
    <OrderID>MWK01017_HJ_02120126</OrderID>
    <ProductionLine>WCW00032</ProductionLine>
    <TPANumber/>
    <DeliveryNumber/>
    <MaterialNumber>2630490X</MaterialNumber>
    <StartPickingDateTime>2025-11-18T15:51:34.999</StartPickingDateTime>
    <EndPickingDateTime>2025-11-18T15:50:34.999</EndPickingDateTime>
    <LaunchingDateTime/>
    <StartProductionDateTime/>
    <EndProductionDateTime/>
    <Quantity>12</Quantity>
    <Customer/>
    <ProductionLineUPstream/>
    <UpstreamMaterial/>
    <SourceLocation>OU11</SourceLocation>
    <DestinationLocation>OU12</DestinationLocation>
    <Batch>32537900005</Batch>
    <bbbMode>
      <bbbMode>100</bbbMode>
      <materialGroup>AUTOO</materialGroup>
    </bbbMode>
  </WithdrawalKanban>
</Row>

  • InPlant: 1062

The transaction fails and returns the output shown below:




Further analysis indicates that the failure originates from the transaction SC_MES_API/WKINTEGRATION/TRANSACTION/V1/CHECK_WK_FIELDS, specifically during the time-conversion step:




The underlying issue is that the query SC_MES_API/WKINTEGRATION/QUERY/SELECT_KANBAN_DETAILS returns START_PRODUCTION and END_PRODUCTION as TimeUnavailable, causing the conversion error:


These values correspond to the SCHEDULED_START_DATE(START_PRODUCTION) and SCHEDULED_COMP_DATE (END_PRODUCTION) columns in SHOP_ORDER, both of which are NULL:


Based on this, the problem appears to be data-related and requires validation.

titre: [Buffer Monitoring] When updating the WK with a new start picking date or customer, the update is done successfully in MII and MES, but the NEO status in the buffer is still empty.
description:
During the rescheduling process within WK Integration, the neoStatus field remains null. After conducting a detailed investigation and analysis across both the Order Ingestion service and the WK Integration backend services, it was observed that the rescheduling action does not trigger any update in MII. ( I don't know if it should do that or not at first place)

As a result, the ingestion process does not occur as expected. This behavior suggests a potential issue with the transaction in MII itself. But when a record was manually updated directly in the database MII ( I updated the TPA_NUMBER field) in that case, the neoStatus field in the buffer table was successfully updated for the rows having the same order_id.

Conclusion: The root cause appears to be a transactional problem in the rescheduling workflow and writeback to MII, preventing the expected update of neoStatus and subsequent ingestion in MII.

description:
While investigating the issue related to missing data in production for plant 1062, we identified several recurring errors in the resource ingestion logs. 

Specifically, we observed repeated database connection failures (Unable to connect to the database. Retrying...) and multiple EventHub consumer errors indicating that new receivers with the same epoch were being created, causing the current receivers to be disconnected: "also many errors linked to error loading from files for queue: "Error loading queue from files for queue shiftTracking: Expected double-quoted property name in JSON at position 524288"

These errors occurred across both the ShiftTracking and ShiftTrackingStatus ingestion services and ultimately led to container restarts.

Further analysis showed that data ingestion had actually stopped on 2025-12-06 at 21:37:54:


After a deeper investigation, we confirmed that no new events from plant 1062 were reaching EventHub. This was caused by the site's migration to SP22 during the previous weekend, after which CDC events were no longer being pushed to MES and the old server became unreachable:




As a corrective action, 9tech updated the connector configuration to restore the flow of data. A snapshot was also executed, and the data is now correctly displayed in MES.

description:
mesx-plant-hierarchy-data-ingestion:
-"Violation of PRIMARY KEY" errors found for workcenter and resource but on 2nd December and events can no longer be investigated from this date

-best guest (based on the fact that I faced the same error when testing locally the solution of removing cache for workcenter ingestion) is a race condition between either: 1 update event and 1 create event (I think this is the problem here due to message error which is linked to create event) OR between 2 update events (this was the issue when I tested locally, 2 update events for same object processed concurrently when the object did not exist in database so update logic tried to create the object) OR some other combination where read events are involved with other type of events (we have same logic on read events as for update events). Current logic of using typeorm.save() method and a typeorm.transaction(typeorm.findone() + typeorm.create() + typeorm.save()) does not avoid the race condition. Due to bad timing 2 parallel executions can see that the object does not exist in db right now and both executions will try to insert.
-I propose to replace current logic with the typeorm.upsert() method --> ok for me.(already in place for workcenter case but did not reach production server) which handles this race condition internally. The downside is that .upsert() method is more rudimentary/basic so some of the typeorm/sql flows are not triggered by this method. One flow is that concerning the decorators added to datetime columns which results in the value of updatedAt not being modified automatically when the upsert behaves as an update (if the upsert performs an insert, it works OK). For the workcenter changes I handled this by manually providing current timestamp for the updatedAt column
mesx-shipment-data-ingestion:
-"Violation of PRIMARY KEY" errors found for outboundDeliveryDtl and outboundDelivery are quite frequent. Prod is using 1.6.1 version which has a different logic compared to last version on main. Logic from 1.6.1 has a case when it also tries to save outboundDelivery when an outboundDeliveryDtl event is processed. This auto generated outboundDelivery event is most likely interfering with the real outboundDelivery event due to bad timing of events arrival for processing
-I propose to update last version from main to use typeorm.upsert() method --> ok for me.as well to avoid interference and failure

mesx-master-data-ingestion:
-"... not found" errors are frequent for MaterialService, MaterialStorageLocationService but all modules have the same issues since they have same logic replicated. The update fails with this errors if the object is not already stored in database. The logic for create and read events use the same problematic methods which have the race condition issue which could explain why the materials do not exist in db (the create/read events could have failed with PRIMARY KEY violation) or even simpler explanation the snapshot was not performed correctly or at all.
-I propose we switch to typeorm.upsert() method --> ok for me.which will handle both race condition issues and the case when an update event is received for an object that was not yet created in mesx.

mesx-leveling-board-mv-processor:
-For case of getCustomersByCodesList error, the issue comes from the fact that in ship-api, the endpoint ship-api/customer/getCustomersByCodesList throws a NotFoundException exception which reaches lvl-mp and also logs an error message in ship-api container. This happens if we call the endpoint with empty list of customers [] or with customers that do not exist in mesx. ship-di has the same race condition issue which can result in some data being skipped
-I propose to eliminate the errors (makes most sense to me since we can have WKs without customer) or to move them to functional area inside lvl-mp app and to switch to typeorm.upsert() method in ship-di --> ok for me.( error to be removed)
-For OrderApi 2 errors:
-fetchWKByPlantAndOutbound: thrown because order-api/picking-order/get-wk-by-od-plant?plant=1355&outbound=0080992989' does not find any WKs linked to the specified OD. This error appears when lvl-mp received a notification that an OD or a TPA was modified so all related WKs need to be updated
-I propose we eliminate this log since it has no added value and also modify the endpoint from order-api to not throw an error anymore --> ok for me.
-fetchOrdersByDate: socket hung up (already investigated by Nassim)
-For fetchSebango error: error appears because the endpoint /material-dtl/getMaterialDtlById/:plant/:materialId is called for null material due to Buffer orders with material_number null being retrieved. In Buffer table we have also the orders for action_type Deletion which have minimal details and material_number is missing.
-I propose we modify endpoint from order-api to exclude orders integrated for Deletion--> to be confimred by @JEBALI Hiba

description:
Backend:

In the epb-be repos, introduce a new function named getManagementControlDetails. This function will accept the following parameters:

  • plant: string

  • shiftStartDate: string

  • shiftEndDate: string

  • team: string

  • timezone: string

Within this function, retrieve the mLean token by calling getMleanToken, then invoke the endpoint: 

/mlean/api/v1/gemba-walk-checkpoints-for-board

After receiving the API response, apply the required transformations so that only the fields needed by the frontend are preserved. For the status, use the value returned by the API and convert it into a color-coded status:

StatusColorMeaning
1 Green Status OK
0 Red Status NOK
≠ 0 and status ≠ -1
Red Not assessed considered as NOK

For example, given this API response: 

{
  "id": 401,
  "checkpoint_description": "CP - AIRGAP - TPM - Control of diameter of Lambda spater cover",
  "checkpoint_results": [
    {
      "assessment_id": 409630,
      "status": 1,
      "label": "OK",
      "schedule_entry_id": 409630,
      "schedule_id": 32510,
      "has_improvement_drivers": false
    }
  ],
  "checkpoint_category_color": "#c414db",
  "checkpoint_category_description": "Unofficial claims"
}

The transformed output should be: 

{
  "id": 401,
  "checkpoint_description": "CP - AIRGAP - TPM - Control of diameter of Lambda spater cover",
  "labelIsDashorOK": true,
  "checkpoint_results": [
    {
      "status": "green",
      "label": "OK"
    }
  ],
  "checkpoint_category_color": "#c414db",
  "checkpoint_category_description": "Unofficial claims"
}

The field labelIsDashorOK should be set to true when the label is "-" or "OK"; otherwise it should be false.

titre: [eDashboard] [Analysis] Data is not displayed for shift hours that do not start at 00 minutes
description:
Shift hour display issue – analysis

The problem

  • Symptom: Shift table shows empty rows when the shift starts at times like 13:30 instead of 13:00.

  • Backend state: Production data exists and is returned by the API, but the UI fails to map and display it.

Why it happens

  • Mismatch between API and UI time formats:

    • API: "dateHourFrom": "2025-12-11T14:30:00.000"

    • UI: Expected "14:00" because of hardcoded logic.

  • Result: Keys didn’t match → lookup failed → rows appeared empty.

Root cause

  • expectedHours.push(`${current.getHours().toString().padStart(2, '0')}:00`);    

  • Hardcoded minutes: The hour list generator in the UI was fixed to use “:00” minutes for all hours.

  • Edge case failure: Works for on-the-hour shifts (e.g., 14:00) but breaks for starts like 13:30, 14:30, etc.

  • View change (missed nuance):

    • Originally: Dashboard showed only hours that had data (sparse view).

    • Now: Dashboard shows all hours in the shift (full view), which requires generating a complete hour list.

    • Bug: The generation logic didn’t preserve the actual start/end times, causing the first hour to be rounded to “:00” and keys to misalign.

  • Analogy: Like searching a contact by exact spelling — if it doesn’t match, you won’t find it.

The fix

  • Hour generation update:

    • First hour: Use the actual shift start time with hh:mm (e.g., 13:30).

    • Middle hours: Normalize to “:00” for consistency.

  • Outcome: API keys and UI labels now align; data displays correctly.

Secure APIs
description:
wiki link New page - Wiki - Overview
We decided to introduce a middleware in the Auth Proxy responsible for validating whether the authenticated user is authorized to access the requested plant.

This middleware will:

  • Extract the plant identifier from the request query parameter

  • Verify that the plant is included in the list of plants assigned to the user (from token claims or identity provider)

  • Allow the request to proceed only if the plant is authorized

API Standardization Rule

To make this middleware reliable and generic, we defined the following rule:

All APIs that are scoped by plant must expose the plant as a query parameter: 

 
 
 
?plant=plantId

  • The plant parameter represents authorization scope, not resource identity

  • Resource identifiers (e.g. workcenterId, orderId, kpiName) remain in the path

  • Path-based plant identifiers (/{plant}, /{plantId}) are deprecated

Middleware Behavior

The Auth Proxy middleware will follow this logic:

  1. Check for plant query parameter

    • If the parameter exists:

      • Validate that the user is authorized for this plant

      • Reject the request with 403 Forbidden if access is not allowed

    • If the parameter does not exist:

      • No plant-level authorization check is performed

      • The request is forwarded as-is

  2. Authorization Source

    • User’s allowed plants are retrieved from:

      • JWT claims, or

      • Identity Provider (e.g. PingFederate)

titre: [eDashboard] [Analysis] The Ref in prod is shown unavailable for the Widget 'Reference in prod'
description:
🛠 Problem Analysis: Reference Widget Timezone Misalignment

📌 Context

  • The Reference widget in production is designed to display the material being produced in the current hour.

  • Backend services correctly provide the payload with the required data.

  • Despite this, the widget sometimes shows “Unavailable”, even though data exists.

🔍 Root Cause

  • The frontend logic determines the current hour using the system datetime (local machine/server timezone).

  • Plants operate in different timezones (e.g., UTC), but the system may run in another timezone (e.g., UTC+1).

  • This mismatch causes the widget to look for data in the wrong hour slot:

    • Example:

      • Plant timezone = UTC

      • System timezone = UTC+1

      • At 10:00 UTC, the plant has data.

      • The system interprets it as 11:00 UTC+1, so the widget fails to find data for the “current hour.”

⚠️ Impact

  • Data availability issue: Widget incorrectly shows “Unavailable” despite valid backend payload.

✅ Resolution Strategy

  1. Timezone Alignment

    • Replace system datetime usage with plant timezone datetime when determining the current hour.

Plant timezone of 1665 : UTC

[Analysis] Change eventhub partition key for shift_tracking topics
description:
As part of our ingestion optimization for SHIFT_TRACKING and SHIFT_TRACKING_STATUS, I’d like to share with you an update regarding partition key options and their impact on performance and real-time dashboard latency.

Current Situation

  • Both tables currently use plant as the partition key.
  • This causes hot partitions for high-volume plants, limiting ingestion throughput and slowing replica processing.

Option 1: plant:plc_id:shift_start_date

Limitation:

  • SHIFT_TRACKING_STATUS does not have shift_start_date, so we cannot apply this key consistently across both streams.
  • Using different partition keys will increase processing speed for SHIFT_TRACKING due to higher partition distribution and possible parallel replica execution, but in contrast, SHIFT_TRACKING_STATUS will remain slower, leading to uneven latency in receiving both KPIs on the real-time dashboard.

Recommended Approach

Option 2: plant:plc_id

  • Available in both tables → consistent partitioning.
  • Improves distribution across Event Hub partitions compared to plant-only.
  • Preserves ordering per PLC, which is sufficient for most dashboards.
  • Minimal consumer changes.

Optional Enhancement

Option 3: plant:plc_id:date_hour_from

  • Further improves distribution by adding time granularity.
  • Reduces risk of hot partitions for high-volume PLCs.
  • Drawbacks:
    • Ordering guaranteed only within hour buckets.

Summary

Our recommendation is to switch both tables to plant:plc_id for balanced performance.

[eDashBoard] Two Parts in Production
description:
As operator, I want to know current Parts/references which are in production, machine can be producing several different parts in one cycle.
Then having the widget displaying references description or code, limited to 4. which are currently in production will be helpful to know which prod is ongoing. 

This user story is the following of : User Story 129930: [eDashBoard] Widget Production - Part in production, we are speaking about the same widget, simply we manage there a logic more advanced.

Parts in production widget can be alone or complementary to Tool in production

Resource managed by Part :

Only the part actually produced during a cycle should be taken into account.

Resource managed by Tool:
Only the reference actually produced during a cycle should be taken into account,
or
References produced simultaneously within the same cycle (belonging to the same batch) should be considered.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The “Reference in Prod” widget should display only the references that are being produced simultaneously within the same cycle, that is, the ones belonging to the same batch. These are the references the operator is currently producing.

The retrieve of reference(s) that's currently produced is based on CHANGE_TOOLS table in MII

Rule

  • Retrieve the reference that's in production from the column PARTS on the PLC_ID

  • If have multiple parts produced in different cycle, we can be based on the DATE_TO of the reference to get the most recent produced part: The current part in production is the row whose DATE_TO is set to the = 9999-12-31 23:59:59.000.
  • It's the same for managed by TOOL, just we'll be retrieving a list of rows instead of one row.

❗ Attention point: Ingest the table CHANGE_TOOLS from MII to MES

[Analysis] Batch Mangement for Ingestion - RSRCE- MaxBatchSize
description:
Technical Analysis Approach

The analysis will be split into two main parts:

Part 1 – Subscription by Batch 

The current batch subscription configuration includes a parameter that can be adjusted. As shown below, this parameter must be updated to 100 (for example).


As part of the analysis, we will first measure the data integration time before any change, specifically:

  • Time taken for data to be integrated into MII

  • Time taken for data to be propagated and available in MES

Once the baseline metrics are collected, we will update the parameter value to 100 and closely monitor:

  • Whether the data is correctly inserted into MES

  • The impact of the change on integration time on the MES side

  • Any potential side effects or regressions introduced by this configuration change

If the results are satisfactory and no negative impact is observed, the maxBatchSize parameter will be externalized into the application configuration, and the application will be updated to read this value from the config rather than using a hardcoded value.

Part 2 – Processing Layer (Deep Analysis Required)
This part requires a deeper technical investigation focused on the database layer, specifically:

  • Analysis of the bulk insert strategy

  • Evaluation of database-side performance, locking, and transactional behavior

At this stage, we will start with Part 1.

[Dev-Fix] [eDashboard] Fix the issue with target & prod data retrieval in the shift tracking
description:
Technical Analysis – Root Cause & Fix

Issue
The initial query joined the change_tools table using a LEFT JOIN directly into an hourly aggregation query.
Because change_tools can contain multiple rows per plant and resource, this join created a many-to-one relationship with shift_tracking_details.

As a result, each detail row was duplicated for every matching change_tools row, causing:

  • Inflated SUM(targetQty) and SUM(realQty) values

  • Incorrect production metrics

  • Misleading aggregated results despite correct raw data

This behavior is expected in SQL and occurs before the GROUP BY is applied.

Root Cause
Aggregations (SUM, STRING_AGG) were executed after a join that multiplied rows.
LEFT JOIN does not prevent row multiplication; it only preserves unmatched rows.

Fix – Solution (Implemented)
The aggregation of change_tools (tools and materials) was moved to a separate query, executed once per (plant, resource).

  • Hourly production is calculated without joining change_tools

  • Tools and materials are aggregated independently

  • Results are merged at the application level

  • Duplicate tool/material values are removed explicitly

Result

  • ✔ Correct target and production values

  • ✔ No row multiplication

Key Rule Applied

Data that does not depend on the grouping dimension must not be joined into an aggregation query.

[ANALYSIS] [Downtime Classification] Split cannot be done for tickets without an end date
description:
Root Cause

The Split screen uses a custom date filter dateAfterFirstTicket() to enable or disable days in the calendar: 

<q-date :options="dateAfterFirstTicket" />

This function always computes both:

  • a minimum date from the ticket start date, and

  • a maximum date from ticket2EndDate.

Issue with Missing End Date

When the original ticket has no end date, ticket2EndDate.value is an empty string ('').

As a result, the following logic is executed: 

ticket2EndDate.value.split('-') // → ['']
new Date('undefined-undefined-') // → Invalid Date

Because the computed max date is invalid, the comparison: 

selected <= max

always evaluates to false.

Impact

  • Every date is rejected by the filter.

  • The date picker renders visually, but no date can be selected.

  • This matches the behavior shown in “Pasted Image 2”.

Why the Time Picker Also Looked Broken

if Plant is configured with only Level 1 causes.

titre: [Analysis] Batch Mangement for Ingestion - RSRCE- MaxBatchSize
description:
Mid-batch checkpointing: check the PR attached
  • Checkpoint every N events (e.g., every 10 events)
  • If the service crashes after processing 95 events, only the last 5 events need reprocessing (since last checkpoint was at event 90)
This will be configurable via environment variables: one to enable or disable mid-batch checkpointing, and another to define the checkpointing interval (for example, every 10 events).

Error 502 + Error of checkpointing:

The observed RestError 502 during Event Hub initialization and the Error updating checkpoint are expected transient failure patterns in Azure Container Apps, not application defects. Container Apps amplify these behaviors due to cold starts, delayed outbound networking, frequent scaling, and pod eviction.

The 502 error occurs when the Event Hub SDK makes control-plane or AMQP calls before network readiness or during Event Hub gateway rebalancing. Without retries on initialization, a single transient infrastructure failure can crash the container.

Checkpoint update failures are tightly coupled to long batch processing (maxBatchSize) and auto-scaling. Extended processing increases the risk of lease expiration, while scale-out can lead to multiple replicas competing for partition ownership, causing rejected checkpoint writes by design.

These errors often appear together during scale or restart events and may result in duplicate event processing. They are normal in Container Apps but must be handled through retryable initialization, smaller or time-based checkpointing, idempotent consumers, and graceful shutdown logic to ensure resilience and correctness.


maxBatchSize Impact

Parallel Processing (Most Beneficial Case)

Benefits

  • Higher throughput due to fewer Event Hub fetch calls and reduced SDK/network overhead

  • Better CPU utilization, as workers stay busy instead of waiting on receive cycles

  • Improved burst handling, allowing faster catch-up during backlog scenarios

  • More efficient checkpointing, with fewer checkpoint writes to storage

Drawbacks / Risks

  • Increased memory usage if batches are too large

  • Longer processing windows can still risk lease expiration if concurrency is uncontrolled

  • Requires safe checkpointing (time- or count-based) to limit replay size

Sequential Processing (Limited Benefit, Higher Risk)

Benefits

  • Minor gains only for very lightweight and fast event processing

  • Can slightly reduce receive overhead in trivial pipelines

Drawbacks

  • High memory pressure, as the full batch is held in memory

  • Checkpoint delays, leading to large replays on crash or eviction

  • Higher end-to-end latency, especially for the last events in a batch

  • Error amplification, where a single failure blocks checkpointing for many events

Summary

👉 Increasing maxBatchSize is most effective in parallel, async processing, where it improves throughput, reduces SDK overhead, and better absorbs traffic bursts.

👉 In sequential processing, benefits are minimal and risks are higher (memory pressure, latency, replay size), so batch size should remain conservative.

[BA Design] eDashBoard] Shift details V2 - ShiftTracking 8h+
description:
📌 Shift details V2 - ShiftTracking 8h+

✔️Current Behavior

The eDashboard / Live Status display is managed for shifts lasting up to 8 hours.

Requirement: All shift hours are displayed in a single view, with no manual scrolling required.

✔️Enhancement

Extend the eDashboard / Live Status display to support shifts longer than 8 hours (ex 12-hour shifts).


Requirements:

  • Always display the most recent 8 hours of the shift.

  • No manual scrolling should be required to view the current shift information.

  • No screen resizing: The information style and size remain unchanged. This approach avoids managing multiple responsive sizes and eliminates the need for four different screen versions for 9- to 12-hour shifts.

Proposed solution:

  • Automatic scrolling should be existing to view the last 8h running hour of the current shift

  • Manual scroll is possible: User can scroll down or up to see the previous or next shift information such the next planned stoppages. 
  • After inactivity time of 15s, the screen should be readjusted back automatically to display the last running hours.
Example: Shift of 12 hours: from H00h to H12
  • From 00:00 to 08:00, the view is aligned to display the first 8 hours (H00 to H08).
    We can scroll to see future planned stoppages for example, but after a period of inactivity (15s), the display automatically returns to H00 to H08.

  • At 09:00 (start of the 10th hour), the view automatically adjusts to show from H01 to H09.
    We can scroll up or down, the display will realign to 01–09 after inactivity.

  • At 10:00 (start of the 11th hour), the view automatically adjusts to show from H02 to H10.
    We can scroll up or down, the display will again realign after inactivity to show the latest hours.

  • During the last hour, the view is aligned to show from H03 to H11.
    We can scroll up, after inactivity the display returns to 03–11.

  • The final time slot ends at 11:59:59. At 12:00:00, a new shift starts.

  • Alert Status (from alert)

Epartboard Backend (epb-be)

Create a new function named getAlertByResourcesDetails.

This function will:

  1. Call getAlertByWorkcentersDetails to retrieve alert and picking-order data.

  2. Call getWorkcentersByListId (from plt-hry-api) to retrieve:

    • Workcenter Description (from plt-hry)

[Live Status] Adjust the calculation rule for the management control KPI
[Dev-Fix] [Live Status] Adjust the calculation rule for the management control KPI
description:
Initially, our understanding of the MLean API output was that the assessment is performed progressively during the shift, meaning that at a given point in time only the labels corresponding to the current shift hour would be available (e.g., during the second hour, only label 2 would be present not the ones for the future next hours). Based on this assumption, the implemented logic retrieves the last available label and performs the KPI calculation exclusively using that label.

However, during data analysis and testing, we observed that the assessment response actually contains all shift hours, and that their assessment statuses are updated progressively throughout the shift. In our current scenario, we are in the 6th hour of the shift, so the expected KPI value is 4/7. Instead, the KPI is currently displayed as 1/7.

This incorrect value is caused by the existing logic relying on label 8. Since none of the items with this label have a status of 1, 0, or -2 (all label 8 entries are marked as red, with only one item marked as OK), the calculation results in 1/7.


To address this issue, the logic has been enhanced to:

  • Base the calculation on the current shift hour number rather than the last label

  • Match the shift hour number with the corresponding labels

  • Preserve the existing behavior for OK and negative statuses

  • Preserve the existing behavior for the total number of items representing all assessment IDs

This adjustment ensures that the KPI accurately reflects the progressive nature of the assessment during the shift.
