titre: [BA Design] [eDashBoard] Widget Production - Tool in production
description:
📌[eDashBoard] Widget Production - Tool in production

✔️ Purpose

Create a new widget to display the current tool in production.

In the current production environment, several situations exist:

  • Multiple tools can be used to produce the same reference.

  • A single tool can produce multiple references.

  • A tool can produce only one reference.

Depending on how the resource is managed, the available production information differs.

✔️ Resource Management Types

  • Resource managed by Part

    • Only the reference in production is available.

    • No tool information is managed or displayed.

  • Resource managed by Tool

    • Both the tool information and the reference(s) in production are available.

✔️ Enhancement points:

- New Widget Creation

  • Widget name: TOOL IN PRODUCTION

  • Widget content: Tool ID

- Widget Display Rules

  • Case 1: Resource Managed by Part

Behavior: Do not Display the TOOL IN PRODUCTION widget.

  • How?

    • Query the resource table in the HRY domain using the resource_id.
    • If the managed_by column = 'PART', the resource is managed by Part.

  • Case 2: Resource Managed by Tool

Behavior: Display the TOOL IN PRODUCTION widget.

  • How?

    • Query the resource table in the HRY domain using the resource_id.
    • If the managed_by column = 'TOOL', the resource is managed by Tool.
Tool retrieval information: Only the tool currently in use must be displayed.

  • How?

    • The current tool is retrieved from the change_tools table in MES.

    • Filter records by resource_id.
    • The current tool in production corresponds to the row where:  DATE_TO = '9999-12-31 23:59:59.000'

    • The tool identifier is retrieved from the tool_id column of that row.



✔️UI UX Design: 

The widget design should be defined in the UI UX design task.

[Analysis] Identify and propose fine tuning for expensive queries identified in ORD and PRD domain
description:
Follow up action following Architect feedback: Jacque KANG

"Upon checking the logs of the container apps in production over the last seven days, I've only found connection errors related to Azure SQL. Based on this, I find it unlikely that the issue is related to SNAT exhaustion. If it were, we would be experiencing similar errors while connecting to other resources like Event Hub, Redis, CosmosDB, etc.

 

I've observed a very high throughput for I/O data reaching our MESX SQL databases, averaging around 40MB per minute and sometimes spiking up to 160MB per minute: View In Metrics Explorer

Additionally, the "query performance insight" of certain SQL databases highlights some long-running queries, which can take over 20 seconds to complete:

  • https://portal.azure.com/#@Faurecia.onmicrosoft.com/resource/subscriptions/3653cf3e-2fef-4062-8ba3-81ffdcdf2fcc/resourceGroups/rg-gptmpxp01-pro-euw-mes-01/providers/Microsoft.Sql/servers/sql-gptmpxp01-euw-pro-mes-01/databases/PRD/queryPerformanceInsight
  • https://portal.azure.com/#@Faurecia.onmicrosoft.com/resource/subscriptions/3653cf3e-2fef-4062-8ba3-81ffdcdf2fcc/resourceGroups/rg-gptmpxp01-pro-euw-mes-01/providers/Microsoft.Sql/servers/sql-gptmpxp01-euw-pro-mes-01/databases/ORD/queryPerformanceInsight

 

Given these observations, I suspect that the error may be related to an excessive number of connections to the SQL databases, compounded by these long-running queries. My recommendation is to try to reduce or optimize the SQL queries to alleviate this issue."

StatusColorMeaning

This information can be displayed either on hover or directly on the item, depending on the chosen UI/UX design.

[ANALASIS] [TPA picking screen] Filter is not working correctly
description:
The backend builds a Cosmos SQL query by concatenating filter strings with AND 
The old “Rescheduled = No” filter string contained an OR without parentheses 



In SQL/Cosmos, AND has higher precedence than OR, so a WHERE clause like:
... AND alertCreated=true AND A OR B
is evaluated as:
(... AND alertCreated=true AND A) OR B

This lets rows matching B pass even when alertCreated=true is false → you see all results .
Business-rule mismatch: the expected meaning of “Rescheduled” is tied to newPromiseTime (null vs not null), but the original backend implementation used reschedulerWkHistories length, which doesn’t reliably represent the UI meaning.

Fix bug by ensuring the rescheduled “No” condition is grouped with parentheses so it can’t override other AND filters .

Aligned “Rescheduled” semantics to your expectation:
Rescheduled = Yes → newPromiseTime is defined and not null
Rescheduled = No → newPromiseTime is null or missing

Planned Approach: Analysis for “In Testing” Marker

  • Purpose: Indicates whether the screen is fully validated (true) or still under testing (false).

  • Expose the isValidated flag in the menu payload.

  • Notes:

    • Update API mapping/logic and DTOs to include isValidated in the response for menus and pages (if present).

3. Frontend / Common UI Library Logic

  • Implement a validation helper that:

    • Accepts the current route path and the menu tree.

    • Finds the corresponding menu/page.

    • Reads its isValidated flag.

  • If isValidated is false, treat the screen as “In Testing”.

4. User Experience Handling

  • Display a clear toast message: "Testing / Pending Validation" when the user navigates to a screen that is not validated.

  • Implement “show once per session” behavior using sessionStorage to avoid repeated notifications on refresh/navigation.

Outcome:

  • Ensures transparency for screens deployed to production but still under final validation.

  • Maintains non-intrusive UI behavior while keeping users informed.

[ANALYSIS] [leveling board]: issue in the display launcher waiting time
description:
Root Cause

When launcherWaitingTime, minLauncherWaitingTime, or maxLauncherWaitingTime are null, undefined, or empty, the UI renders them as 00:00. This is misleading because 00:00 represents a valid time value rather than the absence of data. The underlying issue is that the current formatting logic does not differentiate between missing values and a legitimate zero duration.

Fix Strategy

1. Detection
Enhance the value-preparation logic to explicitly detect missing data. Any value that is null, undefined, or an empty string should be treated as not available, while a numeric 0 should remain a valid value.

2. Display
Replace the misleading 00:00 output with a clear placeholder: NA when the value is missing.

3. Visual Cue
Apply a grey color to NA to clearly communicate that the data is unavailable, without drawing the same visual weight as real values.

Implementation Steps

  1. Update the formatting function (e.g., formatMinutes or the logic responsible for button/label text) to:

    • Return NA when the input value is null, undefined, or empty.

    • Continue formatting numeric values normally, including 0.

  2. Update the UI layer to:

    • Detect when the formatted value is NA.

    • Apply a grey text style (e.g., muted/secondary color) to visually distinguish missing data from valid times.

This approach ensures semantic correctness, improves UX clarity, and avoids misinterpreting missing data as a valid zero-time value.

description:
📌Widget Production - Balancing -N+

✔️Purpose 

Being able to clearly see which balancing currently running on a specific resource.

  • Resource type: Resource type: assembly line or JIT line (not a capacity machine):
The check should be done as following: 
 in table resource in HRY domain in MES where type ='ASSEMBLY_LINE' or 'JIT'

  • Balancing here refers to the way work is distributed across the line: “N-”, “N”, “N+”, or “Special.”

  • N- → low cadence 

  • N → normal cadence 

  • N+ → high cadence 

  • Special → customized cadence: set the number of operators and a manual target 

  • Immediate visibility of the current setup.

✔️ Logsheet functionality 

Enhance the current logsheet in MES to support and follow the current line configuration setup in order to:

  1. Displays the current balancing on the resource each 5 minutes

  2. Interactive behavior:

    • Enhance the logsheet column title with -N+

    • The -N+ should be a clickable button 

    • The button -N+ should be visible only for resource type = Assembly or JIT
    • When we click on the -N+, a drawer should be displayed to enable the user to configure 

✔️ Drawer Content: 


✔️ Data retrieval:

1- The drawer detailed view: 

For the operator information: 
We need to ingest the following information from the table ASSEMBLY_LINE_CONFIG in CPT_FAURECIA:
  • PLANT
  • PLC_ID
  • SHIFT_CODE
  • CONFIG_TYPE = OPERATOR
  • NB_LOW
  • NB_MEDIUM
  • NB_HIGH
Show the nb of operator in each case as following: 
  • NB_LOW for the cadence is N- 
  • NB_MEDIUM for the cadence is N
  • NB_HIGH for the cadence is N+

For the target information: 
We need to ingest the following information from the CADENCE_CONFIG in CPT_FAURECIA:
  • PLANT
  • MACHINE_ID
  • CADENCE_LOW
  • CADENCE_NORMAL
  • CADENCE_HIGH
  • MTL_CODE

Show the target in each case as following: 
  • CADEENCE_LOW for the cadence is N- 
  • CADENCE_NORMAL for the cadence is N
  • CADENCE_HIGH for the cadence is N+
Attention point: 
The target information is shown based on the reference that's currently produced. 
  • How ?

  • -In the CHANGE_TOOLS table in MES, identify the reference currently being produced (the record with date_to = 9999-12-31 23:59:59.000).

  • -In the CADENCE_CONFIG table ingested in MES, search for entries matching the same reference, resource and plant.

  • -Retrieve the target information associated with that reference.

    • Case of multiple references in production: The target will be the Sum of all cadences for each mode (low, nominal or high)

    3- Writeback to MII
    When we add a new configuration on the line from MES, we need to send this information to MII as following: 

    *   Insert a record into ACTION_ON_PROD in MII in CPT_FAURECIA with

    _PLANT: the specified plant
    CREATED_TIMESTAMP: the time when the action is done
    ACTION: LOW, HIGH, or SPECIAL
    TOP_EVENT_ID: NULL
    MACHINE_ID: the resource id
    FROM_TIMESTAMP: the time when start the configuration
    TO_TIMESTAMP: the time when end the configuration
    TARGET: the specified target chosen, either for the level LOW, HIGH, SPECIAL or N
    ARCHIVED: 0
    DESCRIPTION: NULL  
    HIDE_TO_TIMESTAMP:0_

    Please refer to this example:
    ![image.png](https://dev.azure.com/faurecia-cloud/2d001414-181c-4c10-be02-72f9f36c01a2/_apis/wit/attachments/e99449ae-acd8-4132-ac57-88179573993e?fileName=image.png)


    *   Insert a second record into ACTION_ON_PROD in MII with ACTION = HOUR_ACTION, using the same FROM_TIMESTAMP and TO_TIMESTAMP, and a description set to _“Model Y; X OP:”_, including the model (line configuration) and the number of operators.

    _PLANT: the specified plant
    CREATED_TIMESTAMP: the time when the action is done
    ACTION: LOW, HIGH, or SPECIAL
    TOP_EVENT_ID: NULL

    TARGET: the specified target chosen, either for the level LOW, HIGH, SPECIAL or N

    Attention point: 
    This insertion is done only one time by hour.
    Example: Insert the ACTION=HOUR_ACTION for the specific hour when the configuration is done.
    example H06


    Then keep the insertion of the ACTION=MODE each time the configuration is updated.

    *  Update the SPEED column record in SHIFT_TRACKING_STATUS in CPT_FAURECIA MII on the specific resource of the specific hour and 5 minutes slot with the chosen configuration

    if it's N+: it should be 1 
    if it's N-:  it should be -1

    Speed Target  SPEED

[Dev-Fix] [eDashboard] Fix the issue with shift starting time
description:
Issue Analysis & Solution

The Problem

The original logic failed to identify overnight shifts that cross midnight because it treated dates and times as separate comparisons, which doesn't work when a shift spans two calendar days.

Example: For shift 2026-01-25 23:00:00 → 2026-01-26 10:59:59 at time 2026-01-26 10:31:00:

  • startDate = "20260125" (yesterday)
  • endDate = "20260126" (today)
  • currentDate = "20260126" (today)
  • The condition startDate === currentDate was false, so it was never considered as current

The Solution

Changed to date-aware comparisons that explicitly handle three shift scenarios:

Current Shift Detection:

  1. Same-day shifts (startDate === currentDate && endDate === currentDate): Check if current time is between start/end times
  2. Overnight shifts starting today (startDate === currentDate && endDate > currentDate): Check if current time is after start time
  3. Overnight shifts from yesterday (startDate === yesterdayDate && endDate === currentDate): Check if current time is before end time 

Previous Shifts Detection:

Similar logic but looks for shifts that ended before the current time, including:

  • Same-day shifts that ended earlier today
  • Overnight shifts from yesterday that ended earlier today
  • Any shifts that fully ended yesterday

This approach correctly handles all shift patterns across midnight boundaries.

                "plant": 1062

        },
        "status": "failure",

        "timestamp": "2026-01-27T10:25:59.525Z",

There was an error connecting to the API manager URL : 10.223.16.68:8443



The error occurs during an HTTPS call initiated by the service (WkIntegrationService) using Axios.

The application attempts to connect to the endpoint api-qa.app.corp resolved as 10.223.16.68 on port 8443, but the TCP connection is immediately refused by the target host.

The integration relies on an MII transaction (SC_MES_API/INTERFACE/WKINTEGRATION/V1/XCT_INTEGRATE_WK_KANBAN
) that includes a writeback step executed through the API Manager.

Due to the API Manager connection failure (ECONNREFUSED), the transaction could not complete successfully. As a result, the writeback operation was never executed.

Because the writeback did not occur, the integration buffer state was not updated, which explains why the buffer status remained RECEIVED instead of transitioning to a subsequent state.

I tried to integrate a new WK right after with @JARRAHI Chaima and it was successful ( apparently the issue with the API manager was fixed, thus the writeback got to work)

titre: [Analysis]--Enabling Filter orders ingestion based on plant
description:
Feature: Filter Order Ingestion Based on Plant

Overview

This feature introduces plant-based filtering to prevent data originating from excluded plants from being ingested, routed, or processed.
The goal is to ensure that only relevant plant data enters the system and propagates across domains.

Configuration

Configuration Property

  • Property name: ORDER_DI_EXCLUDED_PLANTS

  • Format: Comma-separated list of plant identifiers
    Example: 1146,1062

  • Behavior when empty or not set:

    If the value is empty, missing, or blank, no plants are excluded

    All plants are ingested and processed normally

Azure App Configuration

  • Stored in Azure App Configuration

  • Environment-specific (DEV / PPR / QA / PROD)

  • Centrally managed and versioned

  • Changes can be applied without redeployment, subject to refresh policy

Runtime Behavior

  • The excluded plant list is:

    • Read at startup for Dapr-based services

    • Read on first use for controller-based components

  • The exclusion list is cached as an in-memory Set:

    • No per-message configuration lookups

    • No unbounded memory growth

Filtering Strategy

Filtering occurs as early as possible in the ingestion flow:

  • Before queuing

  • Before persistence

  • Before routing

  • Before downstream propagation
    This applies to both Event Hub consumers and Dapr bindings.

Implementation Details

  • The existing  checkPlantConsistency method is extended to:

    • Accept an optional excluded-plant Set

    • Return false when the record’s plant is part of the excluded set

  • This approach:

    • Centralizes skip logic in a single consistency check

    • Avoids duplicated filtering logic across consumers

    • Introduces no additional allocations during message processing

Outcome

If plant ∈ ORDER_DI_EXCLUDED_PLANTS:

  • Data is ignored at ingestion time

  • Data is not stored

  • Data is not routed

  • Data is not propagated to downstream services

Scenario 1 – Global Filtering Across Domains

(Order Router + Order Data Ingestion Domain)

Scope

Plant-based filtering is applied across two layers:

Order Router / Event Hub SDK

  • Picking Orders

  • Production Orders

Order Data Ingestion Domain

  • Alerts

  • KPI Values

  • Material

  • Buffer

  • Other order-domain sources

Behavior

  • Messages originating from excluded plants are discarded immediately

  • No persistence

  • No routing

  • No downstream propagation

  • Filtering is domain-wide, ensuring full data consistency across all consumers and features

Estimated Effort (DEV only)

  • 4 User Stories

titre: Remove unused soft-delete predicate to restore index efficiency and improve query performance
description:
Our current SQL queries include the condition deleted_at IS NULL, although soft delete is not implemented anywhere in the application and the deleted_at column is never populated. Because this column is nullable, unindexed, and low selectivity, the SQL optimizer frequently chooses table scans instead of index seeks, preventing the effective use of existing indexes.

This behavior results in degraded performance across high‑read tables, especially in real-time MES workloads.

To ensure optimal plan selection and improve execution time, we need to remove the unnecessary predicate from all affected queries.

Add watch dog for redis x read
description:
1) The stream subscription loop is stuck (blocked) rather than stopped

  • Your subscribeToStream() loop prints “No messages …” every time xRead returns (even empty).
  • When those logs stop, but the actor keeps responding to reminders, it strongly suggests the loop thread is awaiting something that never returns (most likely the xRead call), not that the whole process died.
  • In this “hung await” state:
    • isProcessing remains true (because it’s only set back to false in the finally after the function returns).
    • Each reminder calls triggerStreamSubscription(), but your guard (if (this.isProcessing || this.isShuttingDown) return) prevents a new loop from starting—so you keep seeing reminder logs, but the subscription loop never restarts.

Why would xRead hang indefinitely?

  • Redis TCP half‑open or a network hiccup/connection drop where the client library doesn’t surface an error or timeout, so the pending await never resolves or rejects.
  • A client/SDK mismatch in xRead/options that occasionally leaves a blocked read unbounded.
  • A rare server failover/connection state where the socket remains open but the command never completes.

This is the cleanest fit with your logs: reminders keep working, process is alive, but the blocked stream call stops your 5‑second “No messages …” cadence and also keeps isProcessing=true, so reminders cannot re‑start the loop.

As a fix  i added a Client‑side watchdog around xRead (timeout + reconnect).

[BA_DESIGN] Automatic reprocess mechanism in case we have master data issue
description:
Context

A WK  can fail for two main reasons:

  1. Buffer Status = ERROR
    → The failure occurred during functional and/or technical checks at the MES layer.

  2. NEO Status = ERROR
    → The failure occurred at the MII integration layer.

UI Enhancements

1. Reprocess Button

  • Add a “Reprocess” button on the screen.

  • The button is enabled only when at least one WK in ERROR status is selected.

2. Batch Selection

  • Add a multi-select column (checkbox) to allow users to select multiple WKs at once.

  • Batch reprocessing must be supported.

Reprocessing Logic

A. WK Creation Failure

  • Condition: WK failed during creation.

  • Action:

    • The system must call the WK Creation API again.

    • All functional and technical checks must be re-executed.

B. WK Rescheduling Failure

  • Condition: WK failed during rescheduling.

  • Action:

    • The system must call MII to reprocess the integration.

    • No recreation of the WK is required.

Multiple Lines for the Same WK

  • If the user selects multiple rows related to the same WK:

    • The system must only process the latest record.

    • The last line sent by Preactor is the one to be considered.

Expected Behavior Summary

  • User selects one or more WKs in ERROR.

  • User clicks Reprocess.

  • System:

    • Identifies the failure type (Creation vs Rescheduling).

    • Routes the reprocessing to:

      • MES API (Creation)

      • MII (Rescheduling)

    • in case duplicates WKs and processes only the most recent entry per WK.

System Error Handling

  • The system must handle all errors occurring during WK reprocessing, including:

    • MES API failures

    • MII integration errors

    • Functional validation failures

    • Technical exceptions (timeouts, unavailable services)

  • Errors must be logged for traceability 

User Feedback Requirements

1. Toast Notifications


Provide immediate, non-blocking feedback to the user after initiating or completing a reprocessing action.

Behavior

  • When the user clicks Reprocess:

    • Display an informational toast:

      • “Reprocessing started for X WK(s).”

  • Once processing is completed:

    • Display a result toast depending on the outcome:

      • Success:

        • “X WK(s) reprocessed successfully.”

      • Partial Success:

        • “Y WK(s) succeeded, Z WK(s) failed. Please check details.”

      • Failure:

        • “Reprocessing failed. Please try again or contact support.”

description:
Today, the ingestion service aggregates data from multiple MII tables (shop_order, s_picking_order, s_production_order) into two consolidated event types:

  • picking_order
  • production_order

This aggregation was introduced to simplify downstream processing, but it now presents technical limitations, especially as the volume and structure of the source tables evolve. The aggregation logic creates constraints for sequencing, payload completeness, maintenance, and further evolutions of the ingestion.

Goal

Refactor the ingestion pipeline so that events are no longer aggregated, but instead ingested and published separately, aligning with the real structure of the source system.
Each MII table should generate its own event stream without merging logic.

description:
Here's a brief description of each function in the Cosmos DB

1. generateTemplateKey()
Generates a unique template identifier using UUID format (TPL-{uuid})
Used when creating new templates without a provided ID

2. upsertTemplate()
Creates or updates a template in Cosmos DB
Automatically converts any existing published templates with the same scope to 'draft' status
refactor: update upsertTemplate to remove scopes from existing published template
Ensures only one published template exists per scope combination
Returns the upserted template

3. getTemplate()
Retrieves a single template by its ID
Returns the template if found, undefined otherwise
Used for fetching specific templates for viewing or deletion

4. getTemplatesByPlant()
Fetches all templates (any status) associated with a specific plant
Returns an array of templates for querying all plant-related templates
No status filtering applied

5. deleteTemplate()
Permanently removes a template from Cosmos DB by ID
Validates the template exists and has a valid partition key (plant)
Uses the plant value as the partition key for deletion

6. getTemplatesByScope()
Retrieves the first published template matching plant, scope type, and scope value
Returns only one template (TOP 1) to ensure uniqueness per scope
Returns undefined if no published template exists for that scope

7. getDefaultTemplate()
Fetches the default template for a specific plant
Returns the template marked with default: true

Build Operation Segments
description:
As a

MES PO

I want

MES X.0 to automatically build and maintain Operation Segment objects using data extracted from SAP Routings, following the ISA‑95 (NF C46‑068‑2 / NF EN 62264‑2) model.

So that

each Operation Segment correctly represents the detailed steps within an Operation Definition, including durations, work centers( Hiearachy scope), validity periods, and classification, ensuring accurate scheduling, traceability, and execution within MES.

Object name — Operation segments:

In ISA‑95, an Operation Segment represents a discrete, identifiable step within an Operation Definition (such as a routing step).
MES X.0 must build Operation Segments automatically from SAP Routing Operations and store the following attributes:

  • Unique system‑generated UID
  • SAP operation number
  • Operation description
  • Work center (Hierarchy Scope)
  • Duration components (HMAC, HMOD, HLOG)
  • Production operation type (production / logistics / maintenance / quality / mixed)
  • Link to its Operation Definition
  • Validity period
  • ERP instance source

This ensures consistent MES operation modeling across all plants and ERP systems.


Operation Segment — Field Definitions:


1. ID (UID)

A globally unique identifier for the Operation Segment.

  • Generated by MES (UUID/GUID).
  • Serves as primary key and reference ID across MES modules.

2. ERP Identifier

The SAP operation number from the material routing.

  • Uniquely identifies the operation step inside a routing.

3. Description

Operation name or text extracted from SAP Routing.

4. Hierarchy Scope

The SAP Work Center associated with the routing operation.

  • Defines the hierarchical level in which the segment is executed.

5. HMAC Duration

Machine time per routing operation (for 1,000 pieces or SAP base quantity).
Mapped directly from SAP.

6. HMOD Duration

MOD (Manual Operator Duration) time per routing operation.
Mapped from SAP.

7. HLOG Duration

Logistics time per routing operation.
Mapped from SAP.

8. Duration UOM

Unit of measure for the duration fields (e.g., MIN, SEC, H).
Extracted from SAP routing.

9. Operation Type

Classification of the segment, mapped from SAP:

  • Production – for production operations
  • Inventory – for logistics-related operations
  • Maintenance – for maintenance operations
  • Quality – for inspection/quality operations
  • Mixed – when several categories apply

10. ID Operation Definition

The reference to the Operation Definition that this segment belongs to.

  • Each segment instantiates a specific Operation Definition.

11. Published Date

Timestamp of when the segment was generated or last updated in MES.

12. Effective Start Date

Date from which this Operation Segment version is valid.
Retrieved from SAP routing validity.

13. Effective End Date

End date for segment validity.
Retrieved from SAP routing validity.

14. ERP Source

Identifier of the ERP system (FCS / S4 instance) providing the routing:
Examples: FC1, FC2, FC3.
(Prevents duplicates in multi‑ERP environments.)

Build Operation definition data model
description:
As a

MES PO

I want

to build and maintain an Operation Definition object in MES X.0 using data extracted from SAP Production Versions.

So that

operation models in MES are fully aligned with SAP routing and BOM structures, correctly identified, versioned, and valid within the ISA‑95 framework, ensuring consistent execution, traceability, and interoperability across all MES processes.

Object name  — Operation Definition:

According to ISA‑95 / IEC 62264‑2 (NF C46‑068‑2, NF EN 62264‑2), an Operation Definition represents a uniquely identifiable specification of work to be performed for producing a material.

In MES X.0, the Operation Definition is populated from SAP Production Version  data, enriched with MES governance attributes.

The Operation Definition captures:

  • SAP routing metadata (Task Group ID, Group Counter, Version)
  • Hierarchy context ( Work Center)
  • BOM reference
  • Validity periods
  • ERP source context (to support multi‑ERP scenarios)

The MES system shall generate a unique UID and store all required ISA‑95‑compliant attributes.

Operation Definition — Field Definitions:


1. ID (UID)

Uniquely identifies the operations definition. The ID shall be used in other parts of the model when the operations definition needs to be identified ( can be = plant+WC+ version)

  • Should be system-generated (UUID/GUID).

2. ERP Source

Represent which FCS or S4 instance provided the Production Version( to avoid duplicate in case where MESX can be connected  to diffrent FCS instance) 


Examples:

  • FC1
  • FC2
  • FC3

3. ERP Identifier

Production version coming from SAP(ID= Plant+Material+ Version).

4. Task group ID

The SAP routing group ID referenced by the Production Version.

5. Group Counter

SAP routing group counter from the Production Version.

6. Version

The Production Version number (VERID) from SAP.

7. Description

Operation Definition name, taken from SAP Production Version metadata

8. Hierarchy Scope

SAP Work Center / Production Line defined in the Production Version.
Represents the operational scope according to ISA‑95 hierarchy levels.

Typically corresponds to  Work Center  in SAP.

9. ID Operation Material Bill

ID of the Bill of Materials associated with this Operation Definition→ this field should store the BOM ID .

10. Published Date

The timestamp when the operation definition was  published to MES.

11. Effective Start Date

Starting date from which this operation definition is valid. matches SAP Production Version validity start ( Valid from).

12. Effective End Date

End date for validity ,matches SAP Production Version validity end (valid to).

description:
As a

MES PO 

I want

a dedicated screen in the MES X.0 Master Data module where MESOperator, Process Engineer, Master Data User can search, view, and explore Operation Segments associated with a selected Material.

So that

They can quickly access the detailed execution steps extracted from SAP routing, understand their structure, durations, work centers, and validity periods, and ensure the Operation Model is complete and correct according to ISA‑95 (NF C46‑068‑2 / NF EN 62264‑2).

Description:

The Operation Segment Viewer screen allows users to navigate the full Operation Model for any material.

The screen must:

  1. Allow the user to select a Material through multiple input modes
  2. Automatically load all Operation Segments linked to that material
  3. Display the list of segments (sortable, filterable, with optional pagination)
  4. Allow the user to select an Operation Segment from the list
  5. Show a complete Operation Segment Viewer panel with all attributes defined in the Operation Segment object
    • Hierarchy Scope
    • HMAC / HMOD / HLOG durations
    • Operation type
    • SAP Work Center
    • UOM
    • Validity dates
    • ERP identifiers
    • Published date
    • Reference to Operation Definition

This viewer supports MES users in analysis, troubleshooting, model validation, process audit, and execution support.

Screen Workflow:

Step 1 — User selects a Material

The screen offers three input methods:

  • Dropdown list (with auto-complete)
  • Search bar (by material number, description, plant, etc.)
  • Barcode/QR scan (optional MES flow if enabled)

Once the material is selected → MES triggers the loading of Operation Segments.

Step 2 — System loads all Operation Segments

MES retrieves all Operation Segments associated with the selected Material.

System displays:

  • A table or list view
  • Sorted by operation number by default
  • Each row representing one Operation Segment

If no data exists:

“No operation segments found for selected material”

Step 3 — User selects an Operation Segment

When the user clicks/taps on a segment row:

  • The segment becomes highlighted
  • The Viewer panel activates on the right side or below the list

Step 4 — Viewer displays all details of the selected Operation Segment

The Operation Segment Viewer must display all fields from the Operation Segment object, including:

  • ID (UID)
  • ERP Identifier (SAP operation number)
  • Description (operation text)
  • Hierarchy Scope (work center)
  • Durations:
    • HMAC Duration
    • HMOD Duration
    • HLOG Duration
    • Duration UOM
  • Operation Type
    • Production
    • Inventory
    • Quality
    • Maintenance
    • Mixed
  • ID Operation Definition (clickable link to navigate)
  • Published Date
  • Effective Start Date
  • Effective End Date
  • ERP Source

This panel acts as a read-only viewer, not an editor.

titre: MESX Operation Segments Management (Routing)
description:
According to ISA95 I want the manufacturing routing coming from SAP (L4)to be transformed exclusively into Operation Segments in MESX.0

 So that MES X.0 can build Work Masters that define how each operation is executed on the shopfloor, independently of SAP execution logic.


  • SAP routing is converted into Operation Segments, which formalize WHAT needs to be done.
  • MES X.0 uses these Operation Segments to construct Work Masters, templates defining HOW operations will be executed at plant level.
  • Execution details such as equipment roles, work instructions, or operator interactions are defined only inside the Work Master, not in SAP routing.

This separation ensures:

  • SAP maintains business process ownership
  • MES X.0 retains execution flexibility

  • SAP production version is converted into Operation definition, which formalize Where production Schedule & execution  needs to be done.
  • MES X.0 uses these Operation definition to build Work Masters, templates defining HOW operations will be executed at plant level.
  • Execution details such as equipment roles( WC, WU, etc etc)  is defined only inside the Work Master, not in SAP prod version .

The transaction SC_MES_API/DOWNTIME/TRANSACTION/V1/DOWNTIME_CLASSIF_API was failing with the error "Incorrect syntax near '00'". This error occurs because SQL Server is unable to correctly parse the ISO-8601 datetime format that uses the T separator (e.g. 2026-01-15T14:00:00).


The root cause was identified in the query SC_MES_API/DOWNTIME/QUERY/UPDATE_SHIFT_TRACKING_STATUS, where the “Use Typed Parameters” option was not enabled.

To fix the issue, I enabled this option and submitted the ETF containing the correction: TRANPORT_API_140000_144103_V1.0_IYO_260210_1356_DMA. 

Could you please generate the patch for RM8/PM6?

thank you!

titre: [BA Design] [Live Status] GAP widget - Ok First part - detail view & interaction
description:
📌 User Story – mLean KPI: First OK Part

Purpose

This user story focuses on the mLean KPI related to the First OK Part, enabling users to access detailed information by clicking on the KPI element.

⚠️ Current View

The current implementation is based on a Gantt view.
More details are available in this task:
https://dev.azure.com/faurecia-cloud/MES_X.0/_workitems/edit/141717

🎯 Required Change

The existing Gantt view will be replaced with a Waterfall view.

Reason

  • A Gantt view is designed to visualize task planning and duration in a structured and scheduled manner.

  • A Waterfall view focuses on displaying events in the order they occur, emphasizing the real-time sequence of activities.

Since this KPI reflects event flow rather than task planning, the waterfall view is more appropriate.

New Waterfall View – Expected Behavior



This waterfall view will display events in reverse chronological order:

  • Top of the page → newest item

  • Bottom of the page → oldest item

The list will update dynamically as new events occur.

✔️Duration Representation

The slot width (instead of height) will reflect the actual duration of the item:

  • Longer duration → larger visual width

✔️Vertical Positioning

Items will be ordered based on their created_at timestamp

✔️Scrolling Behavior

If the number of items exceeds the visible area, a scrollable view will allow users to navigate from the newest items at the top to the oldest items at the bottom, and vice versa.

✔️ Displayed Item Information

📍Data retrieval

With the existing ok-first part-schedules API we need: 



  • The ID
  • The ID creation date: start time of the assessment
  • The ID close date: end date of the assessment
  • The ID status

📍Visualisation

Each ID should continue include the following information:

  • Creation date

  • Duration

  • Sub-perimeter description 

This information can be displayed either on hover or directly on the item, depending on the chosen UI/UX design.

1- Sub-Perimeter Information

Currently, the sub-perimeter is retrieved using the same endpoint as the GAP list, with pattern = 5 (Line).

However, this approach may not be consistent across all sites, as the hierarchy may change from one site to another on the mLean side.

Proposed Update

To ensure consistency, the logic will be updated as follows:

  1. Use the API mlean.app.corp/patterns/ to retrieve the Line ID.

  2. Use the retrieved Line ID to query the second API mlean/api/v1/perimeters/ to fetch the corresponding sub-perimeter information.

2- Created time and duration Information

Duration: calculated as the difference between the creation date and the closing date. If the closing date is not available, the duration is calculated from the creation date to the current time.

3- Color Coding 

The existing color convention will be maintained:

StatusColorMeaning
Closed & status 0 Green Status OK
Closed & status -1 Red Status NOK
Not closed & status -1 
 		Red Not assessed considered as NOK

✔️ mLean redirection

  • Open the mLean application for first OK for a specific item:

Each item should redirect the user to mLean

Possibility: By clicking on the tooltip or directly on the item, depending on the chosen UI/UX design.
Link: mlean mPS

Remark: mLean application should be opened in a new tab

titre: Page
Operation definition visualization
description:
As a

MES PO 

I want

a dedicated screen in the MES X.0 Master Data module where MES Operator, Process Engineer, Master Data Owner, Production Planner, or Quality Engineer can search for, list, and visualize Operation Definitions associated with materials.

So that

Thye can clearly understand each Operation Definition generated from SAP Production Versions, including routing metadata, versioning, plant-specific scope, associated BOM, Work Center hierarchy, and validity dates — ensuring traceability, verification, and validation of the operation model according to ISA‑95 (NF C46‑068‑2 / NF EN 62264‑2).

Description:

The Operation Definition Viewer Screen enables MES users to explore how production for a material is structured at SAP routing level.

The screen must:

  1. Allow users to select a material
  2. Load all associated Operation Definitions (from SAP Production Versions)
  3. Display them in a list/table
  4. Allow the user to select one Operation Definition
  5. Show a detailed Operation Definition Viewer with all attributes from the Operation Definition object
  6. Optionally link to related objects (e.g., Operation Segments, BOM)

This screen is strictly read‑only, focused on navigation and analysis.

Screen Workflow:

Step 1 — User selects a Material

The system must support several selection methods:

  • Dropdown (with autocomplete)
  • Search bar (by Material Number, Description, Plant)
  • Barcode/QR scan (optional)

Once a material is selected → MES loads its Operation Definitions.

Step 2 — System loads all Operation Definitions

MES retrieves all Operation Definitions associated with the selected material.

The system displays:

  • A list/table view
  • One row per Operation Definition (Version)

If none found:

“No operation definitions found for this material.”

Step 3 — User selects an Operation Definition

When selecting a row:

  • The Operation Definition becomes highlighted
  • The Viewer panel activates
  • Related operations (segments) can be shown as a nested list (optional)

Step 4 — Detailed Operation Definition Viewer

The viewer displays all fields from the Operation Definition object, including:

Identity

  • ID (UID)
  • ERP Source (FC1 / FC2 / FC3, etc.)
  • ERP Identifier (Plant + Material + Version)

SAP Routing Attributes

  • Task Group ID
  • Group Counter
  • Version (Production Version Number)
  • Description

Hierarchy

  • Hierarchy Scope (Work Center / Production Line)

Manufacturing Structure

  • ID Operation Material Bill (BOM reference)
    (Clickable link if BOM visualization is available)

Lifecycle

  • Published Date (in MES)
  • Effective Start Date (SAP Valid From)
  • Effective End Date (SAP Valid To)

Related Entities (optional links)

  • Operation Segments belonging to this Operation Definition
  • Materials using this Operation Definition

This viewer is read‑only and intended for analysis, audit, model validation, and troubleshooting.

📌[Live Status] GAP widget - Management control - detail view & interaction


Purpose

This user story focuses on the mLean KPI related to the management control, that enable to have the same view as in mLean application. 

We'll manage the coloring code under this user story for each item cross the shift time.

⚠️ Current behavior 
Based on this table: 

1. Definition of NA (Not Applicable)

NA = Not Applicable

  • It means that the audit cannot be performed for that item.

  • The last previously assessed color is reused even if that color is Grey, except for the first hour.

2. Special Case: First Hour

During the first hour of monitoring:

If no item has been assessed as OK or NOK yet, and it's NA, then, the KPI will be Grey

else, it will take the previous hour status

Coloring code for the cell:
Status Meaning Color Notes
1 Assessed and the status is OK Green always
0 Assessed and the status is NOK Red always
-2 Not applicable Same color (Grey/Red/Green) as the previous hour Applicable to shift hours != first hour of the shift
Grey First hour of the shift
null Not assessed Grey always


3. Global KPI result: 

The global KPI depends on the presence of NOK results:

Condition
Global KPI Hour ?
At least one NOK NOK: Red any hours of the shift
No NOK and at least one not assessed or NA NA: Grey Special case: first hour of the shift
NOK: Red NA or Not assessed > first hour of the shift
All is OK OK: Green any hours of the shift


The KPI calculation will remain as today, on hourly basis,

Build Material definition Data model
description:
As a

MES PO

I want

MES X.0 to automatically generate and maintain Material Definition objects based on SAP MATMAS integration, fully aligned with the ISA‑95 Material Model (NF C46‑068‑2 / NF EN 62264‑2).

So that

each material used in MES has a stable, unique identity, independent from ERP keys, and can serve as the foundation for other MES functions/objects such as operations, BOM, routing, traceability, quality processes, and serialization.

Object Name:Material Definition 

The Material Definition object represents the conceptual identity of a material in MES X.0.
It is the top-level ISA‑95 material entity from which:

  • Material Classes
  • Material Class Properties
  • Material Definition Property Values
  • Operational models (Operations, BOM, Segments)

are all linked.

The Material Definition must:

  • Be uniquely identified by a system-generated UID
  • Store the SAP material number (18 or 40 characters)
  • Store a human-readable material description
  • Track the ERP Source for multi‑ERP environments

These attributes derive from SAP MATMAS segments and must remain stable across the lifecycle of the material.


Field Definitions:

1. ID (UID)

Description:
ISA‑95 requires that each Material Definition has a unique identifier.
This identifier shall be stable and independent from ERP keys.

Rules:

  • Must be system‑generated (UUID/GUID v4 recommended).
  • Must uniquely identify a material across:
    • All MES instances
    • All plants
    • All lifecycle states

Recommendation:
materialDefinitionId = UUID
OR
materialDefinitionId = <PlantCode>-<MaterialNumber> 

2. Material Number

Description:
The material number provided by SAP via MATMAS (MARA-MATNR).
It represents the ERP technical identifier.

Source in SAP MATMAS:

  • Segment: E1MARAM
  • Table: MARA
  • Field: MATNR

Rules:

  • Must be received from SAP ECC / S4 and stored without leading zeros


3. Description

Description:
Human‑readable Material Description, corresponding to SAP short text.

Source in SAP MATMAS:

  • Segment: E1MAKTM
  • Table: MAKT
  • Field: MAKTX

Rules:

  • Multi‑language possible (ISA‑95 supports language variants).
  • If language variants exist → MES stores one default description per ERP sourcing language.


4. ERP Source

Description:
Indicates which SAP instance (FCS / S4 / ERP system) provided this material.
Required because MES X.0 can ingest data from several ERP landscapes and must avoid collisions.

Examples:

  • FC1
  • FC2
  • FC3
  • S4P01 (if S/4 Production instance)

Usage:

  • Supports multi‑ERP environments.
  • Ensures uniqueness when the same Material Number exists in multiple SAP systems.
  • Helps with troubleshooting integration issues.

Rules:

  • Mandatory
  • Defined by ERP integration configuration (list of allowed ERP sources)

description:
As a user, I want to be able to view the list of mLean gaps (referred to as the perimeter),

so that I can use it and assign the appropriate gaps to a DMC resource.

In this user story, we will update the technical rule used to correctly retrieve the list of mLean gaps.

Current Behavior

Today, the system retrieves Gaps based on a fixed hierarchy assumption and a predefined pattern value:

  • Pattern = 4

  • Assumed hierarchy: UAP - Gap - Line

This logic assumes that the mLean hierarchy is always structured in the same way.

However, the mLean hierarchy is not always consistent across all sites.

For example, in Allenjoie, the hierarchy is structured as:
UAP - Line - Gap

In this case, the Gap corresponds to pattern = 5, not 4.

Expected Change

The retrieval logic must be updated to handle different hierarchy structures dynamically, ensuring that the correct mLean Gaps are identified regardless of the site configuration.

Design System Specification and technical Analysis
description:
Implementation and Industrialization of the MESX.0 Design System with AI Assistant

Context

Manufacturing Execution Systems MESX.0 require complex, consistent, and scalable user interfaces to support production monitoring, order management, and real-time industrial data. As MESX.0 platforms evolve and integrate multiple backend services, frontend development becomes increasingly complex and costly when UI standards are not strictly enforced.

To address these challenges, a Design System for MESX.0 has already been defined by UX experts using Figma, including a clear identification of components, reusable components, and design tokens. While this Design System provides a strong UX foundation, it must be implemented, industrialized, and adopted by development teams to fully realize its value.

In addition to implementation, developers need clear guidance and tooling to correctly apply the Design System. To support this, the project introduces an AI-powered Design System Assistant that helps developers discover components, understand usage rules, and generate implementation code.

This project focuses on the engineering and industrialization of the MESX.0 Design System, combined with an AI assistant, to improve developer productivity, ensure UI consistency, and accelerate MESX.0 frontend development.

Objectives

• Implement the existing Figma-based MESX.0 Design System into production-ready frontend components using Vue.js, TypeScript, and Quasar.
• Translate identified components and reusable components into a typed, structured, and maintainable UI library.
• Ensure consistency, reusability, scalability, and type safety across all MESX.0 screens.
• Develop a Design System Explorer exposing design tokens, typography, and UI components.
• Provide CSS / Tailwind and TypeScript-based Vue code snippets to facilitate correct developer implementation.
• Design and integrate an AI Assistant to guide developers in using the Design System.
• Guarantee alignment with industrial UX constraints such as clarity, information density, and real-time feedback.

Scope & Methodology

The project will be executed in structured phases:

1. Design System Engineering Analysis

• Analyze the existing Figma Design System and component inventory.
• Define implementation standards (naming conventions, folder structure, versioning).
• Establish mapping rules between Figma components and Vue.js + TypeScript components.

2. Design Tokens & Styling Implementation

• Implement design tokens (colors, typography, spacing, states) using Tailwind CSS.
• Configure theming and global styles aligned with MESX.0 branding.
• Ensure visual consistency across all components.

3. Component Library Implementation (TypeScript-first)

• Implement reusable components using Vue.js, TypeScript, and Quasar, including:

  • Core UI components (buttons, inputs, forms, tables)
  • MES-specific components (KPIs, timelines ,)
  • Layout and navigation components
    • Ensure configurability, accessibility, and responsiveness.

4. Design System Explorer for Developers

• Develop a Design System Explorer integrated into MESX.0 or provided as a standalone module.
• Display:

  • Design tokens (colors, spacing, typography)
  • Typography scales and usage rules
  • UI components with variants and states
    • Expose corresponding Tailwind classes and Vue + TypeScript usage examples.

5. AI-Powered Design System Assistant

• Design and implement an AI assistant integrated into the Design System Explorer.
• Enable developers to interact using natural language to:

  • Discover available components and variants
  • Receive recommendations based on MES use cases
  • Generate TypeScript-based Vue / Quasar code snippets
  • Understand UX rules and design token usage
    • Ensure the assistant relies on the Design System as a controlled and typed knowledge source.

6. Integration into MESX.0

• Integrate the typed component library and Design System Explorer into the MESX.0 frontend.
• Refactor selected MESX.0 screens to adopt standardized components.
• Validate compatibility with real-time data and MESX.0 workflows.

7. Validation, Documentation & Analysis

• Produce technical documentation and TypeScript component contracts.
• Validate the Design System and AI assistant using real MESX.0 scenarios.
• Measure improvements in:

  • Development speed
  • UI consistency
  • Component reuse
  • Developer onboarding efficiency

Expected Deliverables

• Production-ready implementation of the MESX.0 Design System.
• Reusable and documented TypeScript-based frontend component library.
• Design System Explorer displaying tokens, typography, and components.
• Integrated AI Design System Assistant for developer support.
• Refactored MESX.0 screens using standardized components.
• Validation and analysis report.

Technical Stack

• Design Source: Figma (existing Design System and component inventory)
• Frontend Framework: Vue.js + TypeScript
• UI Framework: Quasar
• Styling & Design Tokens: Tailwind CSS
• AI Integration: LLM-based Assistant (Design System–restricted knowledge)
• Architecture: Component-based, typed, Design System–driven UI with AI assistance

Build Material Class
description:
As a

MES PO

I want

to define and manage Material Classes that group Material Definitions for specific operational purposes (manufacturing, logistics, quality, maintenance), using both SAP‑derived classes and MES‑specific classes.

So that

the MES can organize materials consistently according to ISA‑95 standards, integrate SAP MATMAS structures as material classes, and extend them with additional MES‑only configuration when needed.

Object Name: Material Class 

According to ISA‑95 / IEC 62264‑2, a Material Class represents a logical grouping of materials that serve a common purpose within operations.
In MES X.0, a Material Class must support two complementary sources:

1. ERP‑Derived Classes (SAP MATMAS)

  • MES must automatically create Material Classes based on the MATMAS segments received from SAP (e.g., MARA, MAKT, MARC, MARD, MARM, MVKE, etc.).
  • These ERP classes describe standard material attributes originating from the ERP master data structure.

2. MES‑Defined Classes (MES Extensions)

  • MES must allow creation of additional Material Classes for configuration needs that are not defined in SAP.
  • These classes allow MES to support additional manufacturing rules.

Material Classes must follow ISA‑95 conventions and contain a minimal, consistent structure.

Field Definitions

1. ID (UID)

Description:
Uniquely identifies a Material Class within MES.

Rules:

  • Must be system‑generated (UUID/GUID v4).
  • Must uniquely identify the Material Class across all MES sources.
  • Used as the reference key wherever a Material Class is associated with properties or material definitions.

2. Description

Description:
Human‑readable description of the Material Class, indicating its purpose (manufacturing, quality, logistics, maintenance, MES extension, etc.).

Rules:

  • Mandatory field.
  • Can be multilingual if needed.
  • Imported automatically from SAP for ERP‑derived classes, or manually entered for MES‑defined classes.

titre: Build Material class property
description:
As a

MES PO

I want

to define Material Class Properties that describe the characteristics, rules, or attributes associated with each Material Class, using both SAP‑mapped properties (from MATMAS segments) and MES‑defined properties.

So that

each Material Class can accurately represent the data and configuration required by ISA‑95, enabling MES X.0 to manage material behavior, classification, and operational parameters in a structured and consistent way.

Object name: Material Class Property 

According to ISA‑95 / IEC 62264‑2 (NF C46‑068‑2, NF EN 62264‑2), a Material Class Property defines the individual attributes that belong to a Material Class.
These properties give semantic meaning to the class and allow the MES to configure or extend material attributes that originate either from:

1. ERP (SAP MATMAS) mapping

Properties that correspond to SAP tables/fields, e.g. MARA-MTART, MARC-WERKS, MARD-LGPBE, etc.

2. MES‑specific configuration

Properties that are not coming from SAP but are needed for MES functionality (labeling, traceability, routing rules, custom behaviors, etc.).

Each Material Class Property must contain a minimal set of standard fields as defined below.

Material Class Property — Field Definitions

1. ID Property (UID)

Uniquely identifies the property.

  • Must be system-generated (UUID/GUID).
  • Used everywhere this property is referenced.

2. ID Class

Identifier of the Material Class to which this property belongs.

  • Must reference an existing Material Class UID.
  • Ensures each property is attached to the right class.

3. Description (Property Name)

Human‑readable name of the property.
Examples:

  • “Material Type”
  • “Prod Version Plant”
  • “SMALL_LABEL_TYPE”

4. Type

The type of value expected for this property.
Examples:

  • STRING
  • VCHAR
  • NUMBER
  • BOOLEAN
  • DATE
  • LIST

5. External Mapping

Indicates if the property maps to an SAP MATMAS field or another external system.

  • If SAP: store the SAP Table, Field, Segment (e.g., MARC-WERKS, E1MARCM.WERKS)
  • Else: value = NULL or MES to indicate an MES‑defined property.

Build Material Definition Property
description:
As a

MES PO

I want

to store and manage the values assigned to each Material Class Property for each Material Definition.

So that

every Material Definition can have the correct ISA‑95‑compliant attributes, derived from either SAP (ERP‑mapped) or MES‑specific configuration, and these values can be used consistently across MES X.0 for manufacturing, quality, logistics, traceability, and scheduling functions.

Object name: Material Definition Property 


According to ISA‑95 / IEC 62264‑2 (NF C46‑068‑2, NF EN 62264‑2), the Material Definition Property object holds the actual property values associated with a Material Definition.

  • The Material Class Property defines the property structure
  • The Material Definition Property defines the value for a specific material

This is how MES builds material‑specific configuration using both ERP and MES information.

A Material Definition Property therefore requires at least:

  • A reference to the Property ID (the class property)
  • A reference to the Material Definition ID
  • A Property Name (for readability)
  • A Property Value (the actual stored value)

Material Definition Property — Field Definitions

1. ID Property

The identifier of the Material Class Property to which this value corresponds.

  • Must reference an existing Material Class Property UID.

2. ID Material Definition

Identifier of the Material Definition to which the value applies.

  • Must reference an existing Material Definition UID.

3. Description (Property Name)

Human‑readable name of the property.

  • Useful for UI display and search.
  • Derived from the Material Class Property.

4. Property Value

The value assigned to this property for a given material.

description:
While investigating the issue related to the incorrect tool data displayed in production, we identified that the root cause was on the MII side. There was outdated data that had remained unchanged since 2023 (please refer to the attached file containing the obsolete records).

On the MII side, there is no impact because the logic relies on table tags to determine the currently produced parts/tool. However, on the MES side, the filtering is based solely on DATE_TO = '9999-12-31'. As a result, when outdated records remain open with that date, the issue affects only the MES side.

As a workaround, and after synchronizing with the MII team, we proceeded with:

  • Deleting the outdated records on the MII side.

  • Removing the corresponding entries in the change tools table on the MES side for plant 1165.

  • Triggering a new snapshot.

Following these actions, the displayed data is now correct:

[UX Research] Ok First part - 2 OPTIONS and 3rd UX Alternative
description:
0RESEARCH GOAL:
redefining First OK visualization from planning representation to real-time event awareness, and validating the optimal temporal orientation and insertion logic to reduce cognitive load in live production monitoring

For this US we are not just changing a visualization, we are changing the mental model from "Gantt" to "waterfall".
So the question is How do we best support situational awareness ?

Before deciding scroll direction or reversed waterfall, we need to validate:

What does the gap leader really need?
  • See current First OK status immediately.
  • Understand sequence continuity
  • Detect long durations or abnormal gaps
  • Access details quickly (ID, sub-perimeter, duration)
  • Jump to mLean for investigation
Now lets compare the suggested ideas:

Option A : Reversed Vertical Waterfall(Newest at TOP, older below)

Behavior:

  • New event inserted at top

  • List pushes older items downward

  • Vertical internal scroll if container is fixed height

Pros:  
  • Current state always visible at top. 
  • No overlap.
  • Clear “live feed” behavior.
Cons:
  • If auto-refresh pushes content while user is reading older entries = disorientation
  • Internal scroll inside a page = cognitive friction
Option B : Normal Chronological (Oldest Top → Newest Bottom)

Behavior:

  • New items appended at bottom
  • Page scroll handles overflow
  • No internal scroll needed
Pros:  
  • Natural reading direction
  • Page scroll (no nested scroll issues)
Cons:
  • User must scroll down to see latest
  • Not ideal for real-time monitoring
  • Weak “current situation” visibility
=> This is better for history analysis, not monitoring.

Option C : Alternative Concept (Hybrid Model: Pinned Current + Scrollable History)
Instead of pure reversed waterfall:

LAYOUT:
--------------------------------
Current First OK (Pinned)
--------------------------------
Scrollable History (waterfall)
--------------------------------

Behavior:
  • Current open / most recent item always visible
  • Historical items scroll below
  • New event: Moves into pinned zone & Previous one moves to history

This behavior is often used in:

  • Monitoring systems

  • Manufacturing event boards

  • Alert dashboards

titre: [Analysis] [Page Builder] Widget Production - Balancing -N+
description:
Dev Analysis – Widget Production - Balancing -N+


1. Ingestion

Sources (CPT_FAURECIA → MES)

Table 1: ACTION_ON_PROD (CPT_FAURECIA)

Fields to ingest: PLANT, CREATED_TIMESTAMP, ACTION, MACHINE_ID, FROM_TIMESTAMP, TO_TIMESTAMP, TARGET

Purpose: Determines the active balancing mode at any given time for a resource.

Ingestion logic: Full incremental ingestion filtered by relevant ACTION values (LOW, HIGH, SPECIAL, HOUR_ACTION) and by resource scope (assembly/JIT lines only). Need to evaluate impact on existing action-on-prod pipeline — specifically whether ingesting all events breaks existing filters or KPI computations downstream. This is the key risk flagged in the story comments.

Table 2: ASSEMBLY_LINE_CONFIG (CPT_FAURECIA)

Fields to ingest: PLANT, PLC_ID, SHIFT_CODE, CONFIG_TYPE, NB_LOW, NB_MEDIUM, NB_HIGH

Filter on: CONFIG_TYPE = 'OPERATORS'

Purpose: Provides the number of operators per cadence mode per shift.

Table 3: CADENCE_CONFIG (CPT_FAURECIA)

Fields to ingest: PLANT, MACHINE_ID, CADENCE_LOW, CADENCE_NORMAL, CADENCE_HIGH, MTL_CODE

Purpose: Provides target cadence per reference (material code) and resource.

Existing MES table used (no ingestion needed): CHANGE_TOOLS

Used to resolve the currently produced reference (date_to = 9999-12-31 23:59:59.000). Supports the multi-reference case where targets must be summed per cadence mode.


2. Data Models


LineAction (mapped from ACTION_ON_PROD)

Represents an active or historical balancing action on a resource. Key fields: plant, machine_id (resource), action (LOW | HIGH | SPECIAL | HOUR_ACTION), from_timestamp, to_timestamp, target, created_timestamp.

AssemblyLineConfig (mapped from ASSEMBLY_LINE_CONFIG)

Represents operator count configuration per shift and cadence mode. Key fields: plant, plc_id, shift_code, config_type, nb_low, nb_medium, nb_high.

CadenceConfig (mapped from CADENCE_CONFIG)

Represents target cadence per reference and resource. Key fields: plant, machine_id, mtl_code, cadence_low, cadence_normal, cadence_high .


3. APIs

GET /resources/:resourceId/line-configuration

Purpose: Returns the current balancing state for the widget display.

Response: current balancing label, nb_operators for current mode, target for current mode, from_timestamp, to_timestamp.


GET /resources/:resourceId/line-configuration/detail

Purpose: Returns the full configuration detail for the modal/drawer (all three cadence modes with their operator counts and targets, not just the active one).

Use: Populates Section 1 (setup selection) and Section 2 (time range) in the modal. Allows the user to see all available modes before selecting one.


POST /resources/:resourceId/line-configuration

Purpose: Saves a new balancing configuration — writeback to MII.

Payload: action (LOW | HIGH | SPECIAL), from_timestamp, to_timestamp, target (required for SPECIAL), nb_operators (required for SPECIAL), model (line configuration label for description).


4. Frontend Actions

Widget (Default View on eDashboard)

Displays the widget card named "Line Configuration" showing the current balancing label (N-, N, N+, Special) prominently. On mount, it calls GET /line-configuration and renders the resolved label. The widget is clickable — clicking opens the modal/drawer.


Modal / Drawer (Edit View)

Opened on widget click. Calls GET /line-configuration/detail to populate both sections.

Section 1 – Setup selection: The user selects one of the four modes. For N-, N, N+, the operator count and target are pre-filled from the detail response (read-only, coming from config tables). For Special, the user manually inputs nb_operators and a custom target.

Section 2 – Time range: The user selects from_timestamp and to_timestamp. These are validated client-side against shift boundaries before allowing save. A warning is shown if the user attempts to cancel with unsaved changes.

Save action: Triggers POST /line-configuration with the selected mode, timestamps, and relevant values. On success, the modal closes and the widget refreshes its state. On failure, an error message is shown inline.

Cancel action: If changes were made, a confirmation prompt warns the user that changes won't be saved. On confirm, modal closes without any write.

titre: [TEST] Test of Rule‑Based Routing for the Azure Container Apps Environment in DEV
description:
Blocker: HTTP Route Configs cannot replace app-proxy while auth-proxy sidecar dependency exists
The current architecture runs auth-proxy and app-proxy as a tightly coupled pair in the same container. The auth-proxy is hardwired to forward all authenticated requests to the app-proxy running locally alongside it. Removing the app-proxy sidecar, as required by the HTTP Route Configs migration, leaves the auth-proxy with no forwarding target, causing a complete application outage. The migration cannot proceed without first resolving this architectural dependency.

Build Operation Material Bill (BOM Header) Data model
description:
As a

MES PO

I want

MES X.0 to ingest and maintain Operations Material Bill (OMB) Header objects from SAP ECC/S4 BOMs BOMMAT Idoc according to ISA‑95 (NF C46‑068‑2 / NF EN 62264‑2). OperationsMaterialBill (6.1.3).

So that

MES has a complete and stable representation of each SAP BOM header linked to an Operation Definition, ensuring proper alignment for manufacturing, traceability, and consumption logic.

Object name: Operations Material Bill

The OMB Header represents the SAP BOM Header (STKO/STAS) associated with a Production Version and must include:

  • A MES‑generated UID
  • SAP BOM identifier (ERP ID)
  • Description
  • Material Definition ID of the header material
  • ERP Source (ECC/S4 instance)
  • Validity dates
  • Publication timestamp
  • Link to the corresponding Operation Definition

This object is the top-level representation of the MES BOM.

Field Definitions (OMB Header)

  1. ID (UID) :System‑generated UUID
  2. ERP Identifier :SAP BOM ID (STKO/STAS key)
  3. Description :Optional SAP BOM description
  4. ERP Source :SAP system identifier (FC1, FC2, S4P01, etc.)
  5. Material Definition ID :The produced material
  6. Use Type :From SAP BOM usage (K,M,T,E,F,,,)
  7. Plant : Plant code 
  8. Alternative BOM: ( STLAL=01 Main BOM , STLAL≠ 01 is alternative BOM)
  9. Published Date :MES ingestion date
  10. EffectiveStartDate : SAP Valid‑From date
  11. EffectiveEndDate :SAP Valid‑To date
  12. OperationDefinitionID : Link to Production Version in MES

titre: Build Material Bill Items
description:
As a

MES PO

I want

MES X.0 to ingest and maintain OperationsMaterialBillItem objects (the component list) from SAP ECC/S4 BOMs according to ISA‑95 OperationsMaterialBillItem (6.1.4).

So that

MES can correctly identify all components consumed or materials produced, including quantities, UoM, and assembly type, relationships required for manufacturing, traceability, execution, and reporting.

Object name: Operations Material Bill Item

Each Operations Material Bill Item represents a SAP BOM item (STPO) associated with an OMB header.

MES must ingest:

  • Component material
  • Use type : "consumed" for the components, "produced" for the material produced
  • Assembly type :  Physical / Logical
  • Quantity + UOM
  • SAP BOM Item Number
  • Validity dates
  • Parent OperationsMaterialBill ID (foreign key)
  • ERP Source

MES must also handle:

  • Phantom components
  • Multi-level BOM explosions
  • Component allocation to operation segments (future enrichment via Work Master)

Field Definitions (OMB Item)

  1. ID (UID) : System‑generated
  2. MaterialDefinitionID :Component material
  3. Quantity : SAP STPO-MENGE
  4. Quantity UOM : STPO-MEINS
  5. Published Date
  6. EffectiveStartDate
  7. EffectiveEndDate
  8. OperationsMaterialBillID :OMB header reference
  9. ERP Source

description:
In this user story, we will implement the hierarchy integration use case using a single standardized data model.

All hierarchy layers will be represented in one table called Equipment.

Equipment Table Structure

The Equipment table will contain the following columns:

  • ID
    Unique identifier of the equipment.

  • Code
    Business code of the equipment.
    This field may contain:

    • Plant code

    • UAP code (from SAP)

    • Production Line code (from SAP)

    • Work Center code (from SAP)

    • Work Unit code

    • Storage location

  • Description
    Business description of the equipment.
    This field may contain:

    • Plant description

    • UAP description

    • Production Line description

    • Work Center description

    • Work Unit description

    • Storage location Description


  • Equipment Level
    Defines the hierarchy level of the equipment.
    Possible values:

    • Site

    • Area (UAP)

    • Production Line

    • Work Center

    • Work Unit

    • Storage location

  • Equipment Class
    Reference to the Equipment Class table.
    The value stored is the ID of the corresponding equipment class, selected based on the appropriate description.

           The Work Center can have multiple equipment class because it can play 2 roles workcenter and Work Unit
            The equipment Class of the Work Unit can be Production or packing
Parent

  • Reference to the parent equipment ID.
    The hierarchy rules are:

    • Site → parent of UAP 

    • UAP → parent of Production Line

    • Production Line → parent of Work Center

    • Work Center → parent of Work Unit

    • Site → Storage location


  • Plant
    Plant code to which the equipment belongs.

Additional Rules

  • An equipment may have no parent, except for Work Units, which must always have a parent.

  • An equipment may be the parent of multiple child equipment.

  • if an equipment doesn't have a parent, it will be linked to plant code

Hierarchy Definition and Data Sources

The hierarchy is defined by the following layers:

Site

  • Created in MES X.0

  • Integrated from SAP IDoc LOIWCS

[Dev]Handle event reprocessing
description:
✅ Concise Summary of Your Ingestion Steps

1. Receive incoming events (high-burst input)

Accept events from both shift_tracking and shift_tracking_status.

Buffer events into batches (size tuned for throughput & Cosmos RU stability).

 

2. Process batch

2.1 Attempt batch insert into Azure SQL

 

If success → done.

If failure → check SQL error type.

 

3. If Azure SQL batch fails → determine error category

3.1 Transient Azure SQL errors → Retry (async)

Retry only for SQL transient error classes: To Be Defined

After 3 retries @ 100ms, 300ms, 900ms→ treat as temporary system failure → send whole batch to DLQ.

 

3.2 Permanent Azure SQL errors → isolate bad record

Permanent errors include:

Constraint violations

Unique key conflicts

FK errors

Invalid data

Malformed values

 

Action:

 

Switch to per-event processing, find the “guilty” record.

Store the bad record in CosmosDB (error store).

Successfully ingest remaining valid records.

 

4. CosmosDB throttling during error storage

This is separate from SQL errors.

If Cosmos returns:

 

429 (throttling) → retry using header x-ms-retry-after-ms

 

5. If batch still fails after SQL transient retries → send to DLQ

 

DLQ partition count starts at 1

Scale partitions could be done later if replay throughput becomes a problem

 

Another container app “rsrce_dlq_processor” will process the DLQ later.

 

6. Main ingestion continues

Even if:

 

SQL is slow

Cosmos throttles

DLQ grows

Error records exist

 

➡️ No blockage. No accumulated latency. Near real-time preserved.

In DLQ Processor, if db error still persists after retries, let the readiness probe manage:

Recommended defaults for DLQ worker

  • Attempt 1: after 5s ± 50% jitter
  • Attempt 2: after 15s ± 50%
  • Attempt 3: after 30s ± 50%

[Analysis]--Performance Optimization Strategy
description:
FYI
@ABASSI Chifa @KHEMIRI Karima

Strategic Technical Analysis: MES Data Architecture & Risk Mitigation

1. Impact Analysis: JSON Storage Performance

Binary Efficiency (JSONB) vs. Text Parsing The primary disadvantage of traditional SQL Server is its text-based JSON handling (NVARCHAR). In that environment, every query requires the engine to parse a string from scratch to find a value. In contrast, PostgreSQL utilizes JSONB (Binary JSON).

  • Storage Optimization: PostgreSQL stores data in a pre-parsed binary format.

  • Impact: This eliminates the "Query Complexity" and "CPU Overhead" found in SQL Server, allowing for NoSQL-like retrieval speeds within a robust relational framework.

Update Performance & Atomic Operations In SQL Server, updating a single field within a JSON document typically triggers a full rewrite of the text string. PostgreSQL handles these operations at the binary level:

  • Partial Updates: Modification of a specific attribute (e.g., a machine's current OEE or temperature) occurs without re-serializing the entire document.

  • Concurrency: This prevents the locking issues and transaction log bloat common in high-frequency manufacturing environments where machine statuses change every second.

The GIN Index Advantage Relational databases traditionally struggle to index semi-structured data. SQL Server requires "Computed Columns" to index JSON, which creates a rigid schema and high maintenance overhead.

  • PostgreSQL GIN Indexes: A single Generalized Inverted Index on a JSONB column automatically indexes every nested key and value.

  • Result: This provides immediate filtering and search capabilities for complex ISA-95 equipment properties without requiring manual schema adjustments every time a new sensor is added.

2. Why PostgreSQL is Superior to Cosmos DB (SQL API) for ISA-95

While Cosmos DB offers horizontal scaling, it is a document-oriented system that introduces specific risks for an MES:

  • Relational Integrity for ISA-95 Level 4: Manufacturing data requires strict consistency for production orders and material tracking. PostgreSQL provides immediate ACID compliance across related tables, whereas Cosmos DB often relies on eventual consistency, which can lead to data integrity gaps in a factory setting.

  • Join Performance: The ISA-95 hierarchy (Site > Area > Line) requires joining multiple levels of data. In Cosmos DB, these "Joins" are computationally expensive and can cause unpredictable spikes in Request Unit (RU) costs. PostgreSQL is architecturally optimized for these hierarchical joins at a predictable performance level.

  • Schema Governance: PostgreSQL allows us to enforce JSON Schema Validation at the database level. This ensures that our shop-floor data remains flexible but always follows our standardized naming conventions, a feature that is harder to manage in a purely schema-less Cosmos DB environment.

3. Migration Risk Analysis: The Path to Graph DB

A critical factor in this decision is ensuring we are not "locked in." If the system eventually requires a transition to a Graph Database for deep genealogy or traceability, PostgreSQL offers the lowest friction for three reasons:

  1. Recursive Logic Compatibility: The ISA-95 hierarchy is essentially a tree (a subset of a graph). PostgreSQL handles this natively through Recursive CTEs. The logic written for these queries maps almost 1:1 to Graph traversal logic, unlike SQL Server’s more cumbersome hierarchical support.

  2. Relational-to-Graph Mapping: PostgreSQL’s strict enforcement of UUIDs and clean relational keys ensures that data can be exported as "Nodes" and "Edges" without heavy data cleansing. Since JSONB is a structured object, properties can move to a Graph DB with zero transformation loss.

  3. Open-Standard Portability: Moving away from a proprietary ecosystem like SQL Server or a vendor-specific API like Cosmos DB is often difficult. PostgreSQL is open-source and follows global standards, ensuring our core data logic remains portable to any future graph-based technology.

Conclusion & Recommendation

PostgreSQL represents the lowest-risk, highest-performance choice for a modern MES. It effectively bridges the gap between traditional SQL and NoSQL.

Proposed Strategy:

  • Standardize on PostgreSQL: Utilize JSONB for flexible ISA-95 equipment attributes while maintaining relational columns for stable transactional data.

  • Ensure Decoupling: Use the Repository Pattern in our application layer to keep business logic independent of the database engine.

  • Long-term Safety: This architecture delivers the immediate performance of a document store with the long-term safety of a relational engine, providing a seamless bridge to a Graph DB if our scaling needs evolve.

Link between BOm and operation definition ID : the link between the operation definiton and the BOM is by material, plant, Bom usage and alternative bom

Versioning / Multi-Level BOM

  • MES stores BOMs as single-level structures received from SAP

  • MES detects multi-level BOMs by linking components to other BOM headers

=>If a component material exists as an OperationsMaterialBill header → it is a subassembly

Phantom rule:

A
 ├─ B (phantom)
 │   ├─ C
 │   └─ D
 └─ E
since we don't receive the multilevel bom from SAP so we will save everything at MES side
 If the phantom material has a corresponding OperationsMaterialBill in MES, the execution engine shall dynamically explode the structure and consume the lower-level components instead. like the schema below:
A
 ├─ C
 ├─ D
 └─ E

The mandatory checks to validate the BOM inetgration:
1- in this use case only the IDOC TYPE BOMMAT are inetgrated
2-MATNR, WERKS, STLAN, STLAL, STLNR and DATUV shouldn't be NULL else reject the BOM
3-If MaterialDefinitionID not found in MES → Reject BOM
4- the business key for the BOM are: Material + Plant + Bom Usage + alternative BOM+EffectiveStartDate
if the same key exists than an update is needed else create new BOM
Validity dates are used to track BOM versions
5- if the system cannot find a match with the operation definition than the integration of the IDOC shouldn't be blocked 
6- BOM must contain at least one component (At least one E1STPOM must exist)
7- if IDoc already processed => Prevent duplicate processing
8- for the failed IDOC the reprocess will be treated in a separate more generic user story
9- in case we have a change in the validity dates or the component or qty component a new BOM needs to insert
