[Dev] Integrate Hierarchy from SAP using ISA 95 Equipment Data Model
description:
1. The application listens on two Dapr HTTP endpoints in the controller: one dedicated to LOIWCS, one to LOIRNH,. All  two immediately delegate to the same generic flow, processIdocEvent(), so the ingestion algorithm starts from a single entry point instead of having family-specific controller logic. That entry point is in dapr.controller.ts.
  2. Inside processIdocEvent(), the first real step is payload validation and parsing. The controller expects an EventHub-shaped envelope and checks that body exists; then it parses body from JSON string to object if needed. If the body is empty or invalid JSON, the integration stops immediately and the request is rejected. This is still in dapr.controller.ts.
  3. Once the raw IDoc object is parsed, the controller asks the handler registry to identify which handler should process it. The registry keeps known handlers in priority order, currently preferring LOIWCS v3 before LOIWCS v2, then LOIRNH v1, and it calls canHandle() on each until one matches. That means version/family detection is not hardcoded in the controller; it is delegated to the registry and handler layer in idoc-handler-registry.service.ts.
  4. The selected handler then recognizes the exact IDoc structure. For example, the LOIWCS v3 handler first verifies that the payload belongs to the LOIWCS family, then checks whether ZMII_E1CRHDL is nested under E1CRHDL, which is the real ZLOIWCS3-style structure. The LOIRNH handler is simpler: it just confirms the payload belongs to the LOIRNH family. Those checks live in loiwcs-v3.handler.ts and loirnh-v1.handler.ts.
  5. After detection, the handler does not parse fields itself. Instead, it forwards the parsed IDoc plus its mapping configuration and version string to the generic extractor. This is the main design point of the refactor: handlers decide “which format is this?”, while the extractor decides “how do I flatten it?”. The extraction engine is implemented in configurable-idoc-extractor.service.ts.
  6. The extractor first normalizes the envelope before reading fields. Its unwrapRootKey() method handles payloads like { ZLOIWCS3: { IDOC: ... } } or { LOIRNH01: { IDOC: ... } } by unwrapping the outer root key so the rest of the algorithm can consistently work from the IDOC node. Then it applies mapping-based path resolution, supports array handling, supports “pick first item with property”, and supports nested property extraction such as E1CRTXL[].KTEXT. This generic flattening logic is also in configurable-idoc-extractor.service.ts.
  7. If the source table is LOIWCS, the extractor produces a single flat record by merging the configured segments into one equipment payload. In practice, that means values such as SNDPOR, ARBPL, WERKS, OBJID, VERWE, KTEXT, PARV6, and VGWTS are pulled from the IDoc and written into one normalized record. If the source table is LOIRNH, the extractor instead emits one flat record per hierarchy relation segment, and it filters out SAP root nodes where OBJID_UP = '00000000' so they are not persisted as real business hierarchy links. That branching is in configurable-idoc-extractor.service.ts.
  8. The controller receives the flattened records and starts processing each one. Before calling the business layer, it derives the topic name, emits telemetry for “received”, and routes each record by its internal metadata field __source_table: LOIWCS records go to handleEquipment(), and LOIRNH records go to handleHierarchy(). This routing logic is in dapr.controller.ts.
  9. The domain handler is the bridge between generic flat records and the existing ISA-95 persistence logic. It first validates that the minimum required fields exist, then converts the flat record into the existing DTO shape expected by the equipment service. For LOIWCS it builds an IdocLoiwcsDto; for LOIRNH it builds an IdocLoirnhDto. That conversion and validation step is in idoc-domain-handler.service.ts.
  10. For LOIWCS, the business flow ends in upsertEquipment(). That method resolves VERWE to the internal ISA-95 level/class id, upserts the main isa95.equipment row using sapObjId as the conflict key, reloads the saved equipment id, upserts the equipment-class relation, and optionally upserts extra properties such as cost center and standard value key. So the final result of a LOIWCS integration is an idempotent equipment upsert enriched with classification and optional properties. That logic is in isa95-equipment.service.ts.
  11. For LOIRNH, the business flow ends in linkHierarchy(). That method resolves the child and parent equipment from the database, primarily by sapObjId, with a fallback parent lookup by site. If either side does not exist yet, it throws NotFoundException, because hierarchy links are only valid after the corresponding equipment records already exist. If both exist, it updates the child’s parentEquipmentId, which completes the hierarchy integration. This is also in isa95-equipment.service.ts.
  12. The last step is result handling in the controller. If a record is processed successfully,: If a hierarchy relation fails only because parent or child is missing, that one record is logged as skipped and marked invalid, but the rest of the batch continues. Any other unexpected error bubbles up and fails the request. This final control flow is in dapr.controller.ts.

description:
In a JIT plant, the user want to identify tickets that were opened and automatically classified by machine, and detect those exceeding a defined duration threshold,

so that he can better monitor and manage long-running machine-generated tickets.

Configuration Requirement

In this user story we will manage the configuration:

    • Name: Downtime Ticket Reclassification Threshold
    • Unit: Seconds
    • Default Value: 300 seconds

titre: [BA Design] [Downtime list] Add new column & filter for JIT
description:
Objective

Enable users to easily identify and filter tickets that require manual reclassification, based on specific conditions.

Scope

  • Applies only when: resource_type = JIT
  • How to determine:
    • Check the type in the resource table in the HRY Domain
    • Only resources with type = JIT will display this feature
  • Not visible or usable for other resource types

New Column

  • Name: ticket to classify
  • Type: Boolean (true / false)
  • Visibility: Displayed only for JIT resources

Filter

  • The column should be filterable
  • Users can filter by:
    • true → tickets needing reclassification
    • false → other tickets

Business Logic

A ticket is marked as “ticket to classify” = true if it meets both conditions:

  1. Overtime Condition
    • Ticket duration exceeds a defined threshold
    • How to check:
      • Use the duration column from the down_time_ticket table in the PRD Domain
      • Compare with the threshold defined in this user story: US 148549
    • Logic: Ticket duration > Threshold
  2. Classified by Machine Condition
    • The ticket was last managed (opened or classified) by a machine
    • How to check:
      • Use the user_id column in the down_time_ticket table in the PRD Domain
      • Identify machine actions by checking if user_id = TAG or user_id = API_NTRS

description:
Context

For resources with resource_type = JIT, tickets are automatically declared and initially classified by the machine based on connectivity data. However, this classification is only an approximation and may require manual reclassification by the user.

Objective

Be able to clearly identify tickets that require classification or reclassification,
So that user can quickly review, and correct machine generated classifications when needed.

Requirements
  • Keep the column title “UC Ticket” notification For resource_type = JIT and for non-JIT resources.
Column Behavior (UC Ticket Column)
1- For JIT Resources
Check on the resource type:
  • Applies only when: resource_type = JIT
  • How to determine:
    • Check the type in the resource table in the HRY Domain
    • Only resources with type = JIT 
Check on the notification:
  • The UC ticket column should display:
    • The number of tickets:
      • Created within the current hour: check the column start_date in down_time_ticket table in PRD domain. The notification should be counted in the hour only when the ticket is started.
      • Already classified by the machine: Check the column user_id in down_time_ticket table in PRD domain. The user_id should be = TAG or API_NTRS
      • AND considered “overtime”: Check the column duration in down_time_ticket table in PRD domain. If the duration > threshold, then the ticket is requiring a reclassification.
2- For Non-JIT Resources

Check on the resource type:
  • Applies only when: resource_type != JIT
  • How to determine:
    • Check the type in the resource table in the HRY Domain
    • Only resources with type!= JIT 
Check on the notification:
  • No change:
  • Continue displaying: Number of unclassified tickets within the last hour
Click Behavior (Redirection)
1- For JIT Resources
  • Clicking the UC ticket count should:
    • Redirect the user to: Downtime classification page
    • Open:
      • The most recent ticket of the hour
      • That matches the Resource & Requires reclassification
2- For Non-JIT Resources
  • No change:
  • Redirect to the most recent unclassified ticket

[Dev] Adjust the update on the shift SPEED for the previous hours
description:
Analyses: 

🎯 Context
Currently, two use cases are supported for setting configurations:
1. Configuration on the Current Hour
2. Configuration on the Previous Hour of the Current Shift

✅ Use Case 1: Current Hour
  • The configuration is set using the transaction:
    SC_MES_API/INTERFACE/EPARTBOARD/V1/INSERT_ACTION
  • This transaction:
    • Inserts a record into the ACTION_ON_PROD table in SAP MII
  • Then:
    • The job SAVE_CURRENT_HOUR (executed every minute)
    • Updates the Speed value in the SHIFT_TRACKING_STATUS table

✔️ Result: This use case is working as expected


❌ Use Case 2: Previous Hour of Current Shift
  • The same transaction is used:
    SC_MES_API/INTERFACE/EPARTBOARD/V1/INSERT_ACTION
  • The record is correctly inserted into ACTION_ON_PROD
  • However:
    • The From Timestamp is < current time
    • As a result, it is not processed by the SAVE_CURRENT_HOUR job

❌ Result: This use case is not working

⚠️ Root Cause

The SAVE_CURRENT_HOUR job only processes records related to the current hour and ignores any entries with a timestamp in the past.


Proposed Solution

After analysis on the MII side,
we propose to use the following transaction:

SC_COMPONENTS/DASHBOARD/DMC_EPARTBOARD/QUERY/V2/XCT_SAVE_MODEL

Transaction Behavior

This transaction perform:

1. Overlap Check
  • Verifies if a similar configuration already exists in the ACTION_ON_PROD table
  • If an overlap is detected → ❌ an error message is returned
2. Data Insertion
  • Inserts a new record into the ACTION_ON_PROD table
3. Processing Logic
  • The transaction evaluates the From Timestamp: 
 
 
 
IF From Timestamp < Current Time
   → Call job GET_SHIFT_TRACKING_INFO
   → Job updates the Speed value in SHIFT_TRACKING_STATUS
ELSE
   → No further action

So, this transaction supports both use cases:
    • Current hour
    • Previous hour of the shift

[Live Status] [Analysis] Design - x resources design V1
description:
✅ Live Status × Resources Analysis

1. Overview

The Live Status screen provides a consolidated, real‑time view of all resources belonging to a selected GAP.
It displays shift-level KPIs per resource, global GAP KPIs, and provides quick access to each resource’s detailed dashboard.

✅ 2. Functional Scope

2.1 GAP Selection

  • The GAP can be selected in two ways:
    • By entering the GAP ID in the URL: /live-status/:gapId
    • By selecting the GAP from the existing dropdown
  • The dropdown must be updated to ensure:
    • It loads dynamic GAPs
    • Selecting a GAP triggers Live Status refresh
    • URL updates automatically to reflect selected GAP

2.2 Resource Display

Each resource (machine) is displayed as a card containing shift-level KPIs:

  • Target
  • Production
  • Delta
  • Scrap
  • Status timeline bar (hour-by-hour color segments)
  • Status color / card border color
  • Resource name / description

2.3 Header KPIs

The top of the screen shows GAP-wide KPIs:

  • First OK
  • Routine
  • TPM
  • Management Control
  • Alerts (categorized)

2.4 Navigation

  • Clicking a resource card opens its existing detailed view.
  • Navigation occurs in the same tab.
  • Expected pattern: /edashboard/:gapId/:resourceId (to be confirmed by business).

2.5 Auto-Refresh

  • Live Status automatically refreshes every 1 minute.

✅ 3. Backend Work 

3.1 Wrapper Endpoint: Resource KPIs

A new lightweight wrapper is required to provide the UI with all card KPIs in one call, by:

  • Retrieving resources assigned to the GAP
  • Aggregating hourly data to compute:
    • Shift Target (sum of hourly target)
    • Shift Production (sum of hourly production)
    • Shift Delta (sum of hourly delta)
  • Fetching scrap from existing API
  • Building the status timeline from hourly “status” values
  • Applying existing card color/status rules
  • Returning a compact, UI-friendly structure

Note: This reuses all existing KPI logic from the detailed view. No new business rules.

3.2 Wrapper Endpoint: Header KPIs

Another small wrapper bundles GAP-level KPIs (First OK, Routine, TPM, MC, Alerts) into a single response.
Reuses existing detailed view logic.

✅ 4. Frontend

4.1 New Route

Add a route for: 

/live-status/:gapId

4.2 Data Loading

On page load (or dropdown change), UI calls:

  1. Resources list (existing)
  2. All resource KPIs (new wrapper)
  3. Header KPIs (new wrapper)

Then merges the results to render the screen.

4.3 UI Components

  • Live Status page layout
  • Resource card component
  • Header KPI component
  • Timeline bar renderer

4.4 GAP Dropdown

Modify existing dropdown to:

  • Load available GAPs dynamically
  • Update the URL on selection
  • Trigger Live Status reload
  • Remain synchronized with URL navigation

4.5 Auto-Refresh

Refresh data every 1 minute.

5.5 Dropdown

For the gap selection dropdown , we are going to use the same dropdown used in the hierarchy transco.

[Analysis]Review of WK Integration Codebase and Recommendations for Quality & Anomaly Detection
description:
General Recommendation

  • Use SINGLETON for daprClient in all modules
    • This includes services where a new daprClient is currently created per request
    • There is no clear need for per-request instantiation

WSDL Module

  • Remove formatting and logic from the controller; move it to the service
  • The WSDL controller endpoint is calling a method from another service
  • File
    mesx-wk-integration-backend/src/module/wsdl/mii-automatic-integration-wsdl.ts
    • Is not used
    • Is confusing to keep in the codebase
    • Consider removing it
  • Endpoint /wsdl/process-orders-preactor
    • Is not directly referenced inside MESX
    • Most likely used by an external application

Shop Order Module

  • Nothing special
  • Only read logic is present

Reprocess Module

  • No usage found inside MESX
    • Possibly triggered from a third-party application
  • Endpoint /reprocess/buffer
    • No plant filter
    • This can cause issues if several plants declare WKs with the same ID

WK Integration Module

Dapr Client Usage

  • A new daprClient is created per request for most endpoints
  • There is no clear need for this
  • Reusing a singleton should be sufficient
Following endpoints have been analyzed for WK Integration:

/wk-integration/close-wk/:plant

  • Scheduled as a job in the custom scheduler to close WKs
  • On each execution:
    • Plant details are retrieved
      • These can be cached either:
        • On first execution, or
        • At application startup
          (application restart required if plant details change)
    • isApiManagerEnabled and mesUserName are retrieved every time
      • These can also be cached

/wk-integration/:plant

  • Scheduled as a job in the custom scheduler
  • Automatically integrates WKs from the buffer

Possible caching:

  • Secrets
  • Offsets (with TTL)
  • plantData / plantLink (with TTL)

Logic flow:

  • Retrieve list of WKs from buffer
  • Update WK status to IN_PROGRESS
  • Send all WKs to MII
  • Wait a maximum of X seconds for response
  • Update WKs in MESX based on the MII response

/wk-integration/automatic-wk-integration-preactor

  • Used for ad‑hoc integration of a specified XML document
  • Mostly used by Preactor, but not limited to it

Code and logic improvements:

  • Methods parseAndDecode and extractGeneralData
    • Can be combined to simplify logic
  • Results can be cached to avoid repeated external calls:
    • getPlantById (cache at startup or per request, with max size limit)
    • getPlantConfigFlags (same caching strategy)

Kanban Processing Logic for the list of kanbans specified in XML document

Initial Split

  • All kanbans are split into two lists:
    • Rescheduled kanbans
    • Creation / deletion kanbans

Creation / Deletion Kanbans

  • Processed item-by-item
  • Concurrency: 100
    • This is too high
    • 10–20 would be more appropriate

Validation:

  • Each kanban is validated against KANBAN_VALIDATION_SCHEMA
    • Schema maps field type and length
    • Order of validated fields is defined in the schema
    • Each validated property is appended to an internal object
    • actionType is verified before being appended
      • This is NOK, but works due to correct field order in the schema

Deletion case

  • Only OrderID must:
    • Be non-empty
    • Not exceed max length defined in the schema
  • The in-app object createBufferTableDto contains only:
    • plant
    • actionType
    • orderId
  • All other properties are ignored

Creation case

  • All fields are validated individually
  • createBufferTableDto is built incrementally
  • Mandatory fields:
    • actionType
    • orderId
    • materialNumber
    • productionLine
    • sourceLocation
    • destinationLocation
    • startPickingDatetime
    • endPickingDatetime
    • launchingDatetime
    • quantity

Extra validations (using cache, no limits — cache is per request):

  • Batch
    • If batch is empty:
      • Retrieve bbbMode
      • If mode = 400
      • If source location (taken directly from XML, not from validated object) is non-poolstock
      • → Generate error
  • Customer
    • Existence is checked if customer is specified
  • Source / Destination Location
    • Verify existence of combination:
      • plant
      • materialNumber (taken directly from XML node)
      • storageLocation
    • Error if not found or check fails
  • Delivery Number
    • Checks OD and TPA number for emptiness
    • Condition does not match the comment
    • Currently:
      • Error is generated if only one field is filled
      • Error message states both cannot be empty
      • Accepted cases are:
        • Both filled
        • Both empty
    • When both are filled:
      • Verify existence of combination:
        • plant
        • materialNumber (from XML)
        • od (from XML)
      • Error if not found
      • Error if status is one of:
        • CLOSEDSAP
        • CLOSEDMII
        • PICKCLOSED
    • Additional error if plant-level setting mandatoryDatesFromPreactor is enabled and:
      • TruckDepartureDateTime (from XML) is missing
      • EndPreparationDateTime (from XML) is missing
  • Production Line
    • Verify existence of combination:
      • plant
      • workcenter
    • Error if not found

Datetime validation:

  • Start/end datetime pairs:
    • startPickingDatetime / endPickingDatetime
    • startProductionDatetime / endProductionDatetime
  • End date must not be before start date

After all validations:

  • bufferStatus is determined based on generated errors
  • There is also a case where current bufferStatus is checked
    • It is unclear where this value could have been set previously
  • The in-app object is then stored in the DB

Rescheduled Kanbans

  • Processed in batches of 20
  • Concurrency: 5

Logic:

  • Same validations as creation
  • WKs are split into two categories:
    • WKs with validation errors or not existing in MESX (bufferWKNotExist which is stored in mesx buffer table)
    • WKs with no errors and existing in MESX:
      • Stored in bufferTableDtos (stored to mesx buffer table but with status updated by MII from below request)
      • Also added to kanbanWithBbbMode (this one is sent to MII on the spot)

Key difference vs creation/deletion:

  • Rescheduling is executed immediately  when the endpoint is triggered (for kanbans with no errors and which exist in system)
  • Creation/deletion is scheduled for later
  • Reason for this difference is unclear and should be clarified

description:
Proposed Refactoring Strategy

The key observation: all LOIWCS variants share the same MESTYP (LOIWCS) and differ only in structural details like CIMTYP. Here's my proposal for a more generic handler approach:

Problem with Current Design

  • Separate handlers for v2 and v3 have duplicated code and similar logic
  • Version-specific canHandle() methods that detect structure differences
  • Hard to extend when new versions arrive
  • The registry needs to maintain references to all version instances

Generic Handler Proposal

Create two unified handlers instead of multiple versioned ones:

  1. LoiwcsHandler (replaces v2 + v3)
    • Single handler for all LOIWCS message types
    • Auto-detects structure variant and selects appropriate mapping
    • No version naming in the class
  1. LoirnhHandler (replaces v1)
    • Single handler for all LOIRNH message types
    • Simple structure detection
    • Implementation Structure
Benefits
✅ Single responsibility: One handler per IDoc family type
✅ Extensible: Add new variants by extending the variants array
✅ No duplication: Shared family pattern and extractor logic
✅ Future-proof: Easy to detect new CIMTYP variants without new handler classes
✅ Cleaner registry: One handler instance per family instead of multiple per version

// Before
this.register('LOIWCS::v2', this.loiwcsV2);
this.register('LOIWCS::v3', this.loiwcsV3);
this.priorityHandlers.push(this.loiwcsV3, this.loiwcsV2);

// After
this.register('LOIWCS', this.loiwcs);
this.priorityHandlers.push(this.loiwcs);

Handler Map Strategy Pattern

The Handler Map Strategy Pattern replaces conditional logic (if/else or switch) with a mapping object that associates keys to handler functions.
  /**
   * Source table handler mapping (Strategy pattern)
   * Maps IDoc source table names to their corresponding domain handlers
   * Easy to extend with new handlers without modifying the routing logic
   */
  private readonly sourceTableHandlers: Record<
    string,
    (record: IdocConvertedRecord) => Promise<void>
  > = {
    LOIRNH: (record) => this.domainHandler.handleHierarchy(record),
    LOIWCS: (record) => this.domainHandler.handleEquipment(record),
  };

How It Works
Before (If/Else)
if (sourceTable === 'LOIRNH') {
  await this.domainHandler.handleHierarchy(record);
} else if (sourceTable === 'LOIWCS') {
  await this.domainHandler.handleEquipment(record);
} else {
  throw new Error(`Unknown source table: ${sourceTable}`);
}

Why It's Better ✨
AspectIf/ElseHandler Map
Readability Scattered logic Centralized, declarative
Extensibility Add conditions Add map entries
Maintainability Hard to track all branches Single source of truth
Testability Mock multiple branches Mock/replace map
Performance O(n) comparisons O(1) lookup

Key Benefits
  • Declarative: What handlers exist is immediately visible in the map
  • Scalable: New handlers just require adding a map entry
  • DRY: No repeated condition checks
  • Type-safe: TypeScript validates all functions have same signature
  • Follows Open/Closed Principle: Open for extension (add handlers), closed for modification (no logic changes)
  • In your case: When you add a new IDoc type (e.g., LOINSPECT), you just add one line to the map instead of adding new if/else branches.

description: We implemented the ISA95 material model by creating and linking these entities: MaterialDefinition (core material record), MaterialDescriptionByLanguage (language-specific descriptions per material), MaterialClass (material classification), PropertyDataType (allowed data type dictionary), MaterialClassProperty (property definition tied to a class and a data type), MaterialMaterialClass (join between material and class), and MaterialProperty (material-level property values/JSON tied to material and class). The relationships were set from the data model using foreign keys and uniqueness constraints, then seeding was aligned to that structure with ordered, key-based references so parent/master entities are loaded first and dependent entities are linked consistently.​

titre: [Dev] MESX Equipment Model Configuration Object Definition - APIs
description:
🏭 ISA-95 Equipment Model - API Catalog

Base Path: /isa95-equipment-model

Base URL Pattern: METHOD /isa95-equipment-model/...

📌 Summary

  • Total endpoints: 45

  • Pagination: Available on /with-relations endpoints (?limit default 50, max 200; ?offset default 0).

  • JSON Operations: Equipment properties now support key-level read/merge/delete via /.../:id/json-properties routes, optimized via SQL Server JSON_VALUE and JSON_MODIFY.

  • Path params: All :id values are integers.

1) Hierarchy & Discovery

Retrieve the structural tree of the equipment model.

POST /getRestrictedHierarchy

Returns the nested tree (SITE → AREA → LINE → CELL). Ancestors of matching nodes are always included to preserve context.

ParameterWhereTypeRequiredDescription
siteQuerystringNoFilter tree to one site (e.g. S001).
equipmentCodeBodystringNoReturn only the specific node.
equipmentIdBodystringNoSubtree rooted at this ID.
equipmentLevelCodeBodystringNoFilter by level (e.g. LINE).
equipmentClassCodeBodystringNoFilter by assigned class code.

2) Equipment (Physical Nodes)

Physical instances in the hierarchy. Equipment is site-scoped.

  • POST /equipment: Create a node. (Unique: site + code + levelId).

  • GET /equipment: List all (Flat).

  • GET /equipment/with-relations: Paginated list with levels, parents, and classes.

  • GET /equipment/:id: Single record (Flat).

  • GET /equipment/:id/with-relations: Single record with all nested data.

  • PATCH /equipment/:id: Partial update of fields.

  • DELETE /equipment/:id: Permanent removal.

3) Equipment Classes & Assignments

Global templates (CUST_ prefix applied automatically) and their links to equipment.

Classes

  • POST /equipment-classes: Create a class template.

  • GET /equipment-classes/with-relations: Paginated list with taxonomy and properties.

  • GET /equipment-classes/:id/with-relations: Full class schema and assigned members.

Assignments (Linking)

  • POST /equipment-equipment-classes: Assign a class to an equipment instance.

  • GET /by-equipment/:equipmentId: Find all classes for a specific node.

  • GET /by-class/:equipmentClassId: Find all equipment assigned to a class.

  • DELETE /by-pair/:equipmentId/:equipmentClassId: Remove assignment by the pair IDs.

4) Equipment Properties (Runtime Values)

Stores actual data values as a JSON object per (equipment, class) pair.

Full Document Operations

  • POST /equipment-properties: Create a new value record with propertiesJson.

  • PATCH /equipment-properties/:id: Full replacement of the JSON document.

Key-Level Operations (SQL Optimized)

Perform atomic updates without loading or rewriting the entire JSON document.

GET /.../:id/json-properties?keys=K1,K2

Retrieves only specified keys.

  • Benefit: Uses JSON_VALUE for high-speed, low-memory extraction.

PATCH /.../:id/json-properties

Merges specific key-value pairs.

  • Body: { "properties": { "KEY": "VALUE" } }

  • Behavior: Uses JSON_MODIFY. Overwrites existing keys; creates new ones; leaves others untouched.

DELETE /.../:id/json-properties

Removes specific keys.

  • Body: { "keys": ["KEY1", "KEY2"] }

  • Behavior: Atomic removal of keys using JSON_MODIFY(..., NULL).

5) Reference Data

ResourceMethodsPurpose
Equipment LevelsGET, POST, PATCH, DELETETier definitions (SITE, AREA, etc.).
Property Data TypesGET, POST, PATCH, DELETEData formats (STRING, NUMBER, etc.).
Class PropertiesGET, POST, PATCH, DELETEDefine the schema (keys) for a class.

Error Codes

StatusMeaningOccurrence
200/201OK / CreatedSuccess.
400Bad RequestValidation failure (Schema or Query).
404Not FoundID does not exist.
409ConflictUnique key violation (Code already exists).
500Server ErrorUnexpected database or logic failure.

titre: [Dev] Material Model Configuration-APIs
description:
# ISA95 Material Model CRUD APIs

## Material Class

1. `POST /classes` and `POST /isa95-material-model/classes`  
   Create a material class.
2. `GET /classes` and `GET /isa95-material-model/classes`  
   List material classes with filtering and pagination.
3. `GET /classes/with-relations` and `GET /isa95-material-model/classes/with-relations`  
   List material classes with nested relations.
4. `GET /classes/:classUid` and `GET /isa95-material-model/classes/:classUid`  
   Get one material class by uid.
5. `GET /classes/:classUid/with-relations` and `GET /isa95-material-model/classes/:classUid/with-relations`  
   Get one material class with nested relations.
6. `PATCH /classes/:classUid` and `PATCH /isa95-material-model/classes/:classUid`  
   Update one material class by uid.
7. `DELETE /classes/:classUid` and `DELETE /isa95-material-model/classes/:classUid`  
   Delete one material class by uid.

## Material Class Property

1. `GET /property-data-types`  
   List property data types for property creation/editing.
2. `POST /classes/:classUid/properties`  
   Create a property under a specific material class.
3. `GET /classes/:classUid/properties`  
   List properties of a specific material class with pagination/filter/search.
4. `GET /properties/:propertyUid`  
   Get one material class property by uid.
5. `PATCH /properties/:propertyUid`  
   Update one material class property by uid.
6. `DELETE /properties/:propertyUid`  
   Delete one material class property by uid.

## Material Definition

1. `POST /isa95-material-model/material-definition` and `POST /isa95-material-model/material-definitions`  
   Create a material definition.
2. `GET /isa95-material-model/material-definition` and `GET /isa95-material-model/material-definitions`  
   List material definitions.
3. `GET /isa95-material-model/material-definition/with-relations` and `GET /isa95-material-model/material-definitions/with-relations`  
   List material definitions with nested relations (paginated).
4. `GET /isa95-material-model/material-definition/:id` and `GET /isa95-material-model/material-definitions/:id`  
   Get one material definition by id.
5. `GET /isa95-material-model/material-definition/:id/with-relations` and `GET /isa95-material-model/material-definitions/:id/with-relations`  
   Get one material definition with nested relations.
6. `PATCH /isa95-material-model/material-definition/:id` and `PATCH /isa95-material-model/material-definitions/:id`  
   Update one material definition by id.
7. `DELETE /isa95-material-model/material-definition/:id` and `DELETE /isa95-material-model/material-definitions/:id`  
   Delete one material definition by id.

## Material-MaterialClass Link

1. `POST /isa95-material-model/material-material-class` and `POST /isa95-material-model/material-material-classes`  
   Create a link between material definition and material class.
2. `GET /isa95-material-model/material-material-class` and `GET /isa95-material-model/material-material-classes`  
   List all links.
3. `GET /isa95-material-model/material-material-class/by-material/:materialDefinitionId` and `GET /isa95-material-model/material-material-classes/by-material/:materialDefinitionId`  
   List links by material definition id.
4. `GET /isa95-material-model/material-material-class/by-class/:materialClassId` and `GET /isa95-material-model/material-material-classes/by-class/:materialClassId`  
   List links by material class id.
5. `GET /isa95-material-model/material-material-class/:id` and `GET /isa95-material-model/material-material-classes/:id`  
   Get one link by id.
6. `PATCH /isa95-material-model/material-material-class/:id` and `PATCH /isa95-material-model/material-material-classes/:id`  
   Update one link by id.
7. `DELETE /isa95-material-model/material-material-class/:id` and `DELETE /isa95-material-model/material-material-classes/:id`  
   Delete one link by id.

## Material Property

1. `POST /isa95-material-model/material-properties`  
   Create material property record.
2. `GET /isa95-material-model/material-properties`  
   List material property records.
3. `GET /isa95-material-model/material-properties/:id`  
   Get one material property by id.
4. `PATCH /isa95-material-model/material-properties/:id`  
   Update one material property by id.
5. `DELETE /isa95-material-model/material-properties/:id`  
   Delete one material property by id.
6. `GET /isa95-material-model/material-properties/:id/json-properties?keys=...`  
   Read selected keys from `propertiesJson`.
7. `PATCH /isa95-material-model/material-properties/:id/json-properties`  
   Merge selected keys into `propertiesJson`.
8. `DELETE /isa95-material-model/material-properties/:id/json-properties`  
   Delete selected keys from `propertiesJson`.

## Property Data Type

1. `POST /isa95-material-model/property-data-types`  
   Create property data type.
2. `GET /isa95-material-model/property-data-types`  
   List property data types.
3. `GET /isa95-material-model/property-data-types/:id`  
   Get one property data type by id.
4. `PATCH /isa95-material-model/property-data-types/:id`  
   Update one property data type by id.
5. `DELETE /isa95-material-model/property-data-types/:id`  
   Delete one property data type by id.

[BA Design] [eDashBoard] Notification center - Structure & Lay out
description:
Purpose

As user, I want a chronological log that sums the events and actions related to my selected resource.

Ordering rule

Notifications are displayed from the beginning of the shift, in a chronological ascending order by start_time.

Impacted screens

  • eDashboard: MESX.0 - Epart Board
  • Live Status: MESX.0 - Live Status

Events that trigger a notification

A notification is created when one of these events occurs:

1. Slowdown: 

Positive (+5mn) or negative (-5mn).
Categories :
    • Comment required
    • Comment added

2. Downtime:

Categories:
    • Classified
    • Classification required
    • Remark required

3. Balancing modifications


Notification content

Each notification contains:
  • Start time: HH:mm:ss format
  • Duration 
    • If end time not provided → display "ongoing"
Specific content for each notification type:

1. Slowdown notifications 

  • If uncommented → request the user to add a comment
  • Else (comment exists) → display that it is commented and allow user to edit
    • Note: a slowdown notification containing a request to add a comment is only displayed once, in the start-time hour

    2. Downtime notifications

    • Case 1: Classified ticket
      • If level 1 is IN [cause_1, cause_4, cause_5] and no remark is added → display level 1 classification and request user to add a remark
      • Else display level 1 classification and sublevels
    Note: Classification is indicated using the downtime color code
    • Case 2: Unclassified ticket
      •  Request user to classify

    3. Balancing/configuration notifications 

    Display old and new status, e.g. N- → N+

    Rules and Interactions

    Rules and interactions for each notification type are defined in the following US:
    • Slowdown : User Story 149901 [eDashBoard] Events center - Comment
    • Downtime : User Story 149896 [eDashBoard] Events center - Downtime ticket
    • Configuration : User Story 149902 [eDashBoard] Events center - Configuration

    Access

    There are two ways to access the events center:

    1. Opening from icon

    • Clicking on icon in header > Opens events center (shows the log of events since the beginning of the shift)

    2. Opening from hour lines

    • User clicks on an hour line (any column except for the Config, Alerts, and Comment columns - still in discussion) > Widget launches with following display rules:
      • The widget is adjusted so that the first corresponding hour notification is aligned to the top of the events center
      • User can scroll up/down to see previous/following hour notifications

    Closing the notifications center

    • Automatically closes after a period of inactivity (to be determined)
    • Clicking on the exit icon
    • Clicking elsewhere on the screen

    UX/UI functional description

    Notifications displayed from the beginning of the shift.
    Ordered in a chronological ascending order by start_time and divided by hour ranges.
    Every notification is a widget (rectangle) with:
    • An indication following the downtime color code
    • Additional colors for slowdown and balancing
    For each hour, widgets are stacked so that the one on top is the last notification (latest start_time).
    An icon to expand all notifications in chronological, ascending order by start_time.

    Filters on top

    Buttons that allow multiple selection to select notification types
      • Select All
      • Slowdown
      • Downtime
      • Configuration

    JIT resources

    JIT resources (resource_type = JIT in HRY domain) won't be treated for the time being as it depends on other US development.
    Future intent: keeping current color code but indicating that it is a different ticket and needs reclassification (e.g., blinking / different color).

titre: [Technical Analysis] MBO writeback failure to MII
description:
Issue – Plant 1495

We received information from the 9tech team indicating the presence of multiple red HTTP worker threads originating from the following SAP MII transaction: 

SC_MES_API/ALERT/TRANSACTION/V1/ALERT_AUTO_ESCALATE.trx

Examples observed:

  • HTTP Worker [@284583965] – ALERT_AUTO_ESCALATE.trx
  • HTTP Worker [@2011363325] – ALERT_AUTO_ESCALATE.trx
  • HTTP Worker [@1759264076] – ALERT_AUTO_ESCALATE.trx
  • HTTP Worker [@1365216611] – ALERT_AUTO_ESCALATE.trx

This transaction is executed via: 

SC_MES_API/INTERFACE/ALERT/V1/XCT_ALERT_AUTO_ESCALATE

and is triggered by the MES job automatic-alert-escalation.

Immediate Workaround

  • The automatic-alert-escalation job was stopped from the MES side.
  • Despite stopping the job, residual calls to the transaction continued.
  • As a precautionary measure, the MESXSystem user was locked to prevent further transaction execution.

Analysis & Findings

Job History

After reviewing the job execution history, we identified a high number of failures with the following error:

{
  "error": "Internal Server Error",
  "errorCode": "UNHANDLED_EXCEPTION",
  "message": "Unexpected error occurred",
  "statusCode": 500,
  "path": "/alert/checkForAlertEscalation/1492",
  "timestamp": "2026-04-01T18:17:00.337Z"
}

  • First occurrence: 2026-04-01T18:17:00.366Z

Before this timestamp, job failures were associated with the message: 

"No alerts to escalate or red bell alerts are empty" (
This behavior is considered normal when no eligible alerts are found.)

Alert Data Verification

  • Database validation confirmed the presence of Red Bell alerts eligible for escalation.
  • The first Red Bell alert was created at: 2026-04-01 17:17:02.320 UTC
  • The list of Red Bell alerts is attached for reference.

Application & Container Logs

  • Container-level logs did not show errors related to automatic-alert-escalation.
  • Errors observed in picking-be were related to automatic alert closure, specifically: Repeated HTTP 400 errors calling .../closeAutomaticAlert
  • Some container restarts were caused by health probes, not alert escalation.
  • No relevant errors were found in:
    • picking-jb
    • job-be
    • picking-be
  • At the MII level, errors were found related to SMS sending:

Root Cause Assessment

Direct execution of the transaction in MII with 7 alerts already showed noticeable latency due to the transaction logic:

  • Loop through alerts
  • For each alert, retrieve users
  • Loop through users to send notifications

Example scenario:

  • 44 alerts
  • 3 users per alert
  • → 132 iterations

Since the job runs every 2 minutes, overlapping executions are likely, leading to:

  • Thread saturation
  • Accumulating HTTP workers
  • Near–infinite execution loops

Further investigation identified the primary bottleneck as the call to: 

HTTP_POST_NOTIF_API

This service:

  • Takes a long time to respond
  • Eventually fails
  • Causes transaction execution to stall and overlap

Next Steps:

  1. Temporarily deactivate SMS sending for MES alerts.
  2. Reactivate the automatic-alert-escalation job.
  3. Monitor system behavior and thread usage.
  4. Improve error handling:
    • Handle MII unavailability and timeout scenarios explicitly
    • Replace generic UNHANDLED_EXCEPTION with clearer, actionable error messages

titre: Support multi‑inheritance → Add a link table to allow equipment classes to inherit from multiple parent classes
description:
Objective: Support Multi‑Inheritance of Equipment Classes

To support multi‑inheritance, where an equipment class can inherit from multiple parent classes, the data model introduces a dedicated link table that represents inheritance relationships between equipment classes. This design allows flexible composition of equipment classifications without enforcing a single‑parent hierarchy.

Core Tables

1. equipment_class

This table represents the definition of an equipment class.

  • Stores the unique identity and metadata of each equipment class.
  • Each record represents a logical class (e.g. SITE, AREA, LINE).
  • Equipment classes are independent of inheritance logic, making them reusable and extensible.


2. equipment_class_inheritance

This table models the inheritance relationship between equipment classes.

  • Acts as a self‑referencing link (junction) table.
  • Each row expresses a direct inheritance relationship:
    • one child equipment class inheriting from one parent equipment class.
  • A child class may reference multiple parent classes, enabling multi‑inheritance.
  • A parent class may be inherited by multiple child classes.

Foreign Keys

  • equipment_class_parent_id → equipment_class.id
  • equipment_class_child_id → equipment_class.id

Relationship Description

  • equipment_class ⟷ equipment_class_inheritance forms a many‑to‑many self‑relationship.
  • An equipment class can:
    • inherit from zero or more parent classes
    • act as a parent for zero or more child classes
  • The overall inheritance structure is a directed acyclic graph (DAG) rather than a simple tree.

Use of the Unique Constraint

A unique constraint is defined on the combination of:

  • equipment_class_parent_id
  • equipment_class_child_id

Purpose

  • Prevents duplicate inheritance relationships between the same parent and child classes.
  • Ensures that each inheritance link is defined once and only once.
  • Preserves data integrity and avoids redundant or conflicting inheritance definitions.

This constraint guarantees that the inheritance model remains deterministic and maintainable as the classification hierarchy evolves.

[analysis] [eDashboard] Fix the issue with Comment drawer
description:
After submitting a comment, the drawer stayed open and kept showing loading even after the backend write had already succeeded.

Root cause:
In shift-tracking-table.vue, the success flow had two issues:

It waited an extra 10 seconds after a successful response before refreshing.
It tried to close the drawer while the submission-pending flag was still active, and the drawer close logic blocked closing during pending state.
Impact:
The user could think the first submit was not accepted and attempt another action, while the UI remained stuck in a misleading loading state.

Fix:
Start loading immediately on submit, remove the artificial post-success wait, clear the local notification state as soon as the API succeeds, then close the drawer immediately and refresh the data in the background.

titre: [BA Design] [Common] Language - Primary language & second languages
description:
Purpose

As an administrator, I want to define a default main language and a set of proposed second languages to users per plant.

As more languages will be deployed to MESX.0, the language list might be too long for users to choose from, so plant administrators define the list of secondary languages spoken in their plant and display it for their users. 
In case someone speaks a different language than the ones defined by the plant administrator, they can still select it from custom attributes.

Impacted screens

  • Site configuration: MESX.0 - Site Maintenance
  • Language menu (header): 

Changes

Location: In Site configuration → Main
  1. Renaming existing field: Language → Main language
  2. Adding a new field under main language allowing multiple selection:
  • Field name: Second languages
  • Type: dropdown with checks, allowing multiple selection
  • Content (including new languages in User Story 150142 [Common] Language - FAS new languages required):
    • Select all
    • English
    • Français
    • Čeština
    • Español (España)
    • Español (México)
    • Português (Portugal)
    • Português (Brasil)
    • Polski
    • Slovenčina
    • 简体中文
    • 繁體中文
    • العربية
  • Rule: If a language is already selected as main language, it will be grayed out, and impossible to select in the second languages field.

Data design

  • Adding a column in HRY domain that contains the second languages.
-> When the user defines second languages in Site config:
filter on plant_id column > update new second_languages column

Language dropdown content order

The language menu (header) content order varies depending on the selected main and second languages.

Order rule:

User clicks on language dropdown:
> Language dropdown retrieves and displays following list, in order:
[Locale language from custom attributes,
Main plant language if different from Locale,
Second languages if exist
else full language list excluding any repetitions]
Note:  No particular order for the second languages. 

Display language rules

Upon launch (no user selection yet):

If the Locale exists in Custom attributes, then the system uses Locale language
> Else system uses Main language in Site configuration ([language_code])

After user selection

If user selects a language from the dropdown, then system uses the selected language
Summary:
If no user selection then Locale (custom attributes)
If locale not defined then Main language (Site config)
Else User selection

User flows

  • Administrator to configure plant languages: Clicks on Site configuration > Main
  • User to define a language: Opens language dropdown > Selects a language

Note : the language selected by the user must remain the same across all menus and pages until the end of the session
Note: in custom attributes, we rename Locale to Language for more clarity

[BA Design] [eDashBoard] Notification center - Downtime ticket
description:
Objective

The objective of this user story is to display the history of Downtime Ticket actions in the Event Center.

Data Retrieval Rules

  • The system retrieves downtime tickets based on their start time.
  • At  even level:
    • When the user clicks on the event icon, the system retrieves all downtime tickets where the start time falls within the selected shift interval.
  • At hour level:
    • When the user selects a specific hour and filters on Downtime, the system retrieves all tickets where the start time is within the selected hour range (e.g., 05:00:00 to 05:59:59).
Display Logic (Card View)

    • Each downtime ticket is displayed as a card containing:

      • Start time of the ticket
      • Duration:
        • If available → display the calculated duration
        • If not available → display “In Progress”
      • Cause hierarchy:
        • Cause Level 1
        • Cause Level 2 (if available)
        • Cause Level 3 (if available)
Navigation & User Interaction
  • The user can click on a downtime ticket card to navigate to the Downtime screen.
  • The selected ticket is passed as context and opened in edit mode.
  • The user can update the ticket and save changes.
  • After saving, the system should ensure data consistency with the Event Center


UI/UX Rules

  • Cause Level 1 must be displayed using the downtime cause color (as defined in the business configuration).

description:
📌[eDashBoard] Notification center - SD comment

✅ Scope:

eDashboard/ Live status

✅ Objective:

Being able to view all the SDs that have been occurred during the current shift in MESX.0 through the event center, so that we can:
  • Add a new comment
  • Report an existing comment 
  • Edit an existing comment 
  • Delete an existing comment

✅ Process Flow:

Considering that the icon to access to the event center is added on the screen (eDashboard or the live status 1:1):
1- eDasboard flow: 
  • Open the eDashboard
  • Select the relevant resource
  • Click the "accessibility icon" to open the event center
  • The Slowdown is shown as information if existing. 
2- Live status flow: 
Scenario 1: multiple resources are assigned to the Gap
  • Open the Live status 
  • Select the relevant Gap
  • Select the relevant resource
  • System is directed to the eDashboard screen for the dedicated resource 
  • Click the "accessibility point" to open the event center
  • The Slowdown is shown as information if existing. 
Scenario 2: one resource assigned to the Gap
  • Open the Live status 
  • Select the relevant Gap
  • Select the relevant resource
  • System is opening the Live status 1:1
  • Click the "accessibility point" to open the event center
  • The Slowdown is shown as information if existing

✅ Relevant information to display 

For a specific hour, display the SD according to the following rules:

  • Overspeed (negative SD): display when the SD value is less than –5 minutes
  • Slowdown (positive SD): display when the SD value is greater than 5 minutes

Comment behavior:

  • If the SD is not justified, request the user to add a comment
  • If the SD is justified, display the existing comment and allow the user to edit it

⚙ Technical checks

  • To retrieve the SD value: 
⚠ Attention point: The rule applied to the comment for the SD case can be applied in this case:

The rule is the following: 

For the selected resource and the corresponding hour, check if

  • SD!= 0 and SD < -5 min or SD > 5 min in the shift_tracking table in the RSRCE domain
      → then show it as an event on the event center and request the user to add a comment 

else if 

  • SD! = 0 and SD < -5 min or SD > 5 min in the shift_tracking_dtl table in the RSRCE domain for hour X, and there is a comment in action_on_prod table in the RSRCE domain for the same hour
          → then show it as an event on the event center and user is able to edit 

else

  • SD = 0 or SD is not < -5 min or > 5 min in the shift_tracking_dtl table in the RSRCE domain for hour X
       → then it will not be considered

  • To retrieve a comment for an existing SD: 
This action will retrieve the data existing into ACTION_ON_PROD table
How?

    • In RSCRE Domain in actions_on_prod table in MES

    • For the selected resource and the corresponding hour and column action ='ACTION_HOUR'

    • Retrieve the value inserted in description column 

  • To insert a comment: 
This action will insert a line into ACTION_ON_PROD table
How?

    • The New comment must be written back to MII using the MII transaction: SC_MES_API/INTERFACE/EPARTBOARD/V1/INSERT_ACTION

    • Trigger the ingestion as Insertion action from [CPT_FAURECIA]. [dbo]. [ACTIONS_ON_PROD] to MES in actions_on_prod in RSRCE domain

  • To edit a comment: 
This action will update the value inserted in Description column in ACTION_ON_PROD table
How?

    • The New added comment must be written back to MII using the MII transaction: SC_MES_API/INTERFACE/EPARTBOARD/V1/INSERT_ACTION

    • Trigger the ingestion as an update action from [CPT_FAURECIA]. [dbo]. [ACTIONS_ON_PROD] to MES in actions_on_prod in RSRCE domain

    • Update the comment on the screen

  • To delete a comment: 
This action will delete the value inserted in Description column in ACTION_ON_PROD table
How?

    • The comment value 'empty' must be written back to MII using the MII transaction: SC_MES_API/INTERFACE/EPARTBOARD/V1/INSERT_ACTION 

    • Trigger the ingestion as an update action from [CPT_FAURECIA]. [dbo]. [ACTIONS_ON_PROD] to MES in actions_on_prod in RSRCE domain with

    • Update the comment to empty on the screen

Attention point!
-The update done to the comment for the SD should be reflected on the column Comment on the shift tracking.

How? 
1- If the comment is inserted from the event center, then do not request a comment on the shift tracking (do not show a notification icon for the SD)

2- If the comment is deleted, then re show again the notification on the column Comment on the shift tracking.

✅ UI UX proposition: 

The SD value could be colored in Red as we have now on the drawer of the comment.

titre: [BA Design] [eDashBoard] Notification center - Configuration
description:
Objective

The objective of this user story is to display the history of configuration actions in the Event Center.

Data Source & Filtering

  • Data is retrieved from the actions_on_prod table (RSRCE domain).
  • The following fields are used:
    • date_hour_from (time only)
    • date_hour_to
    • action (filtered to: LOW, NORMAL, HIGH)
  • The date_hour_from value is stored in UTC and must be converted to the plant time zone before processing and display.
  • When a user selects a specific hour (e.g., 05:00 AM), the system retrieves all records:
    • With the same resource_id
    • Where date_hour_from is within the selected time range (e.g., 05:00:00 to 05:59:59)

Display Logic (Card View)

  • Each event is displayed as a card (as per the provided mockup).
  • The timestamp (hh:mm:ss) corresponds to date_hour_from (converted to plant time zone).
  • Color coding is not yet defined and must be validated with the UX/UI team.
Action Mapping
  • The action field is mapped as follows:
    • NORMAL → N
    • LOW → N-
    • HIGH → N+

“From N” Calculation Rule

To determine the “from N” value:

  1. Retrieve the most recent previous record where:
    • date_hour_to is less than the current record’s date_hour_from.
  2. Apply the following rule:
    • If the time difference between the current date_hour_from and the previous date_hour_to is greater than 1 minute → use the action from the previous record.
    • Otherwise → display N.

titre: [BA Design] [Page Builder] Widget Performance - Actual Time vs Theoretical Cycle Time
description:
Objective

Display the Cycle Time and Theoretical Cycle Time in the E-dashboard / Live Status through a configurable widget.

 Functional Description

1. Widget Creation & Configuration

  • A new widget is available in the Page Builder named "Cycle Time"
  • User can:
    • Add/remove the widget

2. Widget Content

Part 1: Cycle Time Display

Calculation Logic

  • Retrieve the last 31 tags of the current reference in production that has status PRODUCED
  • Calculate differences between consecutive DATE_PROCESS
  • Sort cycle times descending
  • Remove:
    • 25 % Top values (outliers - high)
    • 25% Bottom values (outliers - low)
  • Calculate the average of remaining 50% values

Display Format

  • If Cycle Time < 10 sec → show seconds + milliseconds
    → Example: 5.6
  • If Cycle Time ≥ 10 sec → show seconds only
    → Example: 11

Performance Indicator

  • Calculate ratio:
    Cycle Time / Theoretical Cycle Time
  • Display:
    • 🟢 Green → if Cycle Time ≤ Theoretical
    • 🔴 Red → if Cycle Time > Theoretical

Part 2: Cycle Time Diagram

  • Show last 10 cycle times
  • Visualization:
    • Horizontal line/bar → Theoretical Cycle Time
    • Vertical bars → Actual Cycle Times

the Goal: Quick visual comparison of performance vs target


3.Theoretical Cycle Time – Data Strategy

we propose 3 options here’s a clearer comparison + recommendation:

Option 1: MII + Stored Value (Recommended)

  • Call MII periodically (e.g. daily)
  • Store result in MES DB

Pros:

  • No real-time dependency on MII
  • Stable performance
  • Controlled refresh

Cons:

  • Slight delay if SAP changes during the day

Option 2: Real-time MII Call

  • Call MII at each dashboard refresh

Pros:

  • Always up to date

Cons:

  • High load on MII
  • Risk of latency / failure impacting UI

=> Not recommended 

Option 3: Full MES Calculation

  • Rebuild logic inside MES

Pros:

  • Full control

Cons:

  • High workload
  • Duplicates SAP logic
  • Hard to maintain

=> Overkill for this need

4.Cycle Time Data Retrieval – Technical Options

Option 1: Ingest Tags from MII → MES (Batch / Streaming)

    • Ingest tags from MII (DATE_PROCESS, PLANT, PLC_ID, STATUS, TOOL, PARTS) into MES database
  • Cycle time is fully calculated inside MES

Option 2: Call MII API at Each Refresh

Principle

  • At each dashboard refresh:
    • MES calls MII API
    • MII returns last 31 tags (or directly cycle time)

Test Scenarios – Cycle Time Widget

1. Widget Configuration

Scenario 1.1 – Add widget to page

Given the user is in Page Builder
When they add the "Cycle Time " widget
Then the widget should be added and saved successfully to the page

Scenario 1.2 – Configure widget

Given the widget is added
When the user selects Resource
Then the widget should display data accordingly

2. Cycle Time Calculation

Scenario 2.1 – Correct calculation with valid data

Given 34 valid tags with DATE_PROCESS and status = PRODUCED for the same reference in production
When the system calculates cycle time
Then:

  • Differences between consecutive tags are computed
  • Values are sorted descending
  • Top 25% and bottom 25% are removed
  • Average of remaining 50% values is calculated correctly

Scenario 2.2 – Less than 31 tags available

Given less than 31 tags exist
When calculation is triggered
Then:

  • System should handle it as well (no crash)

Identical timestamps (0 cycle time)

Given consecutive tags have same DATE_PROCESS
Then cycle time = 0 should be handled correctly

3.Diagram (Last 10 Cycle Times)

Scenario 3.1 – Correct data displayed

Given valid cycle times
Then:

  • Last 10 cycle times are displayed
  • Each value corresponds to correct calculation

Scenario 3.2 – Less than 10 values

Given only 6 cycle times available
Then:

  • Chart displays 6 bars only
  • No UI break

4.Data Refresh

Scenario 4.1 – Refresh dashboard

When dashboard is refreshed
Then:

  • Cycle time is recalculated
  • Latest data is displayed

5.Error Handling

Scenario 5.1 – Missing data

Given no tags available
Then:

  • Display message: “No data available”

titre: OpEquipmentSpecification Generation

  • Tool validity changes must be respected over time
  • Co‑production depends on physical reality, not only BOM logic

Group OperationsDefinitions by Shared Physical Asset
description:
1. Purpose

Group OperationsDefinitions into a single WorkMaster when they share an identical active physical asset configuration.

2. Scope & Preconditions

  • OperationsDefinitions exist
  • OperationsSegments exist
  • OpPhysicalAssetSpecifications exist
  • OpMaterialSpecifications exist
  • Material Feature Classes are defined

3. Trigger

  • WorkMaster auto‑generation
  • WorkMaster regeneration after SAP update

4. Inputs

  • OperationsDefinitions
  • OperationsSegments
  • Active OpPhysicalAssetSpecifications
  • Active OpMaterialSpecifications
  • Material Feature Classes with flag IsRelevantForCoProduction = true

5. Output Objects & Properties

WorkMaster

  • OperationsDefinitionID (0..*)
  • OperationsSegmentID (0..*)

6. Detailed Logic / Algorithm

For each candidate OperationsDefinition:

  1. Identify its OperationsSegments
  2. For each OperationsSegment:
    • Retrieve active OpPhysicalAssetSpecification
  3. Build a grouping key composed of:              
    PhysicalAssetID
+ value of each Material Feature Class
  where IsRelevantForCoProduction = true
  4. Compare grouping keys across OperationsDefinitions
  5. Group OperationsDefinitions only if grouping keys are strictly identical
  6. Any mismatch produces a separate WorkMaster

7. Effective Date Rules

  • Only active OpPhysicalAssetSpecifications may trigger grouping
  • OpPhysicalAssetSpec is active if: 
    effective_start ≤ now < effective_end

8. Update / Versioning Rules

  • Grouping is re‑evaluated on every WorkMaster regeneration
  • Change in tool validity or feature class value produces a new grouping

9. Acceptance Criteria

  • Same tool + same feature values ⇒ grouped
  • Same tool + different feature values ⇒ not grouped
  • Inactive tool ⇒ no Case‑1 grouping

titre: SAP Update for AutoGenerated WorkMaster
description:
1. Purpose

Automatically regenerate WorkMaster when SAP data changes and the current WorkMaster has Origin = AutoGenerated, without requiring user intervention.

2. Scope & Preconditions

  • A WorkMaster exists with:
    • Origin = AutoGenerated
    • DefinitionType = Defined
  • The WorkMaster has been generated previously from SAP data

3. Trigger

  • SAP sends updated Production Version, Routing, and/or BOM
  • As a result, OperationsDefinition and OperationsSegments are regenerated

4. Inputs

  • New OperationsDefinitions
  • New OperationsSegments
  • New OperationsMaterialBills
  • Regenerated OpMaterialSpecifications
  • Regenerated OpEquipmentSpecifications
  • Regenerated OpPhysicalAssetSpecifications
  • New effectives dates( published/start/end)

5. Output Objects & Properties

WorkMaster vX+1 ( what's changing)

  • New ID or same functional ID with incremented Version
  • Origin = AutoGenerated
  • DefinitionType = Defined
  • PublishedDate = when WorkMaster is created
  • EffectiveStartDate
  • EffectiveEndDate = NULL
  • Updated references to:
    • OperationsDefinitionID(s)
    • OperationsSegmentID(s)
    • OpResourceSpecifications
    • WorkMasterChild

6. Detailed Logic / Algorithm

  1. Receive SAP update notification
  2. Regenerate OperationsDefinition / OperationsSegment / BOM (already handled upstream)
  3. Regenerate all OpResourceSpecifications (new UIDs)
  4. Re‑evaluate WorkMaster grouping logic (Case 1 → Case 2 → Case 3)
  5. Create a new WorkMaster version vX+1
  6. Generate WorkMasterChild objects for vX+1
  7. Recompute JobOrderEnabled for each WorkMasterChild
  8. Publish WorkMaster vX+1 immediately

7. Effective Date Rules

  • New WorkMaster vX+1:
    • EffectiveStartDate = MAX(effective_start of grouped OperationsDefinitions)
    • EffectiveEndDate = NULL
  • Previous WorkMaster version remains active until execution switches

8. Update / Versioning Rules

  • No user action is required
  • Previous WorkMaster version is not closed at publish time
  • Version closing happens only when MES switches execution to vX+1

9. Acceptance Criteria

  • SAP update automatically generate a new WorkMaster version
  • No override of user data (since none exists)
  • Production can continue on previous version until switch
  • Exactly one WorkMaster is active at execution time

titre: Compute JobOrderEnabled

titre: [Design] Material Data Model Adjustment
description:
Adjust and extend the Material Data Model to improve consistency with MES standards, increase modeling flexibility, and align material and equipment property semantics.
This task focuses on naming alignment, class inheritance redesign, and enrichment of class property definition

1. Terminology alignment

  • Rename Site to Plant across the material data model.
  • Ensure consistency with existing MES database objects and naming conventions.

2. Material Class – Multiple Inheritance

  • Adapt material classes to support inheritance from multiple parent classes instead of a single parent.
  • Replace the current single‑parent structure with a model that allows:
    • One material class to inherit from several parent classes
    • Clear resolution of inherited properties

3.1 Property Cardinality

Introduce a cardinality attribute to specify whether a property is:

  • single → exactly one value is expected
  • array → a list of values is expected

This cardinality will drive:

  • Validation rules
  • Property storage format
  • API payload structure

3.2 Class Property Type

Add a missing attribute class_property_type to define how the property behaves between class and instance levels.

Supported values:

TypeBehavior
ClassTypeValue is fixed at the class level; all instances inherit the same value
InstanceTypeValue is not defined at class level; every instance must provide a value
DefaultTypeClass provides a default value that instances may override

This enables explicit modeling of ISA‑95 semantics and avoids ambiguity at runtime.

3.3 Default and Allowed Values alignment

Align default_value and allowed_values with the existing equipment property properties_json structure.

Handle SAP Update for UserDefined WorkMaster
description:
1. Purpose

Preserve MDO user customizations while integrating SAP updates by creating a reviewable draft WorkMaster.

2. Scope & Preconditions

  • A WorkMaster exists with:
    • Origin = UserDefined
    • DefinitionType = Defined
  • The WorkMaster has been previously published

3. Trigger

  • SAP sends updated Production Version, Routing, and/or BOM

4. Inputs

  • New OperationsDefinitions
  • New OperationsSegments
  • New OperationsMaterialBills
  • Regenerated OpResourceSpecifications
  • Existing customized WorkMaster (version vX)
  • New effectives dates(published/start/end)

5. Output Objects & Properties

WorkMaster vX+1 (Draft)

  • Origin = UserDefined
  • DefinitionType = Undefined
  • PublishedDate = NULL( untill user publication)
  • Updated references to regenerated SAP objects
  • Preserved user modifications where applicable

6. Detailed Logic / Algorithm

  1. Receive SAP update
  2. Regenerate OperationsDefinition / OperationsSegments / BOM
  3. Regenerate all OpResourceSpecifications
  4. Clone the latest published UserDefined WorkMaster → vX+1 (Draft)
  5. Overlay updated SAP references onto the new draft:
    • OperationsDefinitionID
    • OperationsSegmentID
    • OpResourceSpecifications
  6. Rebuild WorkMasterChild structure
  7. Recompute JobOrderEnabled (default logic)
  8. Notify MDO user that a new WorkMaster version is ready for review

7. Effective Date Rules

  • Draft WorkMaster vX+1:
    • Has EffectiveStartDate computed
    • Is not executable until published
  • Current published version remains active

8. Update / Versioning Rules

  • User must explicitly publish vX+1
  • User may further customize before publication
  • No timeout: previous version remains active indefinitely until user acts

9. Acceptance Criteria

  • User modifications are not lost
  • SAP changes are visible in draft version (definition tyep=undefined)
  • No production disruption until user publishes

titre: Generate JobOrders Only from JobOrderEnabled Steps
description:
1. Purpose

As a Key user

I want to ensure that JobOrders are created only from eligible WorkMasterChild steps.

2. Scope & Preconditions

  • WorkMaster is published
  • WorkMasterChild exists
  • JobOrderEnabled is computed
  • OpResourceSpecifications are active

3. Trigger

  • JobOrder creation request

4. Inputs

  • WorkMaster
  • WorkMasterChild
  • JobOrderEnabled flag

5. Output Objects & Properties

JobOrder

  • Linked to:
    • WorkMaster
    • WorkMasterChild

6. Detailed Logic / Algorithm 

IF
   WorkMaster is active
AND
   WorkMasterChild is active
AND
   JobOrderEnabled = true
THEN
   allow JobOrder creation
ELSE
   block JobOrder creation

7. Effective Date Rules

  • JobOrders cannot be created outside the effective window of:
    • WorkMaster
    • WorkMasterChild
    • referenced OpResourceSpecifications

8. Update / Versioning Rules

  • When execution switches to a new WorkMaster version:
    • Only JobOrderEnabled steps of the active version are considered

9. Acceptance Criteria

  • No JobOrder is created from JobOrderEnabled = false 
  • No JobOrder is created directly from OperationsSegment
  • Execution always uses the currently active WorkMaster version

titre: Group Multiple SAP Production Versions (Flexible Production Line)
description:
This feature enables flexible production line support by grouping multiple SAP Production Versions for the same material into one single WorkMaster, when they share the same operational resource intent.

Differences between Production Versions (different work centers, different equipment alternatives) are not reasons to create multiple WorkMasters.

They are instead captured explicitly in OpEquipmentSpecification.

titre: Maintain JobOrderEnabled During WorkMaster Lifecycle
description:
1. Purpose

As a Key user

I want to ensure that JobOrderEnabled remains correct throughout the WorkMaster lifecycle.

2. Scope & Preconditions

  • Multiple WorkMaster versions may exist
  • WorkMaster origin may be AutoGenerated or UserDefined

3. Trigger

  • SAP update
  • User customization and publication of a new version

4. Inputs

  • Existing WorkMaster versions
  • Regenerated OpResourceSpecifications

5. Output Objects & Properties

  • New WorkMaster version with recalculated or preserved JobOrderEnabled

6. Detailed Logic / Algorithm

  • AutoGenerated WorkMaster

    • Rebuild WorkMasterChild
    • Recompute JobOrderEnabled

  • UserDefined WorkMaster

    • Default value recomputed
    • User override preserved in draft
    • Published value governs execution

7. Effective Date Rules

  • Only JobOrderEnabled of the active WorkMaster version applies

8. Update / Versioning Rules

  • No JobOrderEnabled change impacts historical versions
  • Effective dates control execution eligibility

9. Acceptance Criteria

  • SAP updates never accidentally enable/disable execution
  • User intent is preserved
  • Execution continuity is respected

titre: Group Multiple Production Versions into One WorkMaster
description:
1. Purpose

As a Key user

I want that MES Create one WorkMaster for multiple SAP Production Versions when they describe the same manufacturing capability with alternative execution paths.

2. Scope & Preconditions

  • A single Material has multiple SAP Production Versions
  • Each Production Version has:
    • Its own OperationsDefinition
    • Its own OperationsSegments
  • OpResourceSpecifications have been generated
  • Material, equipment and physical asset models exist

3. Trigger

  • Initial WorkMaster auto‑generation
  • WorkMaster regeneration after SAP update

4. Inputs

  • OperationsDefinitions (one per Production Version)
  • OperationsSegments
  • OpMaterialSpecifications
  • OpEquipmentSpecifications
  • OpPhysicalAssetSpecifications

5. Output Objects & Properties

WorkMaster

  • References multiple OperationsDefinitions
  • References multiple OperationsSegments
  • Origin = AutoGenerated
  • Represents one manufacturing capability

6. Detailed Logic / Algorithm

For all OperationsDefinitions producing the same Material:

  1. Compare their OpMaterialSpecifications
    • Must be identical (material definition, class, use)
  2. Compare OpPhysicalAssetSpecifications
    • Must be identical or equivalent
  3. Compare OpEquipmentSpecifications
    • Must represent the same capability, even if:
      • EquipmentID differs
      • Work center differs
  4. If all OpResourceSpecifications are equivalent:
    • Group OperationsDefinitions into one WorkMaster
  5. Store all OperationsDefinitionIDs in the WorkMaster

⚠️ Different Production Versions do NOT require different WorkMasters

7. Effective Date Rules

  • Execution validity controlled by effective‑date semantics

8. Update / Versioning Rules

  • New Production Version added → re‑evaluate grouping
  • Removed Production Version → re‑evaluate grouping
  • Change in resource equivalence → new WorkMaster version

9. Acceptance Criteria

  • One WorkMaster exists for N Production Versions
  • No WorkMaster duplication per Production Version
  • Traceability to each Production Version is preserved

titre: Highlight equipement Diversity in OpEquipmentSpecification
description: This feature ensures that equipment(WC) variability across Production Versions is explicitly modeled inside OpEquipmentSpecification, not by duplicating WorkMasters.

titre: Represent Multiple Equipement (Work Centers )in One OpEquipmentSpecification
description:
1. Purpose

Allow an operation to be executed on different work centers or equipment, using a single OpEquipmentSpecification with various equipement mapped.

2. Scope & Preconditions

  • OperationsSegment exists
  • SAP routing defines multiple equipment / work centers
  • EquipmentClass and Equipment definitions exist

3. Trigger

  • OpEquipmentSpecification generation
  • SAP routing update

4. Inputs

  • OperationsSegment
  • SAP routing alternatives
  • EquipmentClass
  • Equipment definitions
  • HierarchyScope (work center)

5. Output Objects & Properties

OpEquipmentSpecification

  • EquipmentClassID (mandatory – capability)
  • EquipmentID (0..*)
  • HierarchyScope (0..*) → multiple work centers allowed
  • EquipmentSpecificationProperty (optional)

6. Detailed Logic / Algorithm

  1. Identify all valid SAP routing alternatives for the OperationsSegment
  2. Create one OpEquipmentSpecification
  3. Assign:
    • EquipmentClass → shared capability
    • EquipmentID list → execution alternatives
    • HierarchyScope → allowed work centers
  4. Optionally attach properties:
    • Preferred work center
    • Constraints
    • Selection criteria

7. Effective Date Rules

  • OpEquipmentSpecification is active only 
  • Individual equipment validity is respected

8. Update / Versioning Rules

  • Any routing alternative change → regenerate OpEquipmentSpecification
  • Old versions remain historical

9. Acceptance Criteria

  • One OpEquipmentSpecification may reference multiple work centers
  • Execution logic can select an eligible work center
  • WorkMaster remains unchanged

titre: JobOrderEnabled with Flexible Production Lines
description: Ensures JobOrderEnabled logic remains valid when multiple equipment/ work centers exist inside an OpEquipmentSpecification.

titre: Compute JobOrderEnabled for Flexible Lines
description:
1. Purpose

Allow JobOrders to be created when at least one equipment alternative matches the execution context.

2. Scope & Preconditions

  • WorkMasterChild exists
  • OpEquipmentSpecification has multiple alternatives

3. Trigger

  • WorkMasterChild creation
  • WorkMaster regeneration

4. Inputs

  • OperationsDefinition work center
  • OpEquipmentSpecification (with multiple EquipmentID / HierarchyScope)

5. Output Objects & Properties

WorkMasterChild

  • JobOrderEnabled (boolean)

6. Detailed Logic / Algorithm 

IF
   EXISTS equipment alternative in OpEquipmentSpecification
   WHERE equipment OR hierarchyScope matches
   OperationsDefinition execution work center
THEN
   JobOrderEnabled = true
ELSE
   JobOrderEnabled = false

7. Effective Date Rules

  • Same as base JobOrderEnabled rules
  • Only active specs are evaluated

8. Update / Versioning Rules

  • Recomputed on SAP update
  • Preserved in UserDefined WorkMaster

9. Acceptance Criteria

  • Flexible routing does not block execution
  • JobOrders can be created on any valid line

description:

Allow a Key User to customize an AutoGenerated WorkMaster without modifying the original version.

titre: User Publish Customized Version Replacing AutoGenerated or Userdefined WorkMaster
description:

Allow a user to publish a customized WorkMaster version derived from an AutoGenerated or User defined one.

2. Scope & Preconditions

3. Trigger

4. Detailed Logic

On publication:

  1. Set:
    • DefinitionType → Defined
    • PublishedDate → current timestamp
  2. EffectiveStartDate / EffectiveEndDate remain user‑defined
  3. Execution continuity rules apply:
    • Old version remains Active until effective dates enforce switch

5. Acceptance Criteria

  •  Current AutoGenerated/user defined version remains intact until execution switch through effectives dates
  •  No forced execution change ( switch is controlled by effective start date of the new version)

titre: User Update an Existing Active UserDefined WorkMaster
description:

titre: Compute WorkMaster Status
description:
Purpose

Ensure Status is always accurate.

  • WorkMaster creation/update
  • EffectiveStartDate change
  • EffectiveEndDate change
  • Time crossing effective boundary

Rules

Status is a WorkMaster property with only two values:

StatusMeaning
ActiveWithin effective date window
InactiveOutside effective date window
IF EffectiveStartDate ≤ now
AND (EffectiveEndDate IS NULL OR now < EffectiveEndDate)
THEN Status = Active
ELSE Status = Inactive
``

Acceptance Criteria

  •  Status is always Active or Inactive
  • Status cannot be manually edited
  • Status depends only on effective dates.

Purpose

description:
Objective

Integrate the IDOC MDM_EQUIPMENT_SAVEREPLICA into the system to manage Physical Assets (TOOL) in MES.

Incoming Data Mapping (IDOC → MES)
IDOC FieldTarget Field (MES)Description
EQUIPMENT_INT Code Equipment identifier (remove leading zeros)
DESCRIPT Description Equipment description
PLANPLANT Plant Plant identifier
READ_FLOC Physical Asset Location Functional location

Target Table: Physical Asset Definition
FieldSource / Rule
ID Auto-generated
Code From EQUIPMENT_INT (remove leading zeros)
Description From DESCRIPT
Plant From PLANPLANT
Physical Asset Location From READ_FLOC
ERP Source derived (e.g., FC1)
Effective Start Date Derived (see rules below)
Effective End Date Derived (see rules below)

Effective Date Management Logic

Based on IDOC field: FREE_NUM1

Case 1: Active Equipment

  • FRRE_NUM1 = 0
    Equipment is active
    • Effective Start Date = IDOC integration datetime
    • Effective End Date = 9999-12-31

Case 2: Equipment Deactivation

  • FRRE_NUM1 = 000009999
     Equipment is ended
    • Effective End Date = IDOC integration datetime
    • (Start date remains unchanged if already exists)

Case 3: No Valid Dates

  • FRRE_NUM1 = 000005555
     No validity period
    • Effective Start Date = NULL
    • Effective End Date = NULL

Upsert Logic (Insert / Update)

When an IDOC is received:

Identify Existing Record

  • Match on:
    • Code
    • Plant

If NOT exists => Perform INSERT

If exists => Perform UPDATE:

  • Description
  • Physical Asset Location
  • Effective Dates
  • ERP Source (if needed)

NB: Remove leading zeros from EQUIPMENT_INT before storing and comparing.

Test Scenarios 

  • Insert new equipment with FRRE_NUM1 = 0
  • Update existing equipment with new description
  • Deactivate equipment (000009999)
  • Handle null dates (000005555)
  • Validate leading zero removal (00001234 → 1234)
